2.7.s:
2.31
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
durge sarvaguṇopete vāstulakṣaṇasaṃyute ..
vasanvivardhayetkośaṃ dharmeṇa pṛthivīpatiḥ .. 1 ..
2.7.d:
2.31
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
दुर्गे सर्वगुणोपेते वास्तुलक्षणसंयुते ॥
वसन्विवर्धयेत्कोशं धर्मेण पृथिवीपतिः ॥ 1 ॥
2.7.m:
2.31
Puṣkara said:
Residing in a fortress endowed with all good qualities and possessing the architectural characteristics,
the lord of the earth should augment his treasury in accordance with dharma.

2.7.s:
prajānāṃ pālanaṃ kāryaṃ tatra sthāne mahīkṣitā ..
svadeśe devatāyāśca kṛtā rājñaḥ purātanaiḥ .. 2 ..
2.7.d:
प्रजानां पालनं कार्यं तत्र स्थाने महीक्षिता ॥
स्वदेशे देवतायाश्च कृता राज्ञः पुरातनैः ॥ 2 ॥
2.7.m:
The protection of the subjects must be maintained in that place by the ruler of the earth;
and the deities instituted in his realm by former kings,

2.7.s:
dāyaṃ vittaṃ janaṃ tāsāṃ prayatnena ca pālayet ..
devadravyāpahāreṇa rājā narakamṛcchati .. 3 ..
2.7.d:
दायं वित्तं जनं तासां प्रयत्नेन च पालयेत् ॥
देवद्रव्यापहारेण राजा नरकमृच्छति ॥ 3 ॥
2.7.m:
their endowment, property, and people he should diligently preserve.
By misappropriating the property of the gods, a king goes to hell.

2.7.s:
asminnapi tathā loke prāpnoti ca parābhavam ..
pālayanti mahīṃ devāḥ pūjitāḥ pṛthivīkṣitā .. 4 ..
2.7.d:
अस्मिन्नपि तथा लोके प्राप्नोति च पराभवम् ॥
पालयन्ति महीं देवाः पूजिताः पृथिवीक्षिता ॥ 4 ॥
2.7.m:
In this world too, he meets with defeat.
The gods, worshipped by the ruler of the earth, protect the earth.

2.7.s:
daivāyattamidaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtalaṃ dvijapuṅgava ..
dhūpadīpanamaskārapuṣpamālyānulepanaiḥ .. 5 ..
2.7.d:
दैवायत्तमिदं सर्वं भूतलं द्विजपुङ्गव ॥
धूपदीपनमस्कारपुष्पमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥ 5 ॥
2.7.m:
This entire surface of the earth depends on fate, O bull among the twice-born.
With incense, lamps, salutations, flowers, garlands, ointments,

2.7.s:
ratnānusampradānaiśca pūjanīyāḥ surottamāḥ ..
pūjitāḥ pūjayantyete cāyuṣā yaśasā śriyā .. 6 ..
2.7.d:
रत्नानुसम्प्रदानैश्च पूजनीयाः सुरोत्तमाः ॥
पूजिताः पूजयन्त्येते चायुषा यशसा श्रिया ॥ 6 ॥
2.7.m:
and gifts of jewels, the foremost gods are to be worshipped.
When worshipped, they honor [him] with long life, renown, and fortune.

2.7.s:
prāpyate devatābhaktyā cānuṣṭhāne mahatpadam ..
pūjitāḥ saṃprayacchanti kāmānnṛṇāmabhīpsitān .. 7 ..
2.7.d:
प्राप्यते देवताभक्त्या चानुष्ठाने महत्पदम् ॥
पूजिताः संप्रयच्छन्ति कामान्नृणामभीप्सितान् ॥ 7 ॥
2.7.m:
Through devotion to the deities in ritual practice, a high station is attained;
when worshipped, they grant mortals their wished-for desires.

2.7.s:
ekamapyāśrito devaṃ rājā bhārgavanandana ..
sarvāsāṃ pūjanaṃ kuryāddevatānāmasaṃśayam ..8 ..
2.7.d:
एकमप्याश्रितो देवं राजा भार्गवनन्दन ॥
सर्वासां पूजनं कुर्याद्देवतानामसंशयम् ॥8 ॥
2.7.m:
Even if devoted to one deity, O son of Bhṛgu,
the king should undoubtedly worship all deities.

2.7.s:
devatānāṃ na cocchindyātpūrvadāyaṃ kathañcana ..
prāksthitaṃ tanna cocchiṃdyānna ca cchiṃdyāttathā navam .. 9 ..
2.7.d:
देवतानां न चोच्छिन्द्यात्पूर्वदायं कथञ्चन ॥
प्राक्स्थितं तन्न चोच्छिंद्यान्न च च्छिंद्यात्तथा नवम् ॥ 9 ॥
2.7.m:
And he must never cut off an earlier endowment of the deities;
he should not revoke what was established previously, nor should he cut off a new one.

2.7.s:
tacchettā narakaṃ yāti saha pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ ..
api svalpaṃ na hartavyaṃ devadravyaṃ vijānatā .. 10 ..
2.7.d:
तच्छेत्ता नरकं याति सह पूर्वैः पितामहैः ॥
अपि स्वल्पं न हर्तव्यं देवद्रव्यं विजानता ॥ 10 ॥
2.7.m:
One who cuts it off goes to hell together with his former ancestors;
one who knows should not seize property of the gods, even if very little,

2.7.s:
svalpasyāpi phalaṃ ghoraṃ yasmājjanmāntare bhavet ..
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca .. 11 ..
2.7.d:
स्वल्पस्यापि फलं घोरं यस्माज्जन्मान्तरे भवेत् ॥
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिवर्षशतानि च ॥ 11 ॥
2.7.m:
since even for a little there will be a terrible fruition in another birth.
For sixty thousand years and six hundred years

2.7.s:
devadravyāpaharaṇānnarakaṃ pratipadyate ..
santīha devatāḥ saumyāḥ santyugrāścāpi bhārgava .. 12 ..
2.7.d:
देवद्रव्यापहरणान्नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
सन्तीह देवताः सौम्याः सन्त्युग्राश्चापि भार्गव ॥ 12 ॥
2.7.m:
one falls into hell because of stealing the property of the gods.
There are gentle deities here, and there are also fierce ones, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.7.s:
darśayanti ruṣaṃ saumya rājyabhraṃśādibhirnṛṇām ..
asmim̐lloke ruṣaṃ krūrāṃ naiva kurvanti devatāḥ .. 13 ..
2.7.d:
दर्शयन्ति रुषं सौम्य राज्यभ्रंशादिभिर्नृणाम् ॥
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके रुषं क्रूरां नैव कुर्वन्ति देवताः ॥ 13 ॥
2.7.m:
Gentle deities show anger toward men through loss of kingdom and the like;
the deities do not display cruel anger in this world.

2.7.s:
tāsāṃ vittāpaharaṇādrājā narakamṛcchati ..
pūrvaiḥ pitāmahaissārdhaṃ prāguktaṃ phalameva tu .. 14 ..
2.7.d:
तासां वित्तापहरणाद्राजा नरकमृच्छति ॥
पूर्वैः पितामहैस्सार्धं प्रागुक्तं फलमेव तु ॥ 14 ॥
2.7.m:
Because of stealing their wealth, a king goes to hell
together with his former ancestors, reaping the very fruit spoken of earlier.

2.7.s:
devadravyāpaharaṇaṃ naiva jātu bhavedvṛthā ..
sarvasvarahitānkṛtvā devadravyāpahāriṇaḥ .. 15 ..
2.7.d:
देवद्रव्यापहरणं नैव जातु भवेद्वृथा ॥
सर्वस्वरहितान्कृत्वा देवद्रव्यापहारिणः ॥ 15 ॥
2.7.m:
Stealing the property of the gods never goes without effect.
Having deprived those who steal the property of the gods of all their possessions,

2.7.s:
aṅkayitvā dvijaśreṣṭha svarāṣṭrādvipravāsayet ..
traividyā vaṇijo vaiśyā liṅgino devapālakāḥ .. 16 ..
2.7.d:
अङ्कयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठ स्वराष्ट्राद्विप्रवासयेत् ॥
त्रैविद्या वणिजो वैश्या लिङ्गिनो देवपालकाः ॥ 16 ॥
2.7.m:
and having branded them, O best of the twice-born, he should banish them from his kingdom.
Scholars of the three Vedas, traders, vaiśyas, ascetics, guardians of temples,

2.7.s:
tathā tatpratibaddhāśca na kuryuḥ kalahaṃ mithaḥ ..
teṣāṃ sahāyakaḥ svāmī nigrahānugrahī bhavet .. 17 ..
2.7.d:
तथा तत्प्रतिबद्धाश्च न कुर्युः कलहं मिथः ॥
तेषां सहायकः स्वामी निग्रहानुग्रही भवेत् ॥ 17 ॥
2.7.m:
and those connected with them should not quarrel among themselves;
the ruler should be their helper, meting out punishment and favor.

2.7.s:
rāgadveṣaviyuktastu vivāsyaścānyathā bhavet ..
daṇḍaṃ ca devatāgāmi devadravyasya sūcakam .. 18 ..
2.7.d:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तस्तु विवास्यश्चान्यथा भवेत् ॥
दण्डं च देवतागामि देवद्रव्यस्य सूचकम् ॥ 18 ॥
2.7.m: Free from passion and hatred, however, one should exile [them], or otherwise [punish them]; / and a fine for an informer regarding the property of a deity goes to that deity.

2.7.s:
sarvānvivāsayedrājā dhārmiko dharmakāraṇāt ..
rājñā sarvaprayatnena pālanīyāḥ surālayāḥ .. 19 ..
2.7.d:
सर्वान्विवासयेद्राजा धार्मिको धर्मकारणात् ॥
राज्ञा सर्वप्रयत्नेन पालनीयाः सुरालयाः ॥ 19 ॥
2.7.m: A righteous king should exile all [such wrongdoers] for the sake of dharma. / By the king, with every effort, the temples of the gods must be protected.

2.7.s:
kartavyāśca mahābhāga suralokamabhīpsatā ..
devatāstu pratiṣṭhāpya tallokaṃ dhruvamāpnuyāta .. 20 ..
2.7.d:
कर्तव्याश्च महाभाग सुरलोकमभीप्सता ॥
देवतास्तु प्रतिष्ठाप्य तल्लोकं ध्रुवमाप्नुयात ॥ 20 ॥
2.7.m: And they should be built, O fortunate one, by one desiring the world of the gods. / Having consecrated deities, he surely attains their world.

2.7.s:
kṛtvā devagṛhaṃ śubhraṃ svargamāpnotyanuttamam ..
tadā bhogapramāṇena lakṣmīstatrāpi bhārgava .. 21 ..
2.7.d:
कृत्वा देवगृहं शुभ्रं स्वर्गमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥
तदा भोगप्रमाणेन लक्ष्मीस्तत्रापि भार्गव ॥ 21 ॥
2.7.m: Having made a bright temple for a god, he attains unsurpassed heaven. / Then, in proportion to his enjoyment, royal fortune [comes] there also, O Bhārgava.

2.7.s:
mṛtprāsādāddaśaguṇaṃ sthūladārukṛte bhavet ..
phalaṃ daśaguṇaṃ tasmāttathā pakveṣṭakākṛte .. 22 ..
2.7.d:
मृत्प्रासादाद्दशगुणं स्थूलदारुकृते भवेत् ॥
फलं दशगुणं तस्मात्तथा पक्वेष्टकाकृते ॥ 22 ॥
2.7.m: Tenfold the fruit of an earthen temple is obtained from one made of thick wood; / tenfold the fruit from that, likewise, from one made of baked bricks;

2.7.s:
tasmāddaśaguṇaṃ śaile nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
yāvatsaṃkhyaṃ naraḥ kuryāddevaveśma sudhāsitam .. 23 ..
2.7.d:
तस्माद्दशगुणं शैले नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
यावत्संख्यं नरः कुर्याद्देववेश्म सुधासितम् ॥ 23 ॥
2.7.m: tenfold from that for a stone one; no doubt should be entertained on this point. / For as many years as a man whitewashes the temple of a god with lime,

2.7.s:
tāvajjanmāntarāṇīha yaśasā sa virājate ..
kṛtvā ca citravinyāsaṃ gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 24 ..
2.7.d:
तावज्जन्मान्तराणीह यशसा स विराजते ॥
कृत्वा च चित्रविन्यासं गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥ 24 ॥
2.7.m: for so many future births in this world he shines with renown. / And having painted pictures [there], he rejoices with the Gandharvas.

2.7.s:
kṛtvā saṃśodhanaṃ tatra virogaḥ samapadyate ..
prokṣayitvā manastāpānmānavaḥ pratimucyate .. 25 ..
2.7.d:
कृत्वा संशोधनं तत्र विरोगः समपद्यते ॥
प्रोक्षयित्वा मनस्तापान्मानवः प्रतिमुच्यते ॥ 25 ॥
2.7.m: Having performed a cleansing there, he becomes free of disease. / Having sprinkled it [with water], a human being is freed from mental anguish.

2.7.s:
kṛtvopalepanaṃ rāma nākamāpnotyanuttamam ..
gāndharvalokamāpnoti kṛtvā varṇakarañjitam .. 26 ..
2.7.d:
कृत्वोपलेपनं राम नाकमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥
गान्धर्वलोकमाप्नोति कृत्वा वर्णकरञ्जितम् ॥ 26 ॥
2.7.m: Having performed plastering, O Rāma, he attains unsurpassed heaven. / Having coloured it with paints, he reaches the world of the Gandharvas.

2.7.s:
gandhaiḥ samukṣitaṃ kṛtvā gandharvaissaha modate ..
upakārapradānena śriyamāpnotyanuttamām .. 27 ..
2.7.d:
गन्धैः समुक्षितं कृत्वा गन्धर्वैस्सह मोदते ॥
उपकारप्रदानेन श्रियमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.7.m: Having sprinkled it with perfumes, he rejoices with the Gandharvas. / By offering assistance, he attains unsurpassed splendor.

2.7.s:
gītavādyapradānena sukhamāpnotyanuttamam ..
prekṣaṇīyapradānena rūpavānabhijāyate .. 28 ..
2.7.d:
गीतवाद्यप्रदानेन सुखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥
प्रेक्षणीयप्रदानेन रूपवानभिजायते ॥ 28 ॥
2.7.m: By offering singing and instrumental music, he attains unsurpassed happiness. / By presenting a theatrical spectacle, he is reborn handsome,

2.7.s:
tathā aujjvalyamāpnoti yatrayatrābhijāyate ..
snāpayitvā ghṛtenārcāṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 29 ..
2.7.d:
तथा औज्ज्वल्यमाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥
स्नापयित्वा घृतेनार्चां सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 29 ॥
2.7.m: and he attains radiance wherever he is reborn. / Having bathed the idol with ghee, he is freed from all sins.

2.7.s:
snāpayitvā ca tailena virogaḥ samapadyata ..
ambunā snāpayitvā tu saubhāgyamadhigacchati .. 30 ..
2.7.d:
स्नापयित्वा च तैलेन विरोगः समपद्यत ॥
अम्बुना स्नापयित्वा तु सौभाग्यमधिगच्छति ॥ 30 ॥
2.7.m: And having bathed it with oil, he becomes free of disease. / But having bathed it with water, he attains good fortune.

2.7.s:
virūkṣayitvā tāṃ rāma pāpaṃ jahati mānavāḥ ..
anulepanadānena rūpamāpnotyanuttamam .. 31 ..
2.7.d:
विरूक्षयित्वा तां राम पापं जहति मानवाः ॥
अनुलेपनदानेन रूपमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥ 31 ॥
2.7.m: Having dried it, O Rāma, humans cast off sin. / By giving anointment, one attains unsurpassed beauty.

2.7.s:
tathā puṣpapradānena śriyamāpnotyanuttamām ..
dhūpadānena dharmajña ratimāpnoti śobhanām .. 32 ..
2.7.d:
तथा पुष्पप्रदानेन श्रियमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥
धूपदानेन धर्मज्ञ रतिमाप्नोति शोभनाम् ॥ 32 ॥
2.7.m: Likewise, by giving flowers, he attains unsurpassed prosperity. / By giving incense, O knower of dharma, he attains delightful pleasure.

2.7.s:
tathā dīpapradānena cakṣuṣmānabhijāyate ..
annadaḥ sarvamāpnoti yatkiṃcinmanasecchati ..33 ..
2.7.d:
तथा दीपप्रदानेन चक्षुष्मानभिजायते ॥
अन्नदः सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किंचिन्मनसेच्छति ॥33 ॥
2.7.m: Likewise, by giving a lamp, he is born endowed with good vision. / A giver of food attains everything, whatever he desires in his mind.

2.7.s:
pānakānāṃ pradānena tṛptimāpnotyanuttamāma ..
vasudo rūpamāpnoti rūpamāpnoti rūpyadaḥ .. 34 ..
2.7.d:
पानकानां प्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम ॥
वसुदो रूपमाप्नोति रूपमाप्नोति रूप्यदः ॥ 34 ॥
2.7.m: By giving sweet beverages, he attains unsurpassed contentment. / A giver of wealth obtains beauty; a giver of silver obtains beauty.

2.7.s:
rukmadassarvamāpnoti śriyamāpnoti sarvadaḥ ..
chatradaḥ svargamāpnoti tālavṛntaprado divam .. 35 ..
2.7.d:
रुक्मदस्सर्वमाप्नोति श्रियमाप्नोति सर्वदः ॥
छत्रदः स्वर्गमाप्नोति तालवृन्तप्रदो दिवम् ॥ 35 ॥
2.7.m: A giver of gold attains everything; a giver of all attains prosperity. / A giver of an umbrella attains heaven; a giver of a palm-leaf fan attains the celestial realm.

2.7.s:
cāmarāṇāṃ pradānena rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ ..
patākāyāḥ pradānena sarvapāpānvyapohati .. 36 ..
2.7.d:
चामराणां प्रदानेन राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥
पताकायाः प्रदानेन सर्वपापान्व्यपोहति ॥ 36 ॥
2.7.m: By the giving of chowries, one becomes a righteous king. / By the giving of a pennant, he removes all sins.

2.7.s:
dhvajadānena loke'smindhvajabhūto bhavennaraḥ ..
nānāvidhānāṃ bhogānāṃ tathā rāma pradāyakaḥ .. 37 ..
2.7.d:
ध्वजदानेन लोकेऽस्मिन्ध्वजभूतो भवेन्नरः ॥
नानाविधानां भोगानां तथा राम प्रदायकः ॥ 37 ॥
2.7.m: By giving a banner, a man becomes an eminent standard in this world. / So too, O Rāma, a giver of various kinds of pleasures

2.7.s:
tāneva bhogānāpnoti sarvamāpnoti bhūmidaḥ ..
devamālyāpanayanādgodānaphalamāpnuyāt .. 38 ..
2.7.d:
तानेव भोगानाप्नोति सर्वमाप्नोति भूमिदः ॥
देवमाल्यापनयनाद्गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 38 ॥
2.7.m: attains those very pleasures; a giver of land attains everything. / From removing the old garlands of a god, one obtains the fruit of giving a cow.

2.7.s:
tadāhutipradānena tallokamabhipadyate ..
namaskārapraṇāmābhyāmenobhiḥ pratimucyate .. 39 ..
2.7.d:
तदाहुतिप्रदानेन तल्लोकमभिपद्यते ॥
नमस्कारप्रणामाभ्यामेनोभिः प्रतिमुच्यते ॥ 39 ॥
2.7.m: By offering oblations to him, he enters his world. / Through obeisance and prostrations, he is freed from sins.

2.7.s:
pradakṣiṇaṃ tathā kṛtvā bhavatyācāravārannaraḥ ..
stutvā ca devatāṃ rāma manoduḥkhātpramucyate ..40..
2.7.d:
प्रदक्षिणं तथा कृत्वा भवत्याचारवारन्नरः ॥
स्तुत्वा च देवतां राम मनोदुःखात्प्रमुच्यते ॥40॥
2.7.m: And having circumambulated [the temple], a man becomes endowed with good conduct. / And having praised a deity, O Rāma, he is freed from grief of the mind.

2.7.s:
santarpayitvā toyena tṛptiṃ samadhigacchati ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena viśuddhenāntarāpmanā .. 41 ..
2.7.d:
सन्तर्पयित्वा तोयेन तृप्तिं समधिगच्छति ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन विशुद्धेनान्तराप्मना ॥ 41 ॥
2.7.m: Having satisfied [the deity] with water, he arrives at contentment. / Therefore, with all effort, with a purified inner self,

2.7.s:
arcāsthāḥ pūjayetsarvā devatā bhūridarśana ..
tadāśritāṃśca yuñjīta tadā tadvidhipāragān .. 42 ..
2.7.d:
अर्चास्थाः पूजयेत्सर्वा देवता भूरिदर्शन ॥
तदाश्रितांश्च युञ्जीत तदा तद्विधिपारगान् ॥ 42 ॥
2.7.m: one should worship all the deities residing in images, O man of vast insight, / and one should employ their attendants, who are masters of the rituals for them.

2.7.s:
tatpūjane tathā rāma tāṃśca sampūjayetsadā ..
brāhmaṇāśca niyoktavyā vedoktasurapūjane ..43 ..
2.7.d:
तत्पूजने तथा राम तांश्च सम्पूजयेत्सदा ॥
ब्राह्मणाश्च नियोक्तव्या वेदोक्तसुरपूजने ॥43 ॥
2.7.m: In their worship, O Rāma, one should always honour them as well. / And brahmins should be appointed to worship the gods as prescribed by the Veda.

2.7.s:
yasya rājñastu viṣaye devaveśma viśīryate ..
tasya sīdati tadrāṣṭraṃ devaveśma yathā tathā .. 44 ..
2.7.d:
यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये देववेश्म विशीर्यते ॥
तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं देववेश्म यथा तथा ॥ 44 ॥
2.7.m: In whose realm, however, a god's temple falls into ruin, / the kingdom of that king collapses just as does the god's temple.

2.7.s:
saṃskāraṃ lambhayedyastu devaveśma purātanam ..
sa ca saukhyamavāpnoti yatrayatrābhijāyate .. 45 ..
2.7.d:
संस्कारं लम्भयेद्यस्तु देववेश्म पुरातनम् ॥
स च सौख्यमवाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥ 45 ॥
2.7.m: He who brings about the restoration of an ancient temple of a god, / he obtains happiness wherever he is reborn.

2.7.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgānāṃ sadā tridaśaveśmanām ..
bhūyaḥ saṃskārakartā ca labhate muktijaṃ phalam .. 46 ..
2.7.d:
वापीकूपतडागानां सदा त्रिदशवेश्मनाम् ॥
भूयः संस्कारकर्ता च लभते मुक्तिजं फलम् ॥ 46 ॥
2.7.m: One who repeatedly restores reservoirs, wells, ponds, / and always the dwellings of the gods, obtains the fruit born of liberation.

2.7.s:
devasampūjanādrāma vṛddhiṃ samupagacchati ..
rājñastu viṣaye yasya pūjyante satataṃ surāḥ ..47 ..
2.7.d:
देवसम्पूजनाद्राम वृद्धिं समुपगच्छति ॥
राज्ञस्तु विषये यस्य पूज्यन्ते सततं सुराः ॥47 ॥
2.7.m: From worshipping the gods, O Rāma, one attains prosperity. / In the realm of that king where the gods are constantly worshipped,

2.7.s:
ativṛṣṭiranāvṛṣṭirmūṣakāḥ śalabhāḥ śukāḥ ..
rākṣasāśca piśācāśca ripavaśca sudāruṇāḥ ..48..
2.7.d:
अतिवृष्टिरनावृष्टिर्मूषकाः शलभाः शुकाः ॥
राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च रिपवश्च सुदारुणाः ॥48॥
2.7.m: excessive rain, drought, mice, locusts, parrots, / rākṣasas, piśācas, and terrible enemies,

2.7.s: ītayaśca tathaivānyā na bhavanti dvijottama..49..
2.7.d: ईतयश्च तथैवान्या न भवन्ति द्विजोत्तम॥49॥
2.7.m: and likewise other calamities, do not arise, O foremost of the twice-born.

2.7.s:
tasmātprayatnena sadā narendraiḥ pūjā vidheyā viṣaye surāṇām..
surārcanātpūtasamastapāpāssvargaṃ kṣitīśāściramāpnuvanti ..50..
2.32
puṣkara uvāca ..
brāhmaṇānpūjayedrājā brāhmaṇānpālayetsadā ..
brāhmaṇā hi mahābhāga devānāmapi daivatam ..1..
brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣitiṃ dadyādbhogānanyāṃśca pārthivaḥ ..
brāhmaṇeṣu tu yaddattaṃ nidhistatpāralaukikam .. 2 ..
vedalāṅgalakṛṣṭeṣu dvijakṣetreṣu bhārata ..
uptasya dānabījasya phalasyānto na vidyate ..3..
brahmasvaṃ caiva nādadyādbrahmasvaṃ pālayettathā ..
brahmasvaharaṇādrāma narakaṃ paśyate naraḥ .. 4 ..
na viṣaṃ viṣamityāhurbrahmasvaṃ viṣamucyatai ..
viṣamekākinaṃ hanti brahmasvaṃ saptapūruṣam .. 5 ..
brahmasvaṃ praṇayādbhuktaṃ hinastyāsaptamaṃ kulam ..
drohādbhuktaṃ tadeveha kulānāṃ pātayecchatam .. 6 ..
2.7.d:
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन सदा नरेन्द्रैः पूजा विधेया विषये सुराणाम्॥
सुरार्चनात्पूतसमस्तपापास्स्वर्गं क्षितीशाश्चिरमाप्नुवन्ति ॥50॥
2.32
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
ब्राह्मणान्पूजयेद्राजा ब्राह्मणान्पालयेत्सदा ॥
ब्राह्मणा हि महाभाग देवानामपि दैवतम् ॥1॥
ब्राह्मणानां क्षितिं दद्याद्भोगानन्यांश्च पार्थिवः ॥
ब्राह्मणेषु तु यद्दत्तं निधिस्तत्पारलौकिकम् ॥ 2 ॥
वेदलाङ्गलकृष्टेषु द्विजक्षेत्रेषु भारत ॥
उप्तस्य दानबीजस्य फलस्यान्तो न विद्यते ॥3॥
ब्रह्मस्वं चैव नादद्याद्ब्रह्मस्वं पालयेत्तथा ॥
ब्रह्मस्वहरणाद्राम नरकं पश्यते नरः ॥ 4 ॥
न विषं विषमित्याहुर्ब्रह्मस्वं विषमुच्यतै ॥
विषमेकाकिनं हन्ति ब्रह्मस्वं सप्तपूरुषम् ॥ 5 ॥
ब्रह्मस्वं प्रणयाद्भुक्तं हिनस्त्यासप्तमं कुलम् ॥
द्रोहाद्भुक्तं तदेवेह कुलानां पातयेच्छतम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.7.m:
Therefore, worship of the gods should always be performed with effort by kings in their realm; / purified of all sins by the worship of the gods, rulers of the earth attain heaven for a long time.
2.32 / Puṣkara said: / A king should honour brahmins; he should always protect brahmins. / For brahmins, O fortunate one, are the deities even of the gods.
An earthly ruler should give land to brahmins and other enjoyments. / For what is given to brahmins is a treasure in the other world.
When the seed of a gift is sown in the fields of the twice-born / that are ploughed by the plough of the Vedas, O descendant of Bharata, there is no end to the fruit.
One must not seize the property of a brahmin, and one must protect the property of a brahmin. / From taking the property of a brahmin, O Rāma, a man beholds hell.
They say that poison is not poison; the property of a brahmin is called poison. / Poison slays a single individual; the property of a brahmin slays seven generations.
The property of a brahmin enjoyed out of fondness destroys the family up to the seventh [generation]; / that very property enjoyed out of hostility in this world brings down a hundred families.

2.7.s:
suvarṇamekaṃ gāmekāṃ bhūmerapyekamaṅgulam. ..
harannarakamāpnoti yāvadābhūtasamplavam .. 7 ..
dṛṣṭvā viṭaṃ durācāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ na dviṣetkvacit ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ parīvādānnāśamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 8 ..
na jātu brāhmaṇaṃ hanyātsarvapāpeṣvavasthitam ..
naivāsti brāhmaṇavadhātpāpaṃ gurutaraṃ kvacit .. 9 ..
brahmahā narakaṃ yāti yāvadābhūtasamplavam ..
varṣāṇāmayutaṃ rāma pacyate snāyupūrite .. 10 ..
śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃśūngṛhṇātīha dvijanmanām ..
kartā tāvanti varṣāṇi kṛtakṛnnarake vaset .. 11 ..
upadruto dvijo yena tyajejjīvitamātmanaḥ ..
brahmahatyā bhavettasya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 12 ..
dehatyāgācca narakaṃ brāhmaṇo'pi prapadyate ..
tena cādhikamāpnoti rāma pāpaṃ narādhamaḥ ..13..
adaivaṃ daivataṃ kuryuḥ kuryurdaivamadaivatam ..
brāhmaṇāśca mahābhāgā namasyāste sadaiva hi .. 14 ..
2.7.d:
सुवर्णमेकं गामेकां भूमेरप्येकमङ्गुलम्॥।
हरन्नरकमाप्नोति यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् ॥ 7 ॥
दृष्ट्वा विटं दुराचारं ब्राह्मणं न द्विषेत्क्वचित् ॥
ब्राह्मणानां परीवादान्नाशमाप्नोति मानवः ॥ 8 ॥
न जातु ब्राह्मणं हन्यात्सर्वपापेष्ववस्थितम् ॥
नैवास्ति ब्राह्मणवधात्पापं गुरुतरं क्वचित् ॥ 9 ॥
ब्रह्महा नरकं याति यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् ॥
वर्षाणामयुतं राम पच्यते स्नायुपूरिते ॥ 10 ॥
शोणितं यावतः पांशून्गृह्णातीह द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
कर्ता तावन्ति वर्षाणि कृतकृन्नरके वसेत् ॥ 11 ॥
उपद्रुतो द्विजो येन त्यजेज्जीवितमात्मनः ॥
ब्रह्महत्या भवेत्तस्य नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 12 ॥
देहत्यागाच्च नरकं ब्राह्मणोऽपि प्रपद्यते ॥
तेन चाधिकमाप्नोति राम पापं नराधमः ॥13॥
अदैवं दैवतं कुर्युः कुर्युर्दैवमदैवतम् ॥
ब्राह्मणाश्च महाभागा नमस्यास्ते सदैव हि ॥ 14 ॥
2.7.m:
Stealing a single piece of gold, a single cow, or even a single finger-breadth of land, / one goes to hell until the dissolution of all beings.
Having seen a deceitful or misbehaved brahmin, one must never hate him. / From slandering brahmins, a person meets destruction.
One should never kill a brahmin, even one persisting in all sins. / There is nowhere any sin greater than the killing of a brahmin.
A killer of a brahmin goes to hell until the dissolution of all beings. / For ten thousand years, O Rāma, he is cooked in a place filled with sinews.
For as many dust particles as the blood of the twice-born touches here, / for that many years the perpetrator of the deed must dwell in hell.
A twice-born person who, harassed by someone, should abandon his own life— / the sin of killing a brahmin accrues to that person; no doubt should be entertained on this point.
And from abandoning his body, even a brahmin goes to hell; / because of that, O Rāma, that vilest of men incurs even greater sin.
They can make a non-deity into a deity, and a deity into a non-deity; / the highly fortunate brahmins must indeed always be bowed to.

2.7.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā kāryaṃ yatnātkurvīta pārthivaḥ ..
kālātipātaṃ ca tathā viprakārye na kārayet .. 15 ..
niṣpīḍitastūpavasedyena vidvānniśāṃ janaḥ ..
sa rāma narakaṃ yāti varṣāṇāṃ tu daśāyutam .. 16 ..
brāhmaṇī rudatī hanti kulaṃ rodāyate dhruvam ..
tadaśruvahnirdahati kulaṃ tripuruṣaṃ dhruvam .. 17 ..
vidvānapyathavāvidvānbrāhmaṇo mānamarhati ..
praṇītaścāpraṇītaśca yathāgnirdvijapuṅgava .. 18 ..
pratiṣṭhāṃ prāpnuvantīha surā viprapratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 19 ..
tanmukhe tu tathāśnanti devāśca pitṛbhiḥ saha ..
vahnau hutācchreṣṭhatamaṃ hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu .. 20 ..
askandamaviruddhaṃ ca prāyaścittairvivarjitam ..
yāvato grasate grāsānvidvānvipraḥ susaṃskṛtaḥ .. 21 ..
annapradasya tāvantaḥ kratavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ karānmuktaṃ toyaṃ śirasi dhārayet .. 22 ..
2.7.d:
ब्राह्मणानां तथा कार्यं यत्नात्कुर्वीत पार्थिवः ॥
कालातिपातं च तथा विप्रकार्ये न कारयेत् ॥ 15 ॥
निष्पीडितस्तूपवसेद्येन विद्वान्निशां जनः ॥
स राम नरकं याति वर्षाणां तु दशायुतम् ॥ 16 ॥
ब्राह्मणी रुदती हन्ति कुलं रोदायते ध्रुवम् ॥
तदश्रुवह्निर्दहति कुलं त्रिपुरुषं ध्रुवम् ॥ 17 ॥
विद्वानप्यथवाविद्वान्ब्राह्मणो मानमर्हति ॥
प्रणीतश्चाप्रणीतश्च यथाग्निर्द्विजपुङ्गव ॥ 18 ॥
प्रतिष्ठां प्राप्नुवन्तीह सुरा विप्रप्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 19 ॥
तन्मुखे तु तथाश्नन्ति देवाश्च पितृभिः सह ॥
वह्नौ हुताच्छ्रेष्ठतमं हुतं विप्रमुखाग्निषु ॥ 20 ॥
अस्कन्दमविरुद्धं च प्रायश्चित्तैर्विवर्जितम् ॥
यावतो ग्रसते ग्रासान्विद्वान्विप्रः सुसंस्कृतः ॥ 21 ॥
अन्नप्रदस्य तावन्तः क्रतवः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
ब्राह्मणानां करान्मुक्तं तोयं शिरसि धारयेत् ॥ 22 ॥
2.7.m:
Likewise, a king should zealously attend to the affairs of brahmins; / and he should not cause any delay in the work of a brahmin.
The person through whose oppression a learned man fasts during the night, / he goes to hell, O Rāma, for a hundred thousand years.
A weeping brahmin woman surely destroys a family and makes it weep; / the fire of her tears surely burns a family for three generations.
Whether learned or unlearned, a brahmin is worthy of honor, / just as fire is, O best of the twice-born, whether consecrated or unconsecrated.
Here, gods installed by brahmins attain their proper standing.
The gods eat in their mouths together with the ancestors; / an offering poured into the fires of a brahmin's mouth is superior to an offering poured into [sacrificial] fire.
It does not spill, it is not hindered, and it is free from [need of] expiations; / as many mouthfuls as a learned, properly consecrated brahmin consumes,
just so many sacrifices are declared for the giver of food. / One should bear on one's head the water released from the hands of brahmins,

2.7.s:
brāhmaṇasya kare yasmātsarvatīrthasamāgamaḥ ..
brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samutpannaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 23 ..
amoghaśāpā dharmajña kathitāste jagattraye ..
āśīrvādamamoghaṃ ca brāhmaṇānāṃ prakīrtitam .. 24 ..
āśīrvādaparāḥ kāryāstasmādrājñā dvijottamāḥ ..
yaiḥ kṛtaḥ sarvabhakṣyognirapeyaśca mahodadhiḥ .. 25 ..
kṣayī somo'javṛṣaṇastathaiva ca śatakratuḥ ..
yeṣāṃ kopāgniradyāpi daṇḍake nopaśāmyati .. 26 ..
vipulaśca tathā yeṣāṃ prasādo bhṛgunandana ..
yeṣāṃ prasādātkṣīṇo'pi vṛddhimicchati candramāḥ .. 27 ..
yeṣāṃ prasādādrakṣobhirnābhibhūyeta bhāskaraḥ ..
yeṣāṃ prasādādvipulāṃ kārtavīryaḥ śriyaṃ gataḥ .. 28 ..
yeṣāṃ prasādāddhanado dhanādhyakṣatvamāgataḥ ..
asnātaḥ snānamāpnoti vratamāpnotyathāvratī .. 29..
2.7.d:
ब्राह्मणस्य करे यस्मात्सर्वतीर्थसमागमः ॥
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समुत्पन्नं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 23 ॥
अमोघशापा धर्मज्ञ कथितास्ते जगत्त्रये ॥
आशीर्वादममोघं च ब्राह्मणानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 24 ॥
आशीर्वादपराः कार्यास्तस्माद्राज्ञा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
यैः कृतः सर्वभक्ष्योग्निरपेयश्च महोदधिः ॥ 25 ॥
क्षयी सोमोऽजवृषणस्तथैव च शतक्रतुः ॥
येषां कोपाग्निरद्यापि दण्डके नोपशाम्यति ॥ 26 ॥
विपुलश्च तथा येषां प्रसादो भृगुनन्दन ॥
येषां प्रसादात्क्षीणोऽपि वृद्धिमिच्छति चन्द्रमाः ॥ 27 ॥
येषां प्रसादाद्रक्षोभिर्नाभिभूयेत भास्करः ॥
येषां प्रसादाद्विपुलां कार्तवीर्यः श्रियं गतः ॥ 28 ॥
येषां प्रसादाद्धनदो धनाध्यक्षत्वमागतः ॥

ते तृप्तास्तर्पयन्तीह भुवनं सकलं सुराः ॥

2.7.m:
by their mere word—what could be greater than that? / Enjoyment, sovereignty, and heaven are obtained by their word.
Even their anger, which always abides in them, produces purification, O Rāma; / they should be worshipped, they should be honored, and one should provide them with wives.
Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas uphold the entire world; / here, brahmins cause the gods to prosper, O son of Bhṛgu.
Those gods, being gratified, gratify the entire world here. / An oblation offered into the fire by a brahmin, O upholder of the Bhṛgu race,
reaches the sun; from the sun, rain occurs on the surface of the earth; / and from that comes the production of food, and from food the arising of beings is remembered.
Therefore, all the three worlds are sustained by brahmins alone; / the earth has brahmins as its source, the heavens have brahmins as their source.
These worlds belong to the brahmins, and the other worlds as well. / When the twice-born, due to obstruction of sacrifices, Vedic study, and austerities,

ब्राह्मणानां वचः कार्यं राजभिः सततोत्थितैः ॥ 37 ॥

राजा ब्राह्मणवाक्येन यः कुर्याच्छासनादिकम् ॥ 39 ॥
सम्यग्वाप्यथवासम्यक्तेन नाके महीयते ॥
उल्लंघ्य शास्त्रं नृपतिर्यो यथारुचि वर्तते ॥ 40 ॥
स राम नरकं याति सुकृतेनापि कर्मणा ॥
यत्र ब्राह्मणवाक्यानि न करोतीह यो नरः॥। 41 ॥
न तत्र दोषवान्विप्रो राजा दोषेण लिप्यते ॥

यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये ब्राह्मणः सीदति क्षुधा ॥
तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं दुर्भिक्षव्याधितस्करैः ॥ 43 ॥
2.7.m:

Dharma, wealth, and pleasure are established in their speech; / both punishment and favor [rest] upon the word of brahmins.
In this world, both must always be carried out by the king who desires prosperity. / A king who, according to the word of a brahmin, carries out decrees and the like,
whether done properly or improperly, is honored in heaven by that [action]. / A king who transgresses the treatises and acts according to his own pleasure,
he goes to hell, O Rāma, even in spite of his good deeds. / In whichever matter a man does not carry out the words of a brahmin,
there the brahmin is not at fault; the king is stained with guilt. / A ten-year-old brahmin and a hundred-year-old king,
one should know them as father and son; and between the two, the brahmin is the father. / In whose realm a brahmin languishes with hunger, / that king's realm declines through famine, disease, and thieves.

2.7.m:
Therefore, the twice-born must be worshipped, bowed down to, and given shares / with all effort by a king desiring both worlds.
What the fully contented brahmins say, that the deities applaud; / when the visible gods are pleased, the invisible gods are always pleased.
2.33
Puṣkara said:
A king should protect and honor virtuous women; / devoted wives, one and all, uphold the three worlds.
Devoted to her husband's vow, dedicated to her husband, intent on honoring her husband: / such a woman goes to heaven together with her husband, O best of the twice-born.
Whatever hardship devoted wives endure along with their followers, O twice-born, / through that, reaching heaven, they attain manifold happiness.
Great indeed is their power, and their splendor is exceedingly hard to endure; / they should not be angered, they should not be neglected, and one should never disrespect them.
A king should not summon [her] for offenses; her husband would be the one to be punished, / or her son; according to statecraft, the king is not the master [over her] anywhere.

2.7.m:
A woman is not declared virtuous merely by guarding her sexual organ; / she who does not act disagreeably toward her husband, she is remembered as a virtuous woman.
She who seeks the pleasure and welfare of her husband in deed, mind, and speech, / intent on worshipping her husband—that woman is remembered as a virtuous woman.
They must be bowed to, worshipped, and saluted, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / by the king with every effort, and by people everywhere.
And the best of kings should support an unprotected virtuous woman; / whatever gift is given to her is proclaimed to be endless.
By dishonouring virtuous women, a man burns his family; / by revering them, O Rāma, he elevates his own family.
Not by wealth, not by grain, not by good conduct, not by kinsmen, / not by sacrifices accompanied by sacrificial fees, and likewise not by sacred study,
do they call families ignoble, but by the misconduct of women. / Families in which the women are virtuous, O Rāma, bearing the yoke of the lineage,

यामयो यानि गेहानि शपन्त्यप्रतिपूजिताः ॥
तानि कृत्याह तानीव विनश्यन्ति समन्ततः ॥ 19 ॥
2.7.m:
are great families in this world, even if impoverished in wealth. / Even among sons, that son is [superior] for whom a virtuous woman is the fire-drill.
One should employ the son of a virtuous woman in offerings to the gods and offerings to the ancestors; / the giving of even a little to him is declared to yield great religious merit.
Just as the Gāyatrī, O Rāma, just as the Gaṅgā, best of rivers, / is purifying merely by being recited, so is an excellent, virtuous woman.
Women, O tiger of the Bhṛgus, are never corrupted; / month after month their menses removes their misdeeds.
Soma gave them purity, a Gandharva cultured speech, / and Agni all-purifying quality; therefore women are free from blemish.
Brahmins are pure from the feet; cows are pure from the back; / goats and horses are pure from the mouth; but women are pure everywhere.
The households that the female relatives curse when not properly honoured / perish completely, as if destroyed by a Kṛtyā.

मिथ्या न साध्वी भवतीह लोके भवत्यथास्मिन्नपरे च राम ॥
साध्व्यस्तथा पूज्यतमा प्रदिष्टा लोकेषु सर्वेषु चराचरेषु ॥ 21 ॥ ॥
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे साध्वीमाहात्म्यं नाम त्रयस्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 33 ॥
2.34
राम उवाच ॥ ॥
साध्वीनां श्रोतुमिच्छामि देव धर्मानशेषतः ॥
साध्व्यो हि नार्यो लोकानामाधार इह कीर्तितः ॥ 1 ॥
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
एतदेव परं राम रामाणां धर्मकारणम् ॥
यदासां सर्वकार्येषु नित्यं हि परतन्त्रता ॥ 2 ॥
बाल्ये पितुर्वशे तिष्ठेत्पाणिग्राहस्य यौवने ॥
पुत्राणां भर्तरि प्रेते न स्त्री स्वातन्त्र्यमर्हति ॥ 3 ॥
पित्रा भर्त्रा सुतेनेह नेच्छेद्विरहमात्मनः ॥
तेषां च विरहेण स्त्री गर्ह्ये कुर्यादुभे कुले ॥ 4 ॥
2.7.m:
Between women and the fortunes of households there is no distinction at all; / therefore, with every effort, women should always be honoured.
Not falsely does a woman become virtuous in this world, and in the next world as well, O Rāma; / virtuous women are declared most worthy of honour in all the worlds, among both moving and unmoving beings.
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, entitled “The Greatness of the Virtuous Woman,” in the second book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
2.34 / Rāma said: / I desire to hear completely, O lord, the dharmas of virtuous women; / for virtuous women are declared to be the foundation of the worlds in this world.
Puṣkara said: / This alone is the supreme cause of dharma for women, O Rāma: / namely, their perpetual dependence in all matters.
In childhood she should remain under the control of her father, in youth under that of her husband, / and under that of her sons when her husband is deceased; a woman does not deserve independence.
She should not wish for separation from her father, her husband, or her son in this world; / by separation from them, a woman would bring blame upon both families.

2.7.d:
सदा प्रहृष्टया भाव्यं गृहकार्ये च दक्षया ॥
सुसंस्कृतोपस्करया व्यये चामुक्तहस्तया ॥ 5 ॥
यः प्रदद्यात्पिता त्वेनां तदभावेपि कारकः ॥
तं शुश्रूषेत जीवन्तं संस्थितं न तु लंघयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
मङ्गलार्थं स्वस्त्ययनं यज्ञश्चासां प्रजायते ॥
प्रयुज्यते विवाहेषु प्रदानं स्वामिकारितम् ॥ 7 ॥
अनृतावृतुकालोक्ते मन्त्रसंस्कारकृत्पतिः ॥
सुखं नित्यं ददातीह परलोके च योषितः ॥ 8 ॥
विशीलः कामवृत्तो वा गुणैर्वा परिवर्जितः ॥
उपचर्यः स्त्रिया साध्व्या सततं देववत्पतिः ॥ 9 ॥
नास्ति स्त्रीणां पृथग्यज्ञो न व्रतं नाप्युपोषितम् ॥
पतिं शुश्रूषते यत्तु तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ॥ 10 ॥
पाणिग्राहस्य साध्वी स्त्री जीवतो वा मृतस्य वा ॥
पतिलोकमभीप्सन्ती नाचरेत्किञ्चिदप्रियम् ॥11॥
कामं तु क्षपयेद्देहं पुष्पमूलफलैः शुभैः ॥
न तु नामापि गृह्णीयात्पत्यौ प्रेते परस्य तु॥12॥
2.7.m:
She should always be cheerful, skilled in household duties, / with household utensils well maintained, and unsparing in restraint regarding expenditure.
To whomsoever her father gives her, or, in his absence, the one authorized to give, / she should attend upon him while he lives, and should not transgress against him when he has passed away.
The benediction recited for auspiciousness constitutes their sacrifice; / the giving of the bride, arranged by the master, is performed at marriages.
The husband, who performs the sacrament with sacred formulas at the prescribed fertile time as well as outside it, / constantly bestows happiness upon a woman in this world and in the next world.
Though ill-behaved, given to sensual pleasure, or devoid of virtues, / a husband must always be served like a deity by a virtuous woman.
There is no separate sacrifice for women, no vow, and no fasting; / in that she attends upon her husband, by that she is exalted in heaven.
Toward the husband who took her hand, whether he is alive or dead, / a virtuous woman desiring the world of her husband should not do anything displeasing.
She may indeed emaciate her body with auspicious flowers, roots, and fruits, / but she should never even utter the name of another man when her husband is deceased.

2.7.d:
आसीतामरणात्क्षान्ता नियता ब्रह्मचारिणी ॥
यो धर्म एकपत्नीनां काङ्क्षन्ती तमनुत्तमम्॥13॥
अनेकानि सहस्राणि सुमुग्धब्रह्मचारिणाम् ॥
दिवङ्गतानां विप्राणामकृत्वा कुलसन्ततिम् ॥ 14 ॥
मृते भर्तरि साध्वी स्त्री ब्रह्मचर्ये व्यवस्थिता॥
स्वर्गं गच्छत्यपुत्रापि यथा ते ब्रह्मचारिणः ॥ 15॥
अपत्यलोभाद्या तु स्त्री भर्तारमतिवर्त्तते ॥
सेह निन्दामवाप्नोति परलोकाच्च हीयते ॥ 16 ॥
नान्योत्पन्ना प्रजास्तीह न चाप्यन्यपरिग्रहा ॥
न द्वितीयश्च साध्वीनां कश्चिद्भर्तोपदिश्यते॥17॥
पतिं हित्वा निकृष्टं स्वं चोत्कृष्टं या निषेवते॥
निन्द्यैव लोके भवति परपूर्वेति चोच्यते ॥ 18 ॥
व्यभिचारात्तु भर्तुः स्त्री लोकान्प्राप्नोति निन्दितान् ॥
शृगालयोनिं चाप्नोति पापरोगैश्च पीड्यते ॥ 19 ॥
पतिं या नाभिचरति मनोवाग्देहसंयता ॥
इहाग्र्यां कीर्त्तिमाप्नोति परलोके च शस्यते ॥ 20 ॥
2.7.m:
Until death she should remain patient, self-controlled, and celibate, / aspiring to that unsurpassed dharma of women devoted to a single husband.
Many thousands of brahmins who were pure lifelong celibates / went to heaven without having produced lineage succession.
When her husband has died, a virtuous woman established in celibacy / goes to heaven even if sonless, just like those celibates.
However, the woman who transgresses against her husband out of desire for offspring / incurs blame in this world and falls from the next world.
Offspring begotten by another are not recognized here, nor is one who has accepted another [husband]; / no second husband is ever prescribed for virtuous women.
She who abandons her own inferior husband and serves a superior one / is blameworthy in the world and is called “previously belonging to another.”
Through unfaithfulness to her husband, a woman attains condemned worlds; / she obtains rebirth as a jackal and is tormented by loathsome diseases.
She who does not betray her husband, restraining her mind, speech, and body, / obtains foremost fame in this world and is praised in the next world.

2.7.d:
पत्युरभ्यधिकं नारी नोपवासव्रतं चरेत् ॥
अनायुष्यं द्विजश्रेष्ठ पत्युस्तस्यास्तदुच्यते ॥21॥
देवताराधनं कुर्यात्कामं वा ब्राह्मणोत्तम ॥
नारी पतिव्रता राम प्राप्तानुज्ञां तु भर्त्तृतः ॥ 22 ॥
नारी खल्वननुज्ञाता पित्रा भर्त्रा सुतेन वा ॥
विफलं तद्भवेत्तस्या यत्करोत्यौर्ध्वदैहिकम् ॥23॥
स्त्रीणां पूज्यतमा लोके देवतागृहवासिनाम् ॥
या स्ताः सम्पूजनीयाः स्युस्तासामेव यथाविधि ॥ 24 ॥
तासां च पूजनं कार्यं विदितं स्वामिनस्तथा ॥
अन्यथा चेत्प्रवर्त्तेत निर्ग्राह्या सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 25 ॥
गत्वान्यपुरुषं नारी नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
कूटशाल्मलिमित्युक्तं यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् ॥ 26 ॥
गर्हिता च तथा पत्युर्नरकं याति भार्गव ॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तथैवाप्रियवादिनी ॥ 27 ॥
सर्वावस्थास्वपि स्त्रीषु न वधो विद्यते द्विज ॥
परेण शङ्कितामेनां संयतां वासयेद्गृहे ॥ 28 ॥
2.7.m:
A woman should not undertake a fast or a vow exceeding [that of] her husband; / that is declared, O best of the twice-born, to diminish the lifespan of her husband.
Or she may perform the worship of deities at will, O best of brahmins, / if, being a devoted wife, O Rāma, she has obtained permission from her husband.
Indeed, for a woman unauthorized by her father, husband, or son, / whatever funeral or ancestral rite she performs becomes fruitless for her.
The most venerable deities in the world for women are those dwelling in the house; / those which are to be worshipped must be properly revered by them.
And their worship must be done with the knowledge of the master; / if she acts otherwise, she is declared subject to restraint.
A woman who goes to another man reaches the hell / named Kūṭaśālmali until the dissolution of all beings.
Likewise, she who is contemptuous of her husband, O descendant of Bhṛgu, goes to hell / for ten thousand years, as does one who speaks harshly.
Under no circumstances is there killing of women, O twice-born; / if suspected [of infidelity] with another, one should keep her confined in the house.

2.7.d:
हृताधिकारां मलिनां पिण्डमात्रोपजीविनीम् ॥
परिभूतामधःशय्यां वासयेद्व्यभिचारिणीम् ॥ 29 ॥
मूलकर्म न कर्त्तव्यं कथञ्चिदपि योषिता ॥
मूलकर्मरता नारी कल्पं नरकमावसेत ॥ 30॥
दौर्भाग्यं महदाप्नोति तत्र यत्राभिजायते ॥
या च नारी सपत्नीनां कुर्याद्दौर्भाग्यकारणम् ॥ 31 ॥
कुहकैः पश्यति सापि कल्पानां नरके द्विज ॥
पुंस्त्वमूलं तथा लक्ष्मों पत्युर्हिंसति सा तथा ॥32॥
यक्षरक्षःपिशाचानां मूलकर्मरता सदा ॥
वश्यो भवति लोकेषु भर्ता तस्यास्तथैव च ॥ 33 ॥
नारी कृत्वा पतिं वश्यं सततं मूलकर्मणा ॥
लभतेन्ते तु दौर्भाग्यं भूतैर्वा भक्ष्यते ध्रुवम् ॥34॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन मूलकर्म विवर्जयेत् ॥
आत्मानमथ भर्तारं नाशयेन्मूलकर्मणा ॥ 35 ॥
2.7.m:
Stripped of authority, unkempt, subsisting only on a ball of food, / humiliated, and sleeping on the ground—one should keep an unfaithful woman thus.
Sorcery with roots should never be performed by a woman under any circumstances; / a woman engaged in sorcery with roots will inhabit hell for an aeon.
She incurs great misfortune wherever she is reborn, / that woman who causes misfortune to her co-wives.
Through deceitful arts, she too, O twice-born, looks upon hell for aeons; / thus she destroys the masculine power and good fortune of her husband.
Always devoted to root-magic, she belongs to yakṣas, rakṣasas, and piśācas, / and so her husband becomes completely subject to her in the worlds.
Having made her husband subject [to her] continuously by root-magic, / a woman in the end attains misfortune, or is certainly devoured by spirits.
Therefore, with every effort she should avoid root-magic; / she would destroy both herself and her husband through root-magic.

2.7.d:
ब्राह्मणी न पिबेन्मद्यं न च विट्क्षत्रियस्त्रियः ॥
सुरां पिबेयुर्धर्मज्ञ तत्पानान्नाशमाप्नुयुः ॥ 36 ॥
ततो भवति धर्मज्ञ जलौका रक्तपायिका ॥
कल्पावशेषं सकलं तेन घोरेण कर्मणा ॥ 37 ॥
परवेश्मरुचिर्न स्यान्न स्यात्कलहशालिनी ॥
न च तिष्ठेत्तथा द्वारि न च राम गवाक्षके ॥38॥
मण्डनं वर्जयेन्नारी तथा प्रोषित भर्तृका ॥
देवताराधनपरा भवेद्भर्तृहिते रता ॥ 39 ॥
धारयेन्मङ्गलार्थाय किञ्चिदाभरणं तथा ॥
न जातु विधवा वेषं कदाचिदपि कारयेत् ॥40.
पतिव्रता तु या नारी सह भर्त्रा दिवङ्गता ॥
कल्पावशेषं मुदिता पूज्यते त्रिदशालये ॥ 41 ॥
पतिव्रतां सवर्णां स्त्रीं द्विजातिः पूर्वमारिणीम ॥
दाहयेदग्निहोत्रेण यज्ञपात्रैश्च धर्मवित् ॥ 42 ॥
भार्यायै पूर्वमारिण्यै दत्त्वाग्नीनन्त्यकर्मणि ॥
पुनर्दारक्रियां कुर्यात्पुनराधानमेव च ॥ 43 ॥
2.7.m:
A brahmin woman should not drink liquor, nor should the women of vaiśyas or kṣatriyas / drink liquor, O knower of dharma; through drinking it, they would meet destruction.
From that [sin], O knower of dharma, she becomes a blood-drinking leech / for all the remainder of an aeon, because of that terrible deed.
She should not desire another's house, nor should she be quarrelsome; / nor should she stand at the door, O Rāma, nor at a latticed window.
A woman whose husband has gone abroad should avoid adornment; / she should be devoted to the worship of the gods, intent on her husband's welfare.
She should wear some ornament for the sake of auspiciousness; / she should never, at any time, assume the appearance of a widow.
A devoted wife who has gone to heaven along with her husband / is honoured, full of joy, in the abode of the thirty [gods] for the remainder of an aeon.
A twice-born man who knows dharma should burn a devoted wife of the same class / who dies before him with the agnihotra fire and with sacrificial vessels.
Having offered the fires at the funeral rites for a wife who has died before him, / he should perform the ceremony of taking another wife and re-establish the fires.

2.7.d:
मृते भर्तरि या साध्वी पुत्रमाश्रित्य भार्गव ॥
तपसा शातयेद्देहं तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ॥ 44 ॥
पतिपक्षे नरं कञ्चित्पुत्राभावे समाश्रयेत् ॥
बिभृयाद्धि स चाप्येनां भोजनाच्छादनैः सदा ॥ 45 ॥
पतिपक्षे समुच्छिन्ने पितृपक्षः प्रभुः स्त्रियः ॥
विषमस्थापि भर्तव्या पितृपक्षे स्वबन्धुभिः ॥ 46 ॥
मृतं भर्तारमादाय यदि वाथ पतिव्रता ॥
प्रविशेद्द्विजशार्दूल ज्वलितं जातवेदसम् ॥ 47 ॥
तिस्रः कोट्योर्द्धकोटी च यानि लोमानि मानवे ॥
तावन्त्येव शताब्दानि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 48 ॥
व्यालग्राही यथा सर्पं बिलादुद्धरते बलात् ॥
एवं भर्त्तारमादाय सह तेनैव गच्छति ॥ 49 ।
सद्वृत्तमध्यापयितुं गतानां स्त्रीणां वियोगक्षतकातराणाम् ॥
तासां मृते जीवितवल्लभे हि नाग्निप्रवेशादपरो हि धर्म ॥ 50 ॥।
2.7.m:
When her husband has died, a virtuous woman who, taking refuge in her son, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / emaciates her body through asceticism, is glorified in heaven on account of that.
In the absence of a son, she should take refuge with some man of her husband's side; / and he should indeed maintain her always with food and clothing.
If the husband's side is extinct, the father's side is the guardian of the woman; / even when in distress, she is to be supported by her own relatives on the father's side.
Or if, taking her deceased husband, a devoted wife / should enter the blazing fire, O tiger among the twice-born,
as many as three and a half crores of hairs are on a human body, / for just that many hundreds of years she is honoured in the heavenly world.
Just as a snake-catcher forcefully pulls a serpent out of a hole, / in the same way, taking her husband, she goes together with him alone.
For those women who have gone to learn virtuous conduct, who are distressed by the wound of separation / when the beloved of their life is dead, there is indeed no other dharma than entering the fire.

2.7.m:
Rāma said:
Declare the deities most worthy of worship by women in the world, / and their proper time, ritual rule, and the fruit arising from worship.
Puṣkara said:
Worship of Śrī should always be performed by women in the home / with flowers, arghya, garlands, food-offerings, incense, lamps, and ointments.
Sweeping the house, O Rāma, and smearing it [with cowdung], / presenting flower-offerings, and whitening it with lime,
one should know all this to be the worship of Śrī, O twice-born. / The bathing, anointing, and application of fragrance and colour,
and the golden complexion of women comes from the worship of Śrī. / On all eighth [tithis], Aśokikā should also be worshipped
with fragrances, garlands, reverent salutations, incense, lamps, and the like. / She who eats on that day at night without oil
becomes free from sorrow wherever she is born. / And if she is not able on all eighth [tithis], O descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.7.m:
then on the dark eighth [tithi] after the full moon of Prauṣṭhapadā has passed, O twice-born, / the worship of the Goddess must certainly be performed according to rule.
Like water in the three worlds, Prakṛti is spoken of among women, / who impels deeds in the worlds, O best of the twice-born.
On the bright fifteenth [tithi], worship of her should be performed / with white garlands and ointments, and with fragrant incense,
and by the giving of red garments, and by the offering of lamps, / and with pulses, and likewise with pastries, cooked foods, and suckable foods.
And having worshipped that goddess, she should eat at night, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / If she is never able [to do this] on every fifteenth [tithi],
the worship of the Goddess must certainly be performed in Kārtika. / A woman who worships Upārti is indeed a devoted wife;
she becomes a virtuous woman always devoted to dharma in the world, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / and her mind never turns toward evil.

2.7.m:
Likewise, on the dark eleventh [tithi] in the month of Phālguna, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / in the bright [fortnight], the worship of the deity should be performed, O best of the upholders of dharma.
From the worship of Chandodeva, she does not obtain a son devoid of virtues; / rather, she undoubtedly obtains one endowed with virtues.
Likewise, with devotion, with fragrances, garlands, and so forth, having reached the eleventh [tithi] / of the bright fortnight of Caitra, she should worship the Vāstudevatā.
Having worshipped her, O highly fortunate one, the destruction of the house does not occur. / Having reached the bright eighth [tithi] in the month of Bhādrapada,
she should pluck an expanse of dūrvā grass spreading toward the northern direction; / having brought it to the house, she should worship it with fragrances, garlands, and ointments,
and with fruits and roots, O Rāma, avoiding incense and lamps; / and anything cooked on fire should not be offered as food at all.
And food free from cooking by fire should be eaten, O Rāma. / Having worshipped the Fortune of Youth residing in the sprout of dūrvā grass according to rule,
