yā bhuṅkte gorasaprāyaṃ kṛtvā brāhmaṇapūjanam ..
sapta janmāntarāṇyeva saubhāgyaṃ rūpameva ca ..35..
2.7.d:
आर्द्रकेणेक्षुणा चैव तथा कालोद्भवैः फलैः॥
सर्वैश्च विविधैरन्नैर्गन्धैर्नानाविधैस्तथा॥29॥
पानकैश्च तथा हृद्यैः पूजनीयाश्च कृत्तिकाः ॥
सह चन्द्रमसा राम तेन सौभाग्यमश्नुते ॥30 ॥
नारी च रूपलावण्ये धर्मे चाग्र्यां तथा मतिम् ॥
अवैधव्यं च धर्मज्ञ यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥31॥
लवणस्य तुलां कृत्वा महारञ्जनरंजिते ॥ ॥।
वस्त्रे वस्त्रेण तेनाथ सालङ्कारां सितच्छविम् ॥ 32 ॥
कृत्वा पिण्डं हरिद्राक्तं कृत्तिकानां निवेदयेत् ॥
ग्राहयेद्ब्राह्मणं तां च प्राप्ते चन्द्रोदये तथा ॥ 33॥
अनेन कर्मणा नारी सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥
पुरुषोऽप्यथ वै शुद्धो सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥
कृत्तिकाप्रतिपादे तु तासां कृत्वैव पूजनम्॥34॥ ।
या भुङ्क्ते गोरसप्रायं कृत्वा ब्राह्मणपूजनम् ॥
सप्त जन्मान्तराण्येव सौभाग्यं रूपमेव च ॥35॥
2.7.m:
with ginger and sugarcane, as well as seasonal fruits, / with all kinds of diverse foods and various fragrant substances,
and with pleasant refreshing beverages, the Kṛttikās are to be worshipped / together with the moon, O Rāma; through that, one enjoys good fortune.
A woman also gains beauty, charm, and the highest inclination toward dharma, / and freedom from widowhood, O knower of dharma, wherever she is reborn.
Having made a tulā weight of salt upon a cloth dyed with safflower, / and then with that garment, [having formed] an adorned, bright-shining
ball smeared with turmeric, she should offer it to the Kṛttikās, / and then, when the moon has risen, she should cause a brahmin to accept it.
By this rite a woman obtains great good fortune; / a man too, if pure, obtains great good fortune. / Having worshipped them at the time of the moon's entry into Kṛttikā,
she who, having worshipped brahmins, eats food made mostly of milk / [enjoys] good fortune and beauty throughout seven births,

2.7.s:
svarge tu bhogānāpnoti saha bhartrā tu sā śubhā .. .. 36 ..
prāpya pañcadaśīṃ rāma tathā śuklāṃ ca kārtikīm ..
kārtikaṃ kārtikīṃ rāma gṛhabhittau samālikhet .. 37 ..
upadvāraṃ gṛhādbāhyaṃ nānāvarṇaistu varṇakaiḥ ..
gṛhopakaraṇaṃ śaktyā tayoścaivābhito likhet .. 38 ..
pīṭhakhaḍgāsanādyatra śakaṭolūkhalādikam ..
tatastau pūjayennārī nānābhaktiparā śuciḥ .. 39 ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā ..
ikṣuṇekṣuvikārairvā viśeṣeṇa ca pūjayet .. 40 ..
tayostu pūjanaṃ kṛtvā matsyaṃ ca sikatāyutam .. ..
śuktinetraṃ nyasetkṣīre tacca dadyāddvijātaye .. 41 ..
tataśca naktaṃ bhuñjīta tilatailavivarjitam ..
anayoḥ pūjanādrāma gṛhabhaṅgaṃ na cāpnuyāt..42..
pativratā mahābhāga dīrghamāpnoti jīvitam ..
kārtike ca tathā māsi sārdhaṃ candramasā sadā ..43..
2.7.d:
स्वर्गे तु भोगानाप्नोति सह भर्त्रा तु सा शुभा ॥ ॥ 36 ॥
प्राप्य पञ्चदशीं राम तथा शुक्लां च कार्तिकीम् ॥
कार्तिकं कार्तिकीं राम गृहभित्तौ समालिखेत् ॥ 37 ॥
उपद्वारं गृहाद्बाह्यं नानावर्णैस्तु वर्णकैः ॥
गृहोपकरणं शक्त्या तयोश्चैवाभितो लिखेत् ॥ 38 ॥
पीठखड्गासनाद्यत्र शकटोलूखलादिकम् ॥
ततस्तौ पूजयेन्नारी नानाभक्तिपरा शुचिः ॥ 39 ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥
इक्षुणेक्षुविकारैर्वा विशेषेण च पूजयेत् ॥ 40 ॥
तयोस्तु पूजनं कृत्वा मत्स्यं च सिकतायुतम् ॥ ॥
शुक्तिनेत्रं न्यसेत्क्षीरे तच्च दद्याद्द्विजातये ॥ 41 ॥
ततश्च नक्तं भुञ्जीत तिलतैलविवर्जितम् ॥
अनयोः पूजनाद्राम गृहभङ्गं न चाप्नुयात्॥42॥
पतिव्रता महाभाग दीर्घमाप्नोति जीवितम् ॥
कार्तिके च तथा मासि सार्धं चन्द्रमसा सदा ॥43॥
2.7.m:
and that auspicious woman attains pleasures in heaven together with her husband.
When the fifteenth day of the bright half of Kārttika arrives, O Rāma, / she should draw Kārttika and Kārttikī upon the wall of the house,
beside the door, outside the house, with pigments of various colours. / She should also draw around both of them, according to capacity, the household equipment,
wherein are stools, swords, seats, carts, mortars, and the like. / Then, pure and devoted to various acts of devotion, the woman should worship the two
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food; / and she should worship [them] especially with sugarcane or sugarcane products.
Having worshipped the two, she should place a fish, accompanied by sand / and with pearl-oysters for eyes, into milk, and give that to a twice-born.
Then she should eat at night, avoiding sesame and oil. / From the worship of these two, O Rāma, she suffers no ruin of the household;
the devoted wife, O highly fortunate one, attains a long life. / And likewise in the month of Kārttika, always along with the moon,

2.7.s:
rohiṇyāṃ rohiṇīpūjā kartavyā vidhinā dvija ..
sarvairavidhavācihnairlavaṇena ca bhūriṇā .. 44 ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā ..
tathā kuṃkumaraktena śaktyā bhārgava vāsasā .. 45 ..
saubhāgyaṃ paramāpnoti kṛtvaitatparamāṅganā ..
śuklapakṣatrayodaśyāṃ yā ca nārī pativratā .. 46 ..
pūjayetsopavāsā ca kāmadevamatandritā ..
paṭṭavarṇakavinyāsaṃ tasya bhāryā tathā patim .. 47 ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā ..
guḍena madhunā caiva sitayā cārdrakeṇa ca ..48..
lavaṇena rasaiścānyairgandhaiḥ sasyaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak ..
bhakṣyairnāvidhaiścaiva kuṃkumārdreṇa vāsasā ..49..
gandhatoyāmbupūrṇena drumapallavaśālinā ..
pūrṇakumbhena bhavyena mālyakaṇṭhena bhārgava .. 50 ..
2.7.d:
रोहिण्यां रोहिणीपूजा कर्तव्या विधिना द्विज ॥
सर्वैरविधवाचिह्नैर्लवणेन च भूरिणा ॥ 44 ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥
तथा कुंकुमरक्तेन शक्त्या भार्गव वाससा ॥ 45 ॥
सौभाग्यं परमाप्नोति कृत्वैतत्परमाङ्गना ॥
शुक्लपक्षत्रयोदश्यां या च नारी पतिव्रता ॥ 46 ॥
पूजयेत्सोपवासा च कामदेवमतन्द्रिता ॥
पट्टवर्णकविन्यासं तस्य भार्या तथा पतिम् ॥ 47 ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥
गुडेन मधुना चैव सितया चार्द्रकेण च ॥48॥
लवणेन रसैश्चान्यैर्गन्धैः सस्यैः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
भक्ष्यैर्नाविधैश्चैव कुंकुमार्द्रेण वाससा ॥49॥
गन्धतोयाम्बुपूर्णेन द्रुमपल्लवशालिना ॥
पूर्णकुम्भेन भव्येन माल्यकण्ठेन भार्गव ॥ 50 ॥
2.7.m:
worship of Rohiṇī must be performed according to rule upon the asterism of Rohiṇī, O twice-born, / with all the tokens of a non-widow and with abundant salt,
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food, / and according to capacity, O Bhārgava, with a garment dyed red with saffron.
Having performed this, the excellent woman obtains the highest good fortune. / And that devoted wife who, on the thirteenth of the bright fortnight,
fasting and unwearied, worships Kāmadeva, / as well as the painted figures of his wife and her husband,
with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food, / with molasses, honey, white sugar, and ginger,
with salt and other liquids, distinct perfumes and grains, / with diverse kinds of sweetmeats and a garment moistened with saffron,
with an auspicious, full water-pot filled with fragrant water, / adorned with tree shoots, and with a garland around its neck, O Bhārgava—

2.7.s:
kāmadevāya no dadyādyadamlaṃ kiñcideva tu ..
tataśca paścāddhoktavyaṃ sarvamamlavivarjitam .. 51 ..
2.7.d:
कामदेवाय नो दद्याद्यदम्लं किञ्चिदेव तु ॥
ततश्च पश्चाद्धोक्तव्यं सर्वमम्लविवर्जितम् ॥ 51 ॥
2.7.m: she must not offer anything sour to Kāmadeva; / and afterwards, everything [she] eats must be free of sourness.

2.7.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti kāmapūjāvidhāyinī ..
atha cennaiva śaknoti sarvāṃ rāma trayodaśīm .. 52 ..
2.7.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति कामपूजाविधायिनी ॥
अथ चेन्नैव शक्नोति सर्वां राम त्रयोदशीम् ॥ 52 ॥
2.7.m: The woman who performs the worship of Kāma obtains all her desires. / If, however, she is not able [to perform this] on every thirteenth day, O Rāma,

2.7.s:
caitraśuklena sarvāsāṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena caitraśuklatrayodaśīm .. 53 ..
2.7.d:
चैत्रशुक्लेन सर्वासां फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम्॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन चैत्रशुक्लत्रयोदशीम् ॥ 53 ॥
2.7.m: she undoubtedly obtains the fruit of all of them on the bright thirteenth of Caitra; / therefore, with every effort, on the thirteenth of the bright half of Caitra,

2.7.s:
kāmasya pūjā kartavyā sarvakāmapradāyinī ..
kāmadevaṃ samabhyarcya kāryamātmābhipūjanam .. 54 ..
2.7.d:
कामस्य पूजा कर्तव्या सर्वकामप्रदायिनी ॥
कामदेवं समभ्यर्च्य कार्यमात्माभिपूजनम् ॥ 54 ॥
2.7.m: worship of Kāma, bestower of all desires, is to be performed. / Having worshipped Kāmadeva, worship of oneself should be carried out.

2.7.s:
kuṃkumāṅkaistathā vastrairgandhamālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ ..
bhartāraṃ pūjayetpaścānnārī tu kṛtamaṇḍanā .. 55 ..
2.7.d:
कुंकुमाङ्कैस्तथा वस्त्रैर्गन्धमाल्यविभूषणैः ॥
भर्तारं पूजयेत्पश्चान्नारी तु कृतमण्डना ॥ 55 ॥
2.7.m: With garments marked with saffron, and with perfumes, garlands, and ornaments, / the woman, having adorned herself, should then worship her husband

2.7.s:
kukumāṃkena vastreṇa gandhamālyairmanoharaiḥ ..
puruṣo'pi samabhyarcya kāmadevamasaṃśayam .. 56 ..
2.7.d:
कुकुमांकेन वस्त्रेण गन्धमाल्यैर्मनोहरैः ॥
पुरुषोऽपि समभ्यर्च्य कामदेवमसंशयम् ॥ 56 ॥
2.7.m: with a cloth marked with saffron, and with captivating perfumes and garlands. / A man also, having worshipped Kāmadeva, undoubtedly

2.7.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
tathā śuklacaturthīṣu gaurīpūjā sadā bhavet .. 57 ..
2.7.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
तथा शुक्लचतुर्थीषु गौरीपूजा सदा भवेत् ॥ 57 ॥
2.7.m: attains all desires; of this there is no doubt. / Likewise, on the fourth days of the bright fortnight, worship of Gaurī should always be held

2.7.s:
snātābhiḥ sopavāsābhiḥ sūryasyodayanaṃ prati ..
gandhamālyanamaskāradhūpadīpānnasampadā .. 58 ..
2.7.d:
स्नाताभिः सोपवासाभिः सूर्यस्योदयनं प्रति ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥ 58 ॥
2.7.m: by women who have bathed and fasted, at the rising of the sun, / with an abundance of perfume, garlands, salutations, incense, lamps, and food,

2.7.s:
guḍena sitayā cāpi madhunā cārdrakeṇa ca ..
sarvaiścāvidhavācihnairlavaṇena ca bhūriṇā .. 59 ..
2.7.d:
गुडेन सितया चापि मधुना चार्द्रकेण च ॥
सर्वैश्चाविधवाचिह्नैर्लवणेन च भूरिणा ॥ 59 ॥
2.7.m: with molasses, white sugar, honey, and ginger, / with all tokens of a non-widow, and with abundant salt.

2.7.s:
caturthīdvitaye pūjyā sarvaśaktyā viśeṣataḥ ..
āṣāḍhe'pyathavā māsi māghe cāpyathavā dvija .. 60 ..
2.7.d:
चतुर्थीद्वितये पूज्या सर्वशक्त्या विशेषतः ॥
आषाढेऽप्यथवा मासि माघे चाप्यथवा द्विज ॥ 60 ॥
2.7.m: She should be worshipped especially, with all one's power, on the pair of fourth days / in the month of Āṣāḍha or in the month of Māgha, O twice-born.

2.7.s:
caturṇāmapi kuṇḍānāṃ madhye sūryāṃśusevinī ..
āṣāḍhe sopavāsā tu tṛtīyāyāṃ tathā vaset .. 61 ..
2.7.d:
चतुर्णामपि कुण्डानां मध्ये सूर्यांशुसेविनी ॥
आषाढे सोपवासा तु तृतीयायां तथा वसेत् ॥ 61 ॥
2.7.m: Remaining in the midst of four fire pits, receiving the rays of the sun, / fasting in Āṣāḍha, she should stay thus on the third day.

2.7.s:
na tasyā durlabhaṃ loke kiñcidbhavati bhārgava ..
māghe'pyupoṣitā māsi rātryante tuhinotkaraiḥ ..62..
2.7.d:
न तस्या दुर्लभं लोके किञ्चिद्भवति भार्गव ॥
माघेऽप्युपोषिता मासि रात्र्यन्ते तुहिनोत्करैः ॥62॥
2.7.m: Nothing in the world is difficult for her to attain, O Bhārgava. / Fasting also in the month of Māgha, at the end of the night, when by mounds of frost

2.7.s:
śuklīkṛtyākhilānyaṅgānyadhyāste śayanaṃ yayā ..
tataśca śītatoyena paścātsnānaṃ samācaret .. .. 63 ..
2.7.d:
शुक्लीकृत्याखिलान्यङ्गान्यध्यास्ते शयनं यया ॥
ततश्च शीततोयेन पश्चात्स्नानं समाचरेत् ॥ ॥ 63 ॥
2.7.m: all her limbs have been whitened, she who lies upon the ground / should afterwards perform a bath with cold water.

2.7.s:
sāpi kāmānavāpnoti yānrāma manasecchati..
pativratā sadā lolā subhagā rūpasaṃyutā .. 64 ..
2.7.d:
सापि कामानवाप्नोति यान्राम मनसेच्छति॥
पतिव्रता सदा लोला सुभगा रूपसंयुता ॥ 64 ॥
2.7.m: She too obtains the desires that she wishes for in her heart, O Rāma. / Devoted to her husband, ever playful, fortunate, endowed with beauty,

2.7.s:
dharmapriyā ca bhavati gaurīpūjanatatparā ..
āṣāḍhe dāḍimaṃ puṣpaṃ madhau karpāsasambhavam .. 65 ..
2.7.d:
धर्मप्रिया च भवति गौरीपूजनतत्परा ॥
आषाढे दाडिमं पुष्पं मधौ कर्पाससम्भवम् ॥ 65 ॥
2.7.m: and fond of dharma does she become, devoted to the worship of Gaurī. / Having offered a pomegranate flower in Āṣāḍha, and cotton blossoms in springtime,

2.7.s:
nivedya sarvamāryāyai saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute ..
śakrāṇī ca tathā pūjyā māsi bhādrapade bhavet .. .. 66 ..
2.7.d:
निवेद्य सर्वमार्यायै सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥
शक्राणी च तथा पूज्या मासि भाद्रपदे भवेत् ॥ ॥ 66 ॥
2.7.m: all to the Noble Lady, she attains great good fortune. / Likewise, Śakrāṇī should be worshipped in the month of Bhādrapada

2.7.s:
strīṇāṃ gaurīvidhānena sarvakāmapradā hi sā ..
proṣṭhapadasya māsasya caturthyāṃ dvijasattama .. 67 ..
2.7.d:
स्त्रीणां गौरीविधानेन सर्वकामप्रदा हि सा ॥
प्रोष्ठपदस्य मासस्य चतुर्थ्यां द्विजसत्तम ॥ 67 ॥
2.7.m: by women according to the rite for Gaurī, for she bestows all desires. / On the fourth day of the month of Proṣṭhapada, O best of the twice-born,

2.7.s:
śakrāṇīpūjanaṃ kṛtvā nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyate ..
pūjātithiṣu sarvāsu rāma brāhmaṇapūjanam ..68..
2.7.d:
शक्राणीपूजनं कृत्वा नाकपृष्ठे महीयते ॥
पूजातिथिषु सर्वासु राम ब्राह्मणपूजनम् ॥68॥
2.7.m: having worshipped Śakrāṇī, she is glorified on the surface of heaven. / On all days of worship, O Rāma, the worship of brahmins

2.7.s:
kartavyaṃ yacca naivedyaṃ deyaṃ tatsubhagāsu ca ..
anabhyarcya tathā gaurīṃ gaurīdīpaṃ prapaśyati .. .. 69 ..
2.7.d:
कर्तव्यं यच्च नैवेद्यं देयं तत्सुभगासु च ॥
अनभ्यर्च्य तथा गौरीं गौरीदीपं प्रपश्यति ॥ ॥ 69 ॥
2.7.m: must be performed, and whatever is offered as naivedya should be given to fortunate women. / And without having worshipped Gaurī, she who gazes upon the lamp of Gaurī

2.7.s:
daurbhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti varjitaṃ tasya darśanam ..
gaurīpūjanakāmā strī tasminnahani yā dvija .. 70 ..
2.7.d:
दौर्भाग्यं महदाप्नोति वर्जितं तस्य दर्शनम् ॥
गौरीपूजनकामा स्त्री तस्मिन्नहनि या द्विज ॥ 70 ॥
2.7.m:
She incurs great misfortune; gazing upon it is forbidden.
O twice-born, a woman desiring to worship Gaurī on that day

2.7.s:
snānamuṣṇāmbunā kuryātsāpi saubhāgyamaśnute ..
sampūjya vidhinā gaurīṃ yatrayatrābhijāyate .. 71 ..
2.7.d:
स्नानमुष्णाम्बुना कुर्यात्सापि सौभाग्यमश्नुते ॥
सम्पूज्य विधिना गौरीं यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥ 71 ॥
2.7.m:
Should also bathe with hot water; she too attains good fortune.
Having worshipped Gaurī according to rule, wherever she is born,

2.7.s:
rūpalāvaṇyasaubhāgyayuktā bhavati cāpyatha ..
nityaṃ cāvidhavā rāma tathaiva ca pativratā .. 72 ..
2.7.d:
रूपलावण्यसौभाग्ययुक्ता भवति चाप्यथ ॥
नित्यं चाविधवा राम तथैव च पतिव्रता ॥ 72 ॥
2.7.m: She is endowed with beauty, charm, and good fortune, / and is never widowed, O Rāma, and likewise devoted to her husband.

2.7.s:
etāḥ pūjyatamā strīṣu daivatāstāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
ataḥ paraṃ tu yā kuryātsatīmārgavivarjanam .. 73 ..
2.7.d:
एताः पूज्यतमा स्त्रीषु दैवतास्ताः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
अतः परं तु या कुर्यात्सतीमार्गविवर्जनम् ॥ 73 ॥
2.7.m:
These goddesses are proclaimed as the most worthy of worship among women.
Beyond this, however, whatever woman abandons the path of the chaste wife,

2.7.s:
hiṃsātmakamanirdiṣṭamaśuddhaṃ vā dvijottama ..
devatārādhanaṃ sā tu ciraṃ narakamṛcchati .. 74 ..
2.7.d:
हिंसात्मकमनिर्दिष्टमशुद्धं वा द्विजोत्तम ॥
देवताराधनं सा तु चिरं नरकमृच्छति ॥ 74 ॥
2.7.m: And performs worship of deities that is violent, unauthorised, or impure, O best of the twice-born, / goes to hell for a long time.

2.7.s:
tatastu cāpyanāyuṣyaṃ grahabhūtavivardhanam ..
hiṃsātmakā tu yā nārī devatārādhane ratā .. 75 ..
2.7.d:
ततस्तु चाप्यनायुष्यं ग्रहभूतविवर्धनम् ॥
हिंसात्मका तु या नारी देवताराधने रता ॥ 75 ॥
2.7.m:
From that comes shortening of life and an increase of seizing spirits and ghosts.
A woman who is intent on violence in worshipping deities,

2.7.s:
mūlakarmaratā bhartrā sā vivāhyā bhṛgūttama ..
pauṃścalyādapi nārīṇāṃ rāma hiṃsā vivarjitā .. 76 ..
2.7.d:
मूलकर्मरता भर्त्रा सा विवाह्या भृगूत्तम ॥
पौंश्चल्यादपि नारीणां राम हिंसा विवर्जिता ॥ 76 ॥
2.7.m:
And engaged in sorcery against her husband, must be abandoned, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Even more than unchastity, O Rāma, violence is forbidden for women.

2.7.s:
strīsvabhāvaṃ śubhaṃ rāma saumyatvaṃ mārdavaṃ dayā ..
nirdayā rākṣasī rāma piśācī vā dvijottama .. 77 ..
2.7.d:
स्त्रीस्वभावं शुभं राम सौम्यत्वं मार्दवं दया ॥
निर्दया राक्षसी राम पिशाची वा द्विजोत्तम ॥ 77 ॥
2.7.m:
The auspicious natural disposition of women, O Rāma, is gentleness, softness, and compassion.
A merciless woman, O Rāma, is a rākṣasī or a piśācī, O best of the twice-born.

2.7.s:
athavā sarvamutsṛjya patipūjanatatparā ..
keśavārādhanaṃ kuryācchriyaśca puruṣarṣabha .. 78 ..
2.7.d:
अथवा सर्वमुत्सृज्य पतिपूजनतत्परा ॥
केशवाराधनं कुर्याच्छ्रियश्च पुरुषर्षभ ॥ 78 ॥
2.7.m: Or else, relinquishing everything and devoted to serving her husband, / she should perform the worship of Keśava and Śrī, O bull among men.

2.7.s:
tenaiva sarvamāpnoti yatkiñcitparamṛcchati ..
aphalaṃ sarvameva syādbhartranujñāṃ vinā kṛtam ..79..
2.7.d:
तेनैव सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किञ्चित्परमृच्छति ॥
अफलं सर्वमेव स्याद्भर्त्रनुज्ञां विना कृतम् ॥79॥
2.7.m:
Through that alone she attains everything, whatever supreme [goal] she seeks.
All [other rites] performed without the husband's permission are fruitless.

2.7.s:
keśavārādhanaṃ rāma tathāpi saphalaṃ striyaḥ ..
sarvabhūtāni govindo bhartā nānyastu yoṣitaḥ ..
bhartranujñāṃ vinā tasmāttataḥ pūjā vidhīyate .. 80 ..
2.7.d:
केशवाराधनं राम तथापि सफलं स्त्रियः ॥
सर्वभूतानि गोविन्दो भर्ता नान्यस्तु योषितः ॥
भर्त्रनुज्ञां विना तस्मात्ततः पूजा विधीयते ॥ 80 ॥

2.7.s:
nārāyaṇaḥ pūjyatamo hi loke nārāyaṇaḥ sarvagataḥ pradhānaḥ ..
nārāyaṇārādhanatatparā strī kāmānavāpnoti na saṃśayo'tra .. 81 ..
2.7.d:
नारायणः पूज्यतमो हि लोके नारायणः सर्वगतः प्रधानः ॥
नारायणाराधनतत्परा स्त्री कामानवाप्नोति न संशयोऽत्र ॥ 81 ॥
2.7.m:
Nārāyaṇa is indeed the most worthy of worship in the world; Nārāyaṇa is omnipresent and supreme.
A woman intent on the worship of Nārāyaṇa attains her desires; there is no doubt in this.

2.8.s:
2.36
.. puṣkara uvāca ..
vailomyaṃ dharmarājo'pi nācaratyatha yoṣitām ..
pativratānāṃ dharmajña pūjyāstasyāpi tāssadā .. 1 ..
2.8.d:
2.36
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
वैलोम्यं धर्मराजोऽपि नाचरत्यथ योषिताम् ॥
पतिव्रतानां धर्मज्ञ पूज्यास्तस्यापि तास्सदा ॥ 1 ॥
2.8.m:
2.36
Puṣkara said:
Even Dharmarāja does not act contrary to women [who are]
Devoted to their husbands, O knower of dharma; to him too they are ever worthy of reverence.

2.8.s:
atra te varṇayiṣyāmi kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm ..
yathā vimokṣito bhartā mṛtyupāśāvṛtaḥ striyā ..2 ..
2.8.d:
अत्र ते वर्णयिष्यामि कथां पापप्रणाशिनीम् ॥
यथा विमोक्षितो भर्ता मृत्युपाशावृतः स्त्रिया ॥2 ॥
2.8.m: Here I will relate to you a story that destroys sin, / how a husband entangled in the noose of death was released by a woman.

2.8.s:
madreṣu śākale rājā babhūvā'śvapatiḥ purā ..
aputrastapyamāno'sau putrārthe sarvakāmadam .. 3 ..
2.8.d:
मद्रेषु शाकले राजा बभूवाऽश्वपतिः पुरा ॥
अपुत्रस्तप्यमानोऽसौ पुत्रार्थे सर्वकामदम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.8.m:
Formerly, in the [country of the] Madras, in Śākala, there was a king named Aśvapati.
Being sonless and distressed, for the sake of a son he performed [a rite] that grants all desires:

2.8.s:
sāvitryāḥ kārayāmāsa lakṣahomaṃ dvijottamaiḥ ..
siddhārthakairhūyamānā sāvitrī pratyahaṃ dvija .. 4 ..
2.8.d:
सावित्र्याः कारयामास लक्षहोमं द्विजोत्तमैः ॥
सिद्धार्थकैर्हूयमाना सावित्री प्रत्यहं द्विज ॥ 4 ॥
2.8.m:
He caused a lakṣahoma to Sāvitrī to be performed by the best of the twice-born.
Invoked daily with oblations of mustard seeds, O twice-born,

2.8.s:
śatasaṃkhyaiścaturthyāṃ tu māsāddaśadine gate ..
kāle tu darśayāmāsa svāṃ tanuṃ manujeśvare .. 5 ..
2.8.d:
शतसंख्यैश्चतुर्थ्यां तु मासाद्दशदिने गते ॥
काले तु दर्शयामास स्वां तनुं मनुजेश्वरे ॥ 5 ॥
2.8.m: Numbered in hundreds on the fourth [tithi], when the tenth day of the month had passed, / Sāvitrī revealed her form in time to the ruler of men.

2.8.s:
sāvitryuvāca ..
rājanbhakto'si me nityaṃ prāpsyase tanayāṃ śubhām ..
maddattāṃ yatprasādācca putrānprāpsyasi śobhanān .. 6 ..
2.8.d:
सावित्र्युवाच ॥
राजन्भक्तोऽसि मे नित्यं प्राप्स्यसे तनयां शुभाम् ॥
मद्दत्तां यत्प्रसादाच्च पुत्रान्प्राप्स्यसि शोभनान् ॥ 6 ॥
2.8.m:
Sāvitrī said:
O king, you are ever devoted to me; you shall obtain an auspicious daughter / given by me, and through her grace you will obtain splendid sons.

2.8.s:
puṣkara uvāca .. etāvaduktvā sā rājñaḥ praṇatasyaiva bhārgava ..
jagāmādarśanaṃ devī khe yathā rāma cañcalā .. 7 ..
2.8.d:
पुष्कर उवाच ॥ एतावदुक्त्वा सा राज्ञः प्रणतस्यैव भार्गव ॥
जगामादर्शनं देवी खे यथा राम चञ्चला ॥ 7 ॥
2.8.m:
Puṣkara said:
Having spoken thus to the king while he was bowing down, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / the goddess vanished from sight into the sky, O Rāma, like lightning.

2.8.s:
mālavyā nāma tasyāsti rājñaḥ patnī pativratā ..
suṣāva tanayāṃ kāle sāvitrīmeva rūpataḥ .. 8 ..
2.8.d:
मालव्या नाम तस्यास्ति राज्ञः पत्नी पतिव्रता ॥
सुषाव तनयां काले सावित्रीमेव रूपतः ॥ 8 ॥
2.8.m:
That king had a devoted wife named Mālavyā;
in due time she gave birth to a daughter who was the very image of Sāvitrī in form.

2.8.s:
sāvitryā hutayā dattā tadrūpasadṛśā tataḥ ..
sāvitryeva bhavedeṣā jagāda nṛpatirdvijān .. ..
kālena yauvanaṃ prāptāṃ dadau satyavate pitā ..
nāradastu tataḥ prāha rājānaṃ dīptatejasam .. 10 ..
2.8.d:
सावित्र्या हुतया दत्ता तद्रूपसदृशा ततः ॥
सावित्र्येव भवेदेषा जगाद नृपतिर्द्विजान् ॥ ॥
कालेन यौवनं प्राप्तां ददौ सत्यवते पिता ॥
नारदस्तु ततः प्राह राजानं दीप्ततेजसम् ॥ 10 ॥
2.8.m:
Given by Sāvitrī who had been offered oblations, and resembling her in form,
'She must indeed be Sāvitrī,' the king said to the twice-born.
When in time she attained youth, her father gave her to Satyavat.
Then Nārada said to the king of blazing splendour:

2.8.s:
kṣīṇāyureṣa varṣeṇa bhaviṣyati nṛpātmajaḥ ..
pradīyate sakṛtkanyā cintayitvā narādhipaḥ .. 11 ..
2.8.d:
क्षीणायुरेष वर्षेण भविष्यति नृपात्मजः ॥
प्रदीयते सकृत्कन्या चिन्तयित्वा नराधिपः ॥ 11 ॥
2.8.m:
'In a year this prince will have his life exhausted.'
Reflecting that 'a maiden is given away once,' the lord of men

2.8.s:
tathāpi pradadau kanyāṃ dyumatsenātmaje śubhāma ..
sāvitryapi ca bhartāramāsādya nṛpanandanam .. 12 ..
2.8.d:
तथापि प्रददौ कन्यां द्युमत्सेनात्मजे शुभाम ॥
सावित्र्यपि च भर्तारमासाद्य नृपनन्दनम् ॥ 12 ॥
2.8.m:
Nevertheless bestowed the auspicious maiden upon the son of Dyumatsena.
Sāvitrī too, having obtained the prince as her husband,

2.8.s:
nāradasya tu vākyena dūyamānena cetasā ..
śuśrūṣāṃ paramāṃ cakre bhartṛśvaśurayorvane .. 13 ..
2.8.d:
नारदस्य तु वाक्येन दूयमानेन चेतसा ॥
शुश्रूषां परमां चक्रे भर्तृश्वशुरयोर्वने ॥ 13 ॥
2.8.m: With her mind distressed by Nārada's words, / performed supreme service in the forest to her husband and father-in-law.

2.8.s:
rājyabhraṣṭassabhāryastu naṣṭacakṣurnarādhipaḥ ..
tutoṣa tāṃ samāsādya rājaputrīṃ tadā snuṣām .. 14 ..
2.8.d:
राज्यभ्रष्टस्सभार्यस्तु नष्टचक्षुर्नराधिपः ॥
तुतोष तां समासाद्य राजपुत्रीं तदा स्नुषाम् ॥ 14 ॥
2.8.m: Deprived of his kingdom, with his wife, and having lost his eyesight, the king / was delighted upon receiving that princess as a daughter-in-law.

2.8.s:
caturthe'hani martavyaṃ yadā satyavatā dvija ..
śvaśureṇābhyanujñātā tadā rājñā tu sā snuṣā .. 15 ..
2.8.d:
चतुर्थेऽहनि मर्तव्यं यदा सत्यवता द्विज ॥
श्वशुरेणाभ्यनुज्ञाता तदा राज्ञा तु सा स्नुषा ॥ 15 ॥
2.8.m: When on the fourth day Satyavat was destined to die, O twice-born, / then that daughter-in-law, permitted by her father-in-law, the king,

2.8.s:
cakre trirātraṃ dharmajña prāpte tasmiṃstadā dine ..
cārupuṣpaphalāhāraṃ satyavānprayayau vanam .. 16 ..
2.8.d:
चक्रे त्रिरात्रं धर्मज्ञ प्राप्ते तस्मिंस्तदा दिने ॥
चारुपुष्पफलाहारं सत्यवान्प्रययौ वनम् ॥ 16 ॥
2.8.m: Undertook a three-night fast, O knower of dharma. When that day arrived, / Satyavat went to the forest to gather fine flowers and fruits.

2.8.s:
śvaśureṇābhyanujñātā yācanābhaṅgabhīruṇā ..
sāvitryapi jagāmāśu saha bhartrā mahadvanam .. 17 ..
2.8.d:
श्वशुरेणाभ्यनुज्ञाता याचनाभङ्गभीरुणा ॥
सावित्र्यपि जगामाशु सह भर्त्रा महद्वनम् ॥ 17 ॥
2.8.m: Permitted by her father-in-law, who was afraid of refusing her request, / Sāvitrī also went quickly with her husband to the great forest.

2.8.s:
cetasā dūyamānena gūhamānā ca tadbhayam ..
vane papraccha bhartāraṃ drumāṃśca samṛgāṃstathā .. 18 ..
2.8.d:
चेतसा दूयमानेन गूहमाना च तद्भयम् ॥
वने पप्रच्छ भर्तारं द्रुमांश्च समृगांस्तथा ॥ 18 ॥
2.8.m: With a mind that was grieving, yet concealing that fear, / she asked her husband in the forest about the trees and also about the wild beasts.

2.8.s:
āśvāsayāmāsa sa rājaputrīṃ klāntāṃ vane padmapalāśanetrām ..
sandarśanenātha mṛgadvijānāṃ tathā drumāṇāṃ vipine nṛvīraḥ.. 19 .. ..
2.37
.. satyavānuvāca .. ..
vane'sminṣaṭpadākīrṇaṃ sahakāraṃ manoharam ..
śrotraghrāṇamukhaṃ paśya vasante rativardhanam .. 1 ..
vane sapuṣpaṃ dṛṣṭvaiṣā raktā ślokaṃ manoharam ..
hasatīva manaḥ serṣyaṃ tvāmivāyatalocane .. 2 ..
dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇenaitāṃ paśya ramyāṃ vanasthalīm ..
puṣpitaiḥ kiṃśukairyuktāṃ jvalitāmiva saprabhaiḥ .. 3 ..
sugandhikusumāmodī vanarājivinirgataḥ. .
karoti vāyurdākṣiṇyādāvayoḥ klamanāśanam .. 4 ..
apyutpalaviśālākṣi karṇikāraiḥ supuṣpitaiḥ ..
kāñcanairiva bhātyeṣā vanarājī manoharā .. 5 ..
atimuktalatājālaruddhamārgavanasthalīḥ ..
paśyoccaiścārusarvāṅgi kusumotkara bhūṣaṇā .. 6 ..
2.8.d:
आश्वासयामास स राजपुत्रीं क्लान्तां वने पद्मपलाशनेत्राम् ॥
सन्दर्शनेनाथ मृगद्विजानां तथा द्रुमाणां विपिने नृवीरः॥ 19 ॥ ॥
2.37
॥ सत्यवानुवाच ॥ ॥
वनेऽस्मिन्षट्पदाकीर्णं सहकारं मनोहरम् ॥
श्रोत्रघ्राणमुखं पश्य वसन्ते रतिवर्धनम् ॥ 1 ॥
वने सपुष्पं दृष्ट्वैषा रक्ता श्लोकं मनोहरम् ॥
हसतीव मनः सेर्ष्यं त्वामिवायतलोचने ॥ 2 ॥
दक्षिणे दक्षिणेनैतां पश्य रम्यां वनस्थलीम् ॥
पुष्पितैः किंशुकैर्युक्तां ज्वलितामिव सप्रभैः ॥ 3 ॥
सुगन्धिकुसुमामोदी वनराजिविनिर्गतः॥
करोति वायुर्दाक्षिण्यादावयोः क्लमनाशनम् ॥ 4 ॥
अप्युत्पलविशालाक्षि कर्णिकारैः सुपुष्पितैः ॥
काञ्चनैरिव भात्येषा वनराजी मनोहरा ॥ 5 ॥
अतिमुक्तलताजालरुद्धमार्गवनस्थलीः ॥
पश्योच्चैश्चारुसर्वाङ्गि कुसुमोत्कर भूषणा ॥ 6 ॥
2.8.m:
The heroic man consoled the exhausted princess, whose eyes were like lotus petals, in the forest, / by showing her the deer and birds and also the trees in the wilderness.
2.37
Satyavat said:
Behold in this forest the lovely mango tree, swarming with six-legged bees, / delightful to the ears, nose, and mouth, increasing passionate delight in springtime.
Having seen it in bloom in the forest, this red [creeper], charming as a verse, / seems to mock with envy the mind, like you, O wide-eyed lady.
Behold to the south this delightful woodland tract to the right, / covered with blossoming kiṃśuka trees, blazing, as it were, with brilliance.
Carrying the fragrance of sweetly scented flowers, issued from the line of the forest, / the southern wind courteously dispels the fatigue of us both.
O lady with eyes broad as blue lotuses, with well-blossomed karṇikāra trees, / this enchanting woodland line shines as if made of gold.
Behold on high the forest tracts whose paths are blocked by masses of atimukta creepers, / O lady of lovely limbs, adorned with heaps of flowers.

2.8.s:
madhumattālijhāṅkāravyājena varavarṇini ..
cāpayaṣṭiṃ karotīva kāmaḥ pānthajighāṃsayā .. 7 ..
phullacaṃpakasadvaktrā puṃskokilavinādinī ..
vibhāti cārutilakā tvamivaiṣā vanasthalī .. 8 ..
kokilaścūtaśikhare mañjarīreṇupiñjaraḥ ..
gaditairvyaktatāmeti kulīnaśceṣṭitairiva .. 9 ..
puṣpareṇvanuliptāṅgaḥ priyāmanusaranvane ..
kusumātkusumaṃ yāti kūjankāmī śilīmukhaḥ .. 10 ..
mañjarīṃ sahakārasya kāntācañcvagrakhaṇḍitām ..
svādayatyatipuṣpe'pi puṃskokilayuvā drume .. 11 ..
kākaḥ prasūtāṃ vṛkṣāgre sāmiṣāgreṇa cañcunā ..
kākīṃ sampāyayatyeṣa pakṣācchādita putrakām .. 12 ..
bhūbhāgaṃ nimnamāsādya dayitāsahito yuvā ..
nāhāramapi cādatte kāmī kāmaṃ kapiñjalaḥ .. 13 ..
kalaviṅkastu virutaiḥ sapriyo viṭape sthitaḥ ..
muhurmuhurviśālākṣi utkaṇṭhayati kāminaḥ ..14 ..
2.8.d:
मधुमत्तालिझाङ्कारव्याजेन वरवर्णिनि ॥
चापयष्टिं करोतीव कामः पान्थजिघांसया ॥ 7 ॥
फुल्लचंपकसद्वक्त्रा पुंस्कोकिलविनादिनी ॥
विभाति चारुतिलका त्वमिवैषा वनस्थली ॥ 8 ॥
कोकिलश्चूतशिखरे मञ्जरीरेणुपिञ्जरः ॥
गदितैर्व्यक्ततामेति कुलीनश्चेष्टितैरिव ॥ 9 ॥
पुष्परेण्वनुलिप्ताङ्गः प्रियामनुसरन्वने ॥
कुसुमात्कुसुमं याति कूजन्कामी शिलीमुखः ॥ 10 ॥
मञ्जरीं सहकारस्य कान्ताचञ्च्वग्रखण्डिताम् ॥
स्वादयत्यतिपुष्पेऽपि पुंस्कोकिलयुवा द्रुमे ॥ 11 ॥
काकः प्रसूतां वृक्षाग्रे सामिषाग्रेण चञ्चुना ॥
काकीं सम्पाययत्येष पक्षाच्छादित पुत्रकाम् ॥ 12 ॥
भूभागं निम्नमासाद्य दयितासहितो युवा ॥
नाहारमपि चादत्ते कामी कामं कपिञ्जलः ॥ 13 ॥
कलविङ्कस्तु विरुतैः सप्रियो विटपे स्थितः ॥
मुहुर्मुहुर्विशालाक्षि उत्कण्ठयति कामिनः ॥14 ॥
2.8.m:
O woman of excellent complexion, under the guise of the humming of bees intoxicated with spring, / Love seems to string his bow-shaft with the desire to slay travellers.
With its fair face of open campaka blossoms, resounding with male cuckoos, / this woodland shines with lovely tilaka trees, just like you.
The cuckoo atop the mango branch, yellowed with pollen from flower sprays, / reveals its nature by its calls, just as a noble person does by deeds.
Its body smeared with flower pollen, following its beloved in the forest, / buzzing, the lustful bee goes from flower to flower.
The young male cuckoo savours a mango blossom, / broken by the tip of his beloved's beak, even on a tree heavy with flowers.
At the top of the tree, the crow feeds with a beak tipped with meat / the female crow who has laid eggs and covers her nestlings with her wings.
Having reached a low spot of ground together with his mate, / the impassioned young francolin, filled with longing, takes no food at all.
Perched on a branch with his beloved, the sparrow, / with his chirping, O wide-eyed one, repeatedly fills lovers with yearning.

2.8.s:
kṣudraśākhāṃ samārūḍhaḥ śuko'yaṃ kāntayā saha ..
bhāreṇa namayañśākhāṃ karoti saphalāmiva .. 15 ..
vanebhapiśitāsvādatṛpto nidrāmupāgataḥ ..
śete siṃhayuvā kāntācaraṇāvaraṇānanaḥ .. 16 ..
vyāghrayormidhunaṃ paśya śailakandara saṃsthitam ..
yayornetraprabhālokairguhā bhinneva lakṣyate .. 17 ..
aya dvīpī priyāṃ leḍhi jihvāgreṇa punaḥpunaḥ ..
prītimāyāti mahatīṃ lihyamānaśca kāntyā .. 18 ..
utsaṅgakṛtamūrdhānaṃ nidrāpahṛtacetasam ..
jantūddharaṇataḥ kāntaṃ sukhayatyeva vānarī .. 19 ..
2.8.d:
क्षुद्रशाखां समारूढः शुकोऽयं कान्तया सह ॥
भारेण नमयञ्शाखां करोति सफलामिव ॥ 15 ॥
वनेभपिशितास्वादतृप्तो निद्रामुपागतः ॥
शेते सिंहयुवा कान्ताचरणावरणाननः ॥ 16 ॥
व्याघ्रयोर्मिधुनं पश्य शैलकन्दर संस्थितम् ॥
ययोर्नेत्रप्रभालोकैर्गुहा भिन्नेव लक्ष्यते ॥ 17 ॥
अय द्वीपी प्रियां लेढि जिह्वाग्रेण पुनःपुनः ॥
प्रीतिमायाति महतीं लिह्यमानश्च कान्त्या ॥ 18 ॥
उत्सङ्गकृतमूर्धानं निद्रापहृतचेतसम् ॥
जन्तूद्धरणतः कान्तं सुखयत्येव वानरी ॥ 19 ॥
2.8.m:
Mounted on a small bough together with his mate, / this parrot, bending the branch with his weight, makes it seem laden with fruit.
Satiated from savouring the flesh of a wild elephant and overtaken by sleep, / the young lion lies, his face shaded by his beloved's paws.
Behold the pair of tigers dwelling in the mountain cave, / by the blazing light of whose eyes the cave appears split open.
This leopard repeatedly licks his beloved with the tip of his tongue, / and being licked by his lovely mate, he feels great pleasure.
Resting his head in her lap, his consciousness stolen by sleep, / the female monkey delights her lover just by picking out vermin.

2.8.s:
bhūmau nipatitā kāntaṃ mārjārī darśitodarā ..
nakhairdantaistudatyeṣā na ca pīḍayate tathā .. 20 ..
2.8.d:
भूमौ निपतिता कान्तं मार्जारी दर्शितोदरा ॥
नखैर्दन्तैस्तुदत्येषा न च पीडयते तथा ॥ 20 ॥
2.8.m: Fallen on the ground, exposing her belly to her beloved, / this female cat pricks him with claws and teeth, yet does not hurt him.

2.8.s:
śaśakaḥ śaśikā cobhe saṃsupte pīḍite ime ..
sam̐llīnagātracaraṇe karṇairvyaktimupāgate .. 21 ..
2.8.d:
शशकः शशिका चोभे संसुप्ते पीडिते इमे ॥
सम्̐ल्लीनगात्रचरणे कर्णैर्व्यक्तिमुपागते ॥ 21 ॥
2.8.m: The male hare and female hare, pressed together, are both fast asleep, / their limbs and paws tucked in, made visible only by their ears.

2.8.s:
snātaṃ sarasi padmāḍhye vāraṇaṃ madamantharam ..
sambhāvayati tanvaṅgi mṛṇālaśakalairvaśā .. 22 ..
2.8.d:
स्नातं सरसि पद्माढ्ये वारणं मदमन्थरम् ॥
सम्भावयति तन्वङ्गि मृणालशकलैर्वशा ॥ 22 ॥
2.8.m: Having bathed in a lotus-rich lake, the elephant, sluggish with rut, / is honoured by the female elephant, O slender-limbed one, with pieces of lotus stalks.

2.8.s:
kāntapotrasamutkhātaiḥ kāntā mārgānusāriṇī ..
karoti kavalaṃ mustairvarāhī potakānane .. 23 ..
2.8.d:
कान्तपोत्रसमुत्खातैः कान्ता मार्गानुसारिणी ॥
करोति कवलं मुस्तैर्वराही पोतकानने ॥ 23 ॥
2.8.m: Following the tracks of her beloved, the sow in the forest of saplings / makes a mouthful of nut-grass uprooted by the snout of her mate.

2.8.s:
dṛḍhāṅgasandhirmahiṣaḥ kardamārdratanurvane ..
anuvrajati dhāvantīṃ priyāṃ baddhacatuṣkakaḥ ..24..
2.8.d:
दृढाङ्गसन्धिर्महिषः कर्दमार्द्रतनुर्वने ॥
अनुव्रजति धावन्तीं प्रियां बद्धचतुष्ककः ॥24॥
2.8.m: Firm-jointed of limb, his body damp with mud in the forest, / the buffalo gallops in rhythm behind his running mate.

2.8.s:
paśya cārvaṅgi sāraṅgaḥ tvatkaṭākṣanibhaṃ vane ..
sabhāryāṃ māṃ tu paśyantaṃ kautūhalasamanvitam .. 25 ..
2.8.d:
पश्य चार्वङ्गि सारङ्गः त्वत्कटाक्षनिभं वने ॥
सभार्यां मां तु पश्यन्तं कौतूहलसमन्वितम् ॥ 25 ॥
2.8.m: Behold, O fair-limbed one, the deer in the forest, like a sidelong glance from you, / gazing filled with curiosity at me accompanied by my wife.

2.8.s:
paśya paścimapādena rohī kaṇḍūyate mukham ..
snehārdrabhāvaḥ kaṣati bhartā śṛṅgāgrakoṭinā .. 26 ..
2.8.d:
पश्य पश्चिमपादेन रोही कण्डूयते मुखम् ॥
स्नेहार्द्रभावः कषति भर्ता शृङ्गाग्रकोटिना ॥ 26 ॥
2.8.m: Look, with her hind leg the doe scratches her face, / and her mate, feeling moist with tenderness, rubs it with the very tip of his horn.

2.8.s:
dāḍime camarīṃ paśya sitavālāmagacchatīm ..
anvāste camaraḥ kāmī vīkṣate māṃ ca garvitaḥ .. .. 27 ..
2.8.d:
दाडिमे चमरीं पश्य सितवालामगच्छतीम् ॥
अन्वास्ते चमरः कामी वीक्षते मां च गर्वितः ॥ ॥ 27 ॥
2.8.m: Look at the yak cow with white hair moving toward the pomegranate tree; / the lustful yak bull follows her and gazes haughtily at me.

2.8.s:
ātape gavayaḥ paśya niviṣṭo bhāryayā saha ..
romanthamāsye kurvāṇaḥ kākaṃ kakudi dhārayan .. 28 ..
2.8.d:
आतपे गवयः पश्य निविष्टो भार्यया सह ॥
रोमन्थमास्ये कुर्वाणः काकं ककुदि धारयन् ॥ 28 ॥
2.8.m: Behold the gayal seated in the sunlight with his mate, / chewing the cud in his mouth, bearing a crow upon his hump.

2.8.s:
paśyājaṃ bhāryayā sārdhaṃ nyastāgracaraṇadvayam ..
vipule badarīskandhe tacchadagrāsakāmyayā .. 29 ..
2.8.d:
पश्याजं भार्यया सार्धं न्यस्ताग्रचरणद्वयम् ॥
विपुले बदरीस्कन्धे तच्छदग्रासकाम्यया ॥ 29 ॥
2.8.m: Look at the wild goat along with his mate, having placed both forelegs / on the broad trunk of the jujube tree in a desire to chew its leaves.

2.8.s:
haṃsaṃ sabhāryaṃ sarasi vicarantaṃ sunirmale ..
suśuklasyendubimbasya paśyainaṃ sadṛśa śriyam .. 30 ..
2.8.d:
हंसं सभार्यं सरसि विचरन्तं सुनिर्मले ॥
सुशुक्लस्येन्दुबिम्बस्य पश्यैनं सदृश श्रियम् ॥ 30 ॥
2.8.m: Behold this swan roaming with his mate in the crystal-clear lake, / resembling the splendour of the purely white orb of the moon.

2.8.s:
sabhāryaścakravāko'yaṃ kamalākaramadhyagaḥ ..
karoti padminīṃ kāntāṃ sapuṣpāmiva sundari .. 31 ..
2.8.d:
सभार्यश्चक्रवाकोऽयं कमलाकरमध्यगः ॥
करोति पद्मिनीं कान्तां सपुष्पामिव सुन्दरि ॥ 31 ॥
2.8.m: This cakravāka bird with his mate, dwelling amid the lotus pool, / makes his beloved lotus-bed appear full of blossoms, O beautiful one.

2.8.s:
mayā phaloccayaḥ subhru tvayā puṣpoccayaḥ kṛtaḥ ..
indhanaṃ na kṛtaṃ kiñcittatkariṣyāmi sāṃpratam .. 32 ..
2.8.d:
मया फलोच्चयः सुभ्रु त्वया पुष्पोच्चयः कृतः ॥
इन्धनं न कृतं किञ्चित्तत्करिष्यामि सांप्रतम् ॥ 32 ॥
2.8.m: A heap of fruits has been gathered by me, O fair-browed one, and a heap of flowers by you; / no firewood has been collected, so I will do that now.

2.8.s:
tvamasya sarasastīre drumacchāyāmupāśritā ..
kṣaṇamātraṃ pratīkṣasva viśramasva ca bhāmini .. 33 ..
2.8.d:
त्वमस्य सरसस्तीरे द्रुमच्छायामुपाश्रिता ॥
क्षणमात्रं प्रतीक्षस्व विश्रमस्व च भामिनि ॥ 33 ॥
2.8.m: Taking shelter under the shade of a tree on the bank of this lake, / wait for just a moment, and rest, O lovely lady.

2.8.s:
.. sāvitryuvāca .. ..
evametatkariṣyāmi mama dṛṣṭipathāttvayā ..
dūre kānta na gantavyaṃ bibhemi gahane vane .. 34 ..
2.8.d:
॥ सावित्र्युवाच ॥ ॥
एवमेतत्करिष्यामि मम दृष्टिपथात्त्वया ॥
दूरे कान्त न गन्तव्यं बिभेमि गहने वने ॥ 34 ॥
2.8.m:
Sāvitrī said:
I will do so, but you must not go far / out of my sight, my beloved; I am afraid in the dense forest.

2.8.s:
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
tasya pātayataḥ kāṣṭhaṃ jajñe śirasi vedanā ..
sa vedanārttaḥ saṅgamya bhāryāṃ vacanamabravīt .. 35 ..
2.8.d:
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
तस्य पातयतः काष्ठं जज्ञे शिरसि वेदना ॥
स वेदनार्त्तः सङ्गम्य भार्यां वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 35 ॥
2.8.m:
Puṣkara said:
As he was felling wood, a pain arose in his head; / afflicted by the pain, he approached his wife and spoke these words:

2.8.s:
.. satyavānuvāca .. ..
āyāsena mamānena jātā śirasi vedanā ..
tamaśca praviśāmīva na ca jānāmi kiñcana .. 36 ..
2.8.d:
॥ सत्यवानुवाच ॥ ॥
आयासेन ममानेन जाता शिरसि वेदना ॥
तमश्च प्रविशामीव न च जानामि किञ्चन ॥ 36 ॥
2.8.m:
Satyavān said:
From this exertion, a pain has arisen in my head; / I seem to be entering darkness, and I know nothing at all.

2.8.s:
tvadutsaṅge śiraḥ kṛtvā nidropahatalocanaḥ ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
tadutsaṅge śiraḥ kṛtvā suṣvāpa gatacetanaḥ .. 37 ..
2.8.d:
त्वदुत्सङ्गे शिरः कृत्वा निद्रोपहतलोचनः ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
तदुत्सङ्गे शिरः कृत्वा सुष्वाप गतचेतनः ॥ 37 ॥
2.8.m:
Having placed my head in your lap, my eyes overwhelmed by sleep—
Puṣkara said:
Placing his head in her lap, he fell asleep, bereft of consciousness.

2.8.s:
pativratā mahābhāgā tatassā rājakanyakā ..
dadarśa dharmarājaṃ tu svayaṃ taṃ deśamāgatam . 38..
2.8.d:
पतिव्रता महाभागा ततस्सा राजकन्यका ॥
ददर्श धर्मराजं तु स्वयं तं देशमागतम् । 38॥
2.8.m: Then that princess, the fortunate woman devoted to her husband, / saw the King of Dharma himself arrived at that place.

2.8.s:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ pītāmbaradharaṃ prabhum ..
vidyullatānibaddhāṅgaṃ satoyamiva toyadam .. 39 ..
2.8.d:
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामं पीताम्बरधरं प्रभुम् ॥
विद्युल्लतानिबद्धाङ्गं सतोयमिव तोयदम् ॥ 39 ॥
2.8.m: The lord was dark as the petal of a blue lotus, wearing yellow garments, / his body bound with lightning flashes, like a cloud bearing water,

2.8.s:
kirīṭenārkavarṇena kuṇḍalābhyāṃ virājitam ..
hārabhārārpitoraskaṃ tathāṅgadavibhūṣitam .. 40 ..
2.8.d:
किरीटेनार्कवर्णेन कुण्डलाभ्यां विराजितम् ॥
हारभारार्पितोरस्कं तथाङ्गदविभूषितम् ॥ 40 ॥
2.8.m: resplendent with a crown coloured like the sun and with two earrings, / his chest adorned with the weight of necklaces, and similarly decorated with armlets,

2.8.s:
tathānugamyamānaṃ ca kālena saha mṛtyunā ..
sa tu saṃprāpya taṃ deśaṃ dehātsatyavatastadā .. 41 ..
2.8.d:
तथानुगम्यमानं च कालेन सह मृत्युना ॥
स तु संप्राप्य तं देशं देहात्सत्यवतस्तदा ॥ 41 ॥
2.8.m:
and likewise followed by Time together with Death.
Arriving at that place then, from the body of Satyavān,

2.8.s:
aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ puruṣaṃ pāśabaddhaṃ vaśaṅgatam ..
ākṛṣya dakṣiṇāmāśāṃ prayayau satvaraṃ tadā .. 42 ..
2.8.d:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रं पुरुषं पाशबद्धं वशङ्गतम् ॥
आकृष्य दक्षिणामाशां प्रययौ सत्वरं तदा ॥ 42 ॥
2.8.m: having pulled out the Person the size of a thumb, bound with a noose and brought under control, / he then quickly departed toward the southern quarter.

2.8.s:
sāvitryapi varārohā tyaktvā taṃ gatajīvitam ..
anuvavrāja gacchantaṃ dharmarājamatandritā .. 43 ..
2.8.d:
सावित्र्यपि वरारोहा त्यक्त्वा तं गतजीवितम् ॥
अनुवव्राज गच्छन्तं धर्मराजमतन्द्रिता ॥ 43 ॥
2.8.m: Sāvitrī too, of beautiful hips, leaving behind him who had departed this life, / unweariedly followed behind the departing King of Dharma.

2.8.s:
tāmuvāca yamo gaccha yathāgatamanindite ..
aurdhvadaihikakāryeṣu yuktā bhartuḥ samācara ..44 ..
2.8.d:
तामुवाच यमो गच्छ यथागतमनिन्दिते ॥
और्ध्वदैहिककार्येषु युक्ता भर्तुः समाचर ॥44 ॥
2.8.m: Yama said to her: Go back the way you came, blameless lady; / intent on the funeral rites of your husband, perform them.

2.8.s:
nānugantumasau śakyastvayā lokāntaraṃ gataḥ ..
pativratāsi tena tvaṃ muhūrtamanupaśyasi .. ..45 ..
2.8.d:
नानुगन्तुमसौ शक्यस्त्वया लोकान्तरं गतः ॥
पतिव्रतासि तेन त्वं मुहूर्तमनुपश्यसि ॥ ॥45 ॥
2.8.m: He cannot be followed by you, having gone to the other world; / you are devoted to your husband, and therefore you see [him] for a moment.

2.8.s:
guruśuśrūṣaṇādbhadre tathā satyavato mahat ..
puṇyaṃ samarjitaṃ yena nayāmyenamahaṃ svayam .. 46 ..
2.8.d:
गुरुशुश्रूषणाद्भद्रे तथा सत्यवतो महत् ॥
पुण्यं समर्जितं येन नयाम्येनमहं स्वयम् ॥ 46 ॥
2.8.m: From serving his elders, gentle lady, great religious merit / was gathered by Satyavān, because of which I myself lead him away.

2.8.s:
etāvadeva kartavyaṃ puruṣasya vijānataḥ ..
mātuḥ pituśca śuśrūṣā gurośca varavarṇini .. 47 ..
2.8.d:
एतावदेव कर्तव्यं पुरुषस्य विजानतः ॥
मातुः पितुश्च शुश्रूषा गुरोश्च वरवर्णिनि ॥ 47 ॥
2.8.m:
This much alone is to be done by a wise man:
service to mother and father, and to the teacher, O fair-complexioned one.

2.8.s: gurutritayametacca sadā satyavatā vane .. 48 ..
2.8.d: गुरुत्रितयमेतच्च सदा सत्यवता वने ॥ 48 ॥
2.8.m: And this triad of elders was always in the forest by Satyavān

2.8.s:
pūjitaṃ pūjitassvargastadānena ciraṃ śubhe ..
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa tvagniśuśrūṣayā tathā ..49..
2.8.d:
पूजितं पूजितस्स्वर्गस्तदानेन चिरं शुभे ॥
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण त्वग्निशुश्रूषया तथा ॥49॥
2.8.m:
honoured; therefore heaven was honoured by him for a long time, O auspicious lady.
By austerity, by student-chastity, and likewise by tending the sacred fire,

2.8.s:
puruṣāḥ svargamāyānti guruśuśrūṣaṇena ca ..
ācāryaśca pitā caiva mātā bhrātā ca pūrvajaḥ .. 50 ..
2.8.d:
पुरुषाः स्वर्गमायान्ति गुरुशुश्रूषणेन च ॥
आचार्यश्च पिता चैव माता भ्राता च पूर्वजः ॥ 50 ॥
2.8.m:
and by serving the elders, men attain heaven.
The preceptor, the father, the mother, and the elder brother

2.8.s:
nārtenāpyavamantavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ ..
ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ ..51..
2.8.d:
नार्तेनाप्यवमन्तव्या ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः ॥
आचार्यो ब्रह्मणो मूर्तिः पिता मूर्तिः प्रजापतेः ॥51॥
2.8.m:
must not be disrespected, even in distress, especially by a brahmin.
The preceptor is the embodiment of Brahmā, the father the embodiment of Prajāpati,

2.8.s:
mātā pṛthivyā mūrtiśca bhrātā vai mūrtirātmanaḥ ..
yanmātāpitarau kleśaṃ sahete sambhave nṛṇām .. 52 ..
2.8.d:
माता पृथिव्या मूर्तिश्च भ्राता वै मूर्तिरात्मनः ॥
यन्मातापितरौ क्लेशं सहेते सम्भवे नृणाम् ॥ 52 ॥
2.8.m:
the mother the embodiment of the earth, and the brother indeed the embodiment of oneself.
The distress that mother and father endure in the birth of human beings—

2.8.s:
na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi ..
tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryādācāryasya ca sarvadā .. 53 ..
2.8.d:
न तस्य निष्कृतिः शक्या कर्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ॥
तयोर्नित्यं प्रियं कुर्यादाचार्यस्य च सर्वदा ॥ 53 ॥
2.8.m:
no recompense can be made for it even in a hundred years;
one should always do what is pleasing to them both, and to the preceptor at all times.

2.8.s:
teṣveva triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ satyaṃ samāpyate ..
teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate .. 54 ..
2.8.d:
तेष्वेव त्रिषु तुष्टेषु तपः सत्यं समाप्यते ॥
तेषां त्रयाणां शुश्रूषा परमं तप उच्यते ॥ 54 ॥
2.8.m:
Only when those three are pleased is true austerity fulfilled;
service to those three is declared to be the highest austerity.

2.8.s:
na tairanabhyanujñāto dharmamanyaṃ samācareta ..
ta eva hi trayo lokāsta eva traya āśramāḥ .. 55 ..
2.8.d:
न तैरनभ्यनुज्ञातो धर्ममन्यं समाचरेत ॥
त एव हि त्रयो लोकास्त एव त्रय आश्रमाः ॥ 55 ॥
2.8.m: Without being permitted by them, he should not practice any other dharma. / For they are the three worlds, they are the three stages of life;

2.8.s:
ta eva ca trayo vedāsta evoktāstrayo'gnayaḥ ..
pitā vai gārhapatyo'gnirmātāgnirdakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 56 ..
2.8.d:
त एव च त्रयो वेदास्त एवोक्तास्त्रयोऽग्नयः ॥
पिता वै गार्हपत्योऽग्निर्माताग्निर्दक्षिणः स्मृतः ॥ 56 ॥
2.8.m: They are the three Vedas, and they are declared to be the three fires. / The father is indeed the Gārhapatya fire, the mother is regarded as the Dakṣiṇa fire,

2.8.s:
gururāhavanīyastu agnitretā garīyasī ..
triṣvapramādyanneteṣu trīṃllokāñjayate gṛhī .. 57 ..
2.8.d:
गुरुराहवनीयस्तु अग्नित्रेता गरीयसी ॥
त्रिष्वप्रमाद्यन्नेतेषु त्रींल्लोकाञ्जयते गृही ॥ 57 ॥
2.8.m: And the guru is the Āhavanīya: this triad of fires is supreme. / Not negligent toward these three, the householder conquers the three worlds.

2.8.s:
sa hi divyena vapuṣā devavaddivi modate ..
imaṃ lokaṃ mātṛbhaktaḥ pitṛbhaktastu madhyamam .. 58 ..
2.8.d:
स हि दिव्येन वपुषा देववद्दिवि मोदते ॥
इमं लोकं मातृभक्तः पितृभक्तस्तु मध्यमम् ॥ 58 ॥
2.8.m: With a divine body he rejoices in heaven like a god. / Devoted to his mother [he conquers] this world; devoted to his father, the middle [world];

2.8.s:
guruśuśrūṣayā tvevaṃ brahmalokaṃ samaśnute ..
sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ .. 59 ..
2.8.d:
गुरुशुश्रूषया त्वेवं ब्रह्मलोकं समश्नुते ॥
सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः ॥ 59 ॥
2.8.m: And through service to his guru he attains the world of Brahmā. / All dharmas are honored by him by whom these three are honored;

2.8.s:
anādṛtāstu yasyaite sarvāstasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ ..
yāvattrayaste jīveyustāvannānyatsamācaret .. 60 ..
2.8.d:
अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः ॥
यावत्त्रयस्ते जीवेयुस्तावन्नान्यत्समाचरेत् ॥ 60 ॥
2.8.m: But for him by whom these are disregarded, all ritual acts are fruitless. / As long as these three live, so long he should not practice another;

2.8.s:
tanuṃ nivedayettebhyo mano vacanakarmabhiḥ ..
triṣveteṣvitikṛtyaṃ hi puruṣasya samāpyate .. 61 ..
2.8.d:
तनुं निवेदयेत्तेभ्यो मनो वचनकर्मभिः ॥
त्रिष्वेतेष्वितिकृत्यं हि पुरुषस्य समाप्यते ॥ 61 ॥
2.8.m: He should dedicate his body to them in mind, speech, and action. / For in these three a man's whole duty is fulfilled.

2.8.s:
eṣa dharmaḥ paraḥ sākṣādupadharmo'nya ucyate ..
gurupūjāratirbhartā tvaṃ ca sādhvī pativratā .. 62 ..
2.8.d:
एष धर्मः परः साक्षादुपधर्मोऽन्य उच्यते ॥
गुरुपूजारतिर्भर्ता त्वं च साध्वी पतिव्रता ॥ 62 ॥
2.8.m: This is the supreme dharma directly; any other is called a secondary dharma. / Your husband is devoted to honoring his gurus, and you are a virtuous wife devoted to her husband.

2.8.s:
vinivartasva dharmajñe glānirbhavati te'dhunā ..
sāvitryuvāca ..
patirhi daivataṃ strīṇāṃ patireva parāyaṇam.. 63 ..
2.8.d:
विनिवर्तस्व धर्मज्ञे ग्लानिर्भवति तेऽधुना ॥
सावित्र्युवाच ॥
पतिर्हि दैवतं स्त्रीणां पतिरेव परायणम्॥ 63 ॥
2.8.m: Turn back, O knower of dharma; you are growing weary now. / Sāvitrī said: / A husband is indeed the deity of women; a husband alone is their ultimate refuge.

2.8.s:
anugamyaḥ striyā sādhvyā patiḥ prāṇadhaneśvaraḥ ..
mitaṃ dadāti hi pitā mitaṃ bhrātā mitaṃ sutaḥ .. 64 ..
2.8.d:
अनुगम्यः स्त्रिया साध्व्या पतिः प्राणधनेश्वरः ॥
मितं ददाति हि पिता मितं भ्राता मितं सुतः ॥ 64 ॥
2.8.m: A husband, the lord of life and wealth, must be followed by a virtuous woman. / For a father gives in measure, a brother gives in measure, a son gives in measure;

2.8.s:
amitasya hi dātāraṃ bhartāraṃ kā na pūjayeta ..
nīyate yatra bhartā me svayaṃ vā yatra gacchati .. 65 ..
2.8.d:
अमितस्य हि दातारं भर्तारं का न पूजयेत ॥
नीयते यत्र भर्ता मे स्वयं वा यत्र गच्छति ॥ 65 ॥
2.8.m: Who would not worship a husband, the giver of what is measureless? / Where my husband is taken, or where he goes of his own accord,

2.8.s:
mayāpi tatra gantavyaṃ yathāśakti surottama ..
patimādāya gacchantamanugantumahaṃ yadā .. 66 ..
2.8.d:
मयापि तत्र गन्तव्यं यथाशक्ति सुरोत्तम ॥
पतिमादाय गच्छन्तमनुगन्तुमहं यदा ॥ 66 ॥
2.8.m: I too must go there to the best of my ability, O foremost of gods. / When I am unable to follow you, O god,

2.8.s:
tvāṃ deva na hi śakṣyāmi tadā tyakṣyāmi jīvitam ..
manasvinī tathā kā ca vaidhavyākṣaradūṣitā .. 67 ..
2.8.d:
त्वां देव न हि शक्ष्यामि तदा त्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम् ॥
मनस्विनी तथा का च वैधव्याक्षरदूषिता ॥ 67 ॥
2.8.m: As you depart carrying away my husband, then I shall give up my life. / And what proud woman, blemished by the word 'widowhood',

2.8.s:
muhūrtamapi jīveta maṇḍanārhāpyamaṇḍitā ..
yama uvāca ..
pativrate mahābhāge parituṣṭo'smi te śubhe .. 68 ..
2.8.d:
मुहूर्तमपि जीवेत मण्डनार्हाप्यमण्डिता ॥
यम उवाच ॥
पतिव्रते महाभागे परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते शुभे ॥ 68 ॥
2.8.m: Would live even for a moment, though worthy of ornaments yet unadorned? / Yama said: / O devoted wife, O highly fortunate one, I am pleased with you, O auspicious woman.

2.8.s:
vinā satyavataḥ prāṇānvaraṃ varaya mā ciram ..
sāvitryuvāca ..
vinaṣṭacakṣuṣo rājyaṃ cakṣuṣā saha kāmaye ..
cyutarājyasya dharmajña śvaśurasya mahātmanaḥ .. 69 ..
2.8.d:
विना सत्यवतः प्राणान्वरं वरय मा चिरम् ॥
सावित्र्युवाच ॥
विनष्टचक्षुषो राज्यं चक्षुषा सह कामये ॥
च्युतराज्यस्य धर्मज्ञ श्वशुरस्य महात्मनः ॥ 69 ॥
2.8.m: Choose a boon without [asking for] the life of Satyavat; do not delay. / Sāvitrī said: / I desire the kingdom together with eyesight for my great-souled father-in-law,

2.8.s:
.. yama uvāca ..
kṛtena kāmena nivarta bhadre bhaviṣyatīdaṃ sakalaṃ tvayoktam ..
mamoparodhastava ca klamaḥ syāttathādhvanā tena tava bravīmi .. 70 ..
2.38
sāvittryuvāca..
kutaḥ klamaḥ kuto duḥkhaṃ sadbhiḥ saha samāgame ..
satāṃ tasmānna me glānistvatsamīpe surottama .. 1 ..
sādhūnāṃ vāpyasādhūnāṃ santa eva parā gatiḥ ..
naivāsatāṃ naiva satāmasanto naiva cātmanaḥ .. 2 ..
viṣāgnisarpaśastrebhyo na tathā jāyate bhayam ..
akāraṇajagadvairikhalebhyo jāyate yathā .. 3 ..
santaḥ prāṇānapi tyaktvā parārthaṃ kurvate yathā ..
tathā'santo'pi manujāḥ parapīḍāsu tatparāḥ ..4 ..
tyajatyasūnayaṃ lokastṛṇavadyasya kāraṇāt..
paropadhānasaktāste paralokaṃ tathā satā .. 5 ..
nikāyeṣunikāyeṣu purā brahmā jagadguruḥ ..
asatāmupaghātāya rājānaḥ kṛtavānsvayam .. 6 ..
2.8.d:
॥ यम उवाच ॥
कृतेन कामेन निवर्त भद्रे भविष्यतीदं सकलं त्वयोक्तम् ॥
ममोपरोधस्तव च क्लमः स्यात्तथाध्वना तेन तव ब्रवीमि ॥ 70 ॥
2.38
सावित्त्र्युवाच॥
कुतः क्लमः कुतो दुःखं सद्भिः सह समागमे ॥
सतां तस्मान्न मे ग्लानिस्त्वत्समीपे सुरोत्तम ॥ 1 ॥
साधूनां वाप्यसाधूनां सन्त एव परा गतिः ॥
नैवासतां नैव सतामसन्तो नैव चात्मनः ॥ 2 ॥
विषाग्निसर्पशस्त्रेभ्यो न तथा जायते भयम् ॥
अकारणजगद्वैरिखलेभ्यो जायते यथा ॥ 3 ॥
सन्तः प्राणानपि त्यक्त्वा परार्थं कुर्वते यथा ॥
तथाऽसन्तोऽपि मनुजाः परपीडासु तत्पराः ॥4 ॥
त्यजत्यसूनयं लोकस्तृणवद्यस्य कारणात्॥
परोपधानसक्तास्ते परलोकं तथा सता ॥ 5 ॥
निकायेषुनिकायेषु पुरा ब्रह्मा जगद्गुरुः ॥
असतामुपघाताय राजानः कृतवान्स्वयम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.8.m:
Who has lost his sight and fallen from his kingdom, O knower of dharma. / Yama said: / With your desire granted, turn back, O blessed one; all this that you have spoken will come to pass. / There would be obstruction for me and fatigue for you from the road; therefore I speak to you.
2.38 / Sāvitrī said: / Whence fatigue, whence sorrow in the company of the virtuous? / Therefore, being near you, O foremost of gods, I feel no weariness of the virtuous.
For the good or even for the wicked, the virtuous alone are the supreme refuge; / Never are the wicked [a refuge] for the wicked, never for the good, nor even for themselves.
Fear does not arise from poison, fire, serpents, or weapons / As it arises from wicked people who are gratuitous enemies of the world.
Just as the virtuous, even abandoning their lives, act for the sake of others, / So wicked men are likewise intent on tormenting others.
That for the sake of which this world abandons life like a blade of grass— / Those [wicked ones] are attached to defrauding others, but for the virtuous it is the other world.
In every community in ancient times, Brahmā, the teacher of the world, / Himself made kings for the suppression of the wicked.

2.8.s:
cāraiḥ parīkṣayedrājā dhūrtānsammārjayetsadā ..
nigrahaṃ cāsatāṃ kuryātsa tu lokajiduttamaḥ .. 7 ..
dhānyasaṃrakṣaṇārthāya nirmārṣṭā kakṣamuddharan ..
yathā vardhayate dhānyaṃ varddhanīyāstathā prajāḥ .. 8 ..
nigraheṇā satāṃ rājñā satāṃ ca paripālanaiḥ ..
etāvadeva kartavyaṃ rājñā svargamabhīpsatā .. 9 ..
rājakṛtyaṃ hi lokeṣu nāstyanyajjagatīpate ..
asatāṃ nigrahādeva satāṃ ca paripālanāt .. 10 ..
rājānuśāsitā teṣāmasatāṃ śāsitā bhavān ..
tena tvamadhiko deva devebhyaḥ pratibhāsi me .. 11 ..
jagattu dhāryate sadbhiḥ satāmagryastathā bhavān ..
tena tvāmabhiyāntyā me klamo deva na vidyate .. 12..
yama uvāca ..
tuṣṭosmi te viśālākṣi vacanairdharmasaṃhitaiḥ ..
vinā satyavataḥ prāṇānvaraṃ varaya mā ciram .. 13 ..
2.8.d:
चारैः परीक्षयेद्राजा धूर्तान्सम्मार्जयेत्सदा ॥
निग्रहं चासतां कुर्यात्स तु लोकजिदुत्तमः ॥ 7 ॥
धान्यसंरक्षणार्थाय निर्मार्ष्टा कक्षमुद्धरन् ॥
यथा वर्धयते धान्यं वर्द्धनीयास्तथा प्रजाः ॥ 8 ॥
निग्रहेणा सतां राज्ञा सतां च परिपालनैः ॥
एतावदेव कर्तव्यं राज्ञा स्वर्गमभीप्सता ॥ 9 ॥
राजकृत्यं हि लोकेषु नास्त्यन्यज्जगतीपते ॥
असतां निग्रहादेव सतां च परिपालनात् ॥ 10 ॥
राजानुशासिता तेषामसतां शासिता भवान् ॥
तेन त्वमधिको देव देवेभ्यः प्रतिभासि मे ॥ 11 ॥
जगत्तु धार्यते सद्भिः सतामग्र्यस्तथा भवान् ॥
तेन त्वामभियान्त्या मे क्लमो देव न विद्यते ॥ 12॥
यम उवाच ॥
तुष्टोस्मि ते विशालाक्षि वचनैर्धर्मसंहितैः ॥
विना सत्यवतः प्राणान्वरं वरय मा चिरम् ॥ 13 ॥
2.8.m:
A king should investigate through spies; he should always purge the rogues / And should punish the wicked; he is the supreme conqueror of worlds.
Just as one, clearing the weeds, cleanses [the field] to protect the grain, / And thus causes the grain to thrive, so should the subjects be made to thrive.
By punishing the wicked and protecting the virtuous— / This alone is to be done by a king desiring heaven.
For there is no other duty of kings in the worlds, O lord of the earth, / Than the suppression of the wicked and the protection of the virtuous.
A king is their chastiser, and you are the punisher of the wicked; / Therefore, O god, you appear to me as greater than the gods.
The world is upheld by the virtuous, and you are the foremost of the virtuous; / Therefore, O god, as I follow you, no fatigue is felt by me.
Yama said: / I am pleased with you, O large-eyed woman, by your words conjoined with dharma. / Choose a boon without [asking for] the life of Satyavat; do not delay.

सावित्र्युवाच ॥
सहोदराणां भ्रातॄणां कामयामि शतं विभो ॥
अनपत्यः पिता प्रीतिं पुत्रलाभात्प्रयातु मे॥14॥
यम उवाच ॥
कृतेन कामेन निवर्त भद्रे भविष्यतीदं सकलं तवोक्तम् ॥
ममोपरोधस्तव च क्लमः स्यात्तथाधुना तेन तव ब्रवीमि ॥15॥
2.39
सावित्र्युवाच ॥
धर्मो हि दैवतं स्त्रीणां पतिरेव परायणम् ॥
अनुगम्यः स्त्रिया साध्व्या पतिः प्राणधनेश्वरः ॥ 1 ॥
धर्मार्जने सुरश्रेष्ठ कुतो ग्लानिः कुतः क्लमः॥
त्वत्पादमूलमेवेदं परमं धर्मकारणम् ॥ 2 ॥
धर्मार्जनं सदा कार्यं पुरुषेण विजानता ॥
तल्लाभः सर्वलाभेभ्यो यतो देव विशिष्यते ॥ 3 ॥
धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च त्रिवर्गं जीवतः फलम् ॥
धर्महीनस्य कामार्थौ वन्ध्यासुतसमावुभौ ॥ 4 ॥
धर्मादर्थस्तथा कामो धर्माल्लोकद्वयं तथा ॥
धर्म एकोऽनुयात्येनं यत्र कुत्र च गामिनम् ॥ 5 ॥
2.8.m:
Sāvitrī said: / I desire a hundred brothers born of the same womb, O lord; / May my childless father attain joy through the acquisition of sons.
Yama said: / With your desire granted, turn back, O blessed one; all this that you have spoken will come to pass. / There would be obstruction for me and fatigue for you now; therefore I speak to you.
2.39 / Sāvitrī said: / Dharma is indeed the deity of women; the husband alone is their ultimate refuge. / A husband, the lord of life and wealth, must be followed by a virtuous woman.
In acquiring dharma, O best of gods, whence weariness, whence fatigue? / This very base of your feet is the supreme foundation of dharma.
The acquisition of dharma should always be practiced by a discerning man; / For its gain, O god, is superior to all gains.
Dharma, wealth, and pleasure are the three ends, the fruit of living; / For one devoid of dharma, pleasure and wealth are both like the son of a barren woman.
From dharma comes wealth, and likewise pleasure; from dharma likewise come the two worlds. / Dharma alone follows him wherever he goes.

2.8.d:
शरीरेण समं नाशं सर्वमन्यद्धि गच्छति ॥
एको हि जायते जन्तुरेक एव विपद्यते ॥ 6 ॥
धर्मस्तमनुयात्येको न सुहृन्न च बान्धवाः ॥
रूपसौभाग्यलावण्यं सम्पद्धर्मेण लभ्यते॥ 7॥
ब्रह्मेन्द्रोपेन्द्रशर्वेन्द्रयमार्काग्न्यनिलाम्भसाम् ॥
वस्वश्विधनदाद्यानां ये लोकाः सर्वकामदाः ॥ 8 ॥
धर्मेण तानवाप्नोति पुरुषः पुरुषान्तक ॥
मनोहराणि द्वीपानि वर्षाणि सुमुखानि च॥ 9 ॥
प्रयान्ति धर्मेण नरास्तथैवामरतामिताः ॥
नन्दनादीनि मुख्यानि देवोद्यानानि यानि च ॥ 10 ॥
तानि पुण्येन लभ्यन्ते नाकपृष्ठं तथा नरैः ॥
विमानानि विचित्राणि तथैवाप्सरसः शुभाः ॥ 11 ॥
तैजसानि शरीराणि सदा पुण्यवतां फलम ॥
राज्यं नृपतिपूजा च कामसिद्धिस्तथेप्सिता ॥ 12 ॥
उपस्कराणि मुख्यानि फलं पुण्यस्य दृश्यते ॥
रुक्मवैडूर्यदण्डानि चन्द्रांशुसदृशानि च ॥ 13 ॥
2.8.m:
For everything else goes to destruction along with the body. / Alone a living creature is born, and alone it perishes;
Dharma alone follows it, not a friend and not relatives. / Form, good fortune, grace, and prosperity are obtained through dharma.
Those worlds that grant all desires, belonging to Brahmā, Indra, Upendra, Śarva, Indra, Yama, the Sun, Fire, Wind, the Waters, / The Vasus, the Aśvins, Kubera, and the rest,
A man attains through dharma, O ender of men, / As well as charming continents and pleasant realms.
Likewise, through dharma men attain immortality, having gone from here. / And whatever gardens of the gods there are, chief among them Nandana,
those are gained by men through merit, as is the vault of heaven, / and wondrous celestial chariots, and auspicious Apsarases.
Luminous bodies are ever the fruit of the meritorious, / as are kingship, honour from monarchs, and the attainment of desired wishes.
Eminent regalia are seen as the fruit of merit: / fly-whisks with shafts of gold and cat's-eye gems, resembling moonbeams,

2.8.d:
चामराणि सुराध्यक्ष भवन्ति शुभकर्मणाम् ॥
( पूर्णेन्दुमण्डलाभेन रक्तांशुकमितेन च ॥14॥
धार्यतां यान्ति छत्रेण नरः पुण्येन कर्मणा ॥)
जयशङ्खस्वनादेव सूतमागधनिःस्वनम ॥ 15 ॥
वरासनं सभृङ्गारं फलं पुण्या कर्मणः ॥
वरान्नपानं गीतं च नृत्यमाल्यानुलेपनम् ॥ 16 ॥
रत्नवस्त्राणि मुख्यानि फलं पुण्यस्य कर्मणः ॥
रूपौदार्यगुणोपेताः स्त्रियश्चातिनोहराः ॥ 17 ॥
वासः प्रासादपृष्ठेषु भवन्ति शुभकर्मणाम् ॥
सुवर्णकिंकिणी मिश्रचामराः पीठधारिणः ॥ 18 ॥
वहन्ति तुरगा देव नरं पुण्येन कर्मणा ॥

खेलांघ्रिपदविन्यासैर्यान्ति पुण्येन कर्मणा ॥
सर्वकामप्रदे देवे सर्वापद्दुरितापहे ॥20 ॥
वहन्ति भक्तिं पुरुषास्सदा पुण्येन कर्मणा ॥
तस्य द्वाराणि यजनं तपो दानं दया क्षमा ॥ 21 ॥

belong to those of auspicious deeds, O lord of the gods. / With a parasol shining like the disc of the full moon and measured by red silk,
a man is attended through meritorious deed. / From the sound of conches of victory and the cries of heralds and bards,
an excellent throne with a golden ewer is the fruit of meritorious deed; / excellent food and drink, song, dance, garlands, and unguents;

carry a man, O god, through meritorious deed; / and elephants with golden girths, resembling moving mountains,
with playful stepping of feet, they mount through meritorious deed. / In the God who grants all desires and removes all distress and sin,
men ever bear devotion through meritorious deed. / Its portals are sacrifice, austerity, gift-giving, compassion, forbearance,

2.8.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं च सत्यं च तीर्थानुसरणं शुभे ॥
स्वाध्यायसेवा साधूनां सहवासः सुरार्चनम् ॥22॥
गुरूणां चैव शुश्रूषा ब्राह्मणानां च पूजनम् ॥
इन्द्रियाणां जयश्चैव मार्दवं ह्रीरमत्सरम् ॥ 23 ॥
तस्माद्धर्मः सदा कार्यो नित्यमेव विजानता ॥
न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम् ॥ 24 ॥
बाल एवाचरेद्धर्ममनित्यं देव जीवितम् ॥
को हि जानाति कस्याद्य मृत्युः केन भविष्यति ॥25॥
पश्यतोऽप्यस्य लोकस्य मरणं पुरतः स्थितम् ॥
अमरस्येव चरितमत्याश्चर्यं सुरोत्तम ॥ 26 ॥
युवत्वापेक्षया बालो वृद्धत्वापेक्षया युवा ॥
मृत्योरुत्सङ्गमारूढः स्थविरः किमपेक्षते ॥ 27 ॥
भुवः शैलं समारूढः ततो वृक्षाग्रमाश्रितः ॥
तत्राप्यविन्दतस्त्राणं मृत्योद्भीतस्य का गतिः ॥ 28 ॥
2.8.m:
celibacy, truthfulness, visiting holy bathing places, O auspicious one, / regular study of scripture, service of the virtuous, living together [with them], worship of the gods,
attendance upon teachers, honouring of brahmins, / mastery of the senses, gentleness, modesty, and freedom from malice.
Therefore, dharma should always be performed constantly by one who knows; / for Death does not wait [to see] whether one's duty has been done or not done.
Even while a child, one should practice dharma; life is transient, O god. / For who knows for whom death will occur today, and by what means?
Though this world sees death standing before it, / it acts as if it were immortal: this is a great wonder, O best of the gods.
In expectation of youth, one is a child; in expectation of old age, one is a youth; / mounted upon the lap of Death, what does an old man expect?
One may climb from the earth to a mountain, and then take refuge in the top of a tree; / finding no protection even there, what recourse is there for one terrified of Death?

2.40
सावित्र्युवाच ॥
सर्वधर्मविधानज्ञः सर्वधर्मप्रवर्तकः ॥

तस्मात्ते धर्मराजेति नाम सत्यं निगद्यते ॥ 3 ॥
2.8.m:
There is nowhere any fear greater than death for living beings; / yet even in that, good people who always do good deeds remain fearless.
Yama said: / I am pleased with you, O large-eyed woman, because of your words conjoined with dharma. / Except for the life of Satyavat, choose a boon without delay.
Sāvitrī said: / I choose a hundred sons of my own body, granted by you; / for one without offspring has indeed no path in the worlds.
Yama said: / Your wish granted, turn back, O blessed lady; all this spoken by you shall come to pass. / It would be a hindrance to me and a weariness to you, and therefore I speak thus to you now.
2.40 / Sāvitrī said: / Knowing the ordinances of all dharmas, promoting all dharmas, / you alone are the lord of the worlds, Yama who restrains all creatures.
Because you restrain creatures according to their deeds, / therefore, O god, you are called by the very name Yama.
Because, O lord, you delight all these creatures through dharma, / therefore your name Dharmarāja is truly proclaimed.

2.8.d:
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चोभे पुरोधाय यथा जनाः ॥
त्वत्सकाशमथायान्ति तस्मात्त्वं मृत्युरुच्यसे ॥ 4 ॥
सर्वेषामथ भूतानां यस्मादन्तकरो भवान् ॥॥
तस्मात्वमन्तकः प्रोक्तः सर्वदेवैर्महाद्युते ॥ 5 ॥
विवस्वतस्त्वं तनयः प्रथमः परिकीर्तितः ॥
तस्माद्वैवस्वतो नाम्ना सर्वदेवेषु कथ्यसे ॥ 6 ॥
कालं कलाद्यं कलयन्सर्वेषां त्वं हि तिष्ठसि ॥
तस्मात्कालेति ते नाम प्रोच्यते तत्सुदर्शिभिः ॥7 ॥
आयुष्ये कर्मणि क्षीणे गृह्णासि प्रसभं जनम् ॥॥।
तस्मात्त्वं कथ्यसे लोके सर्वप्राणहरेति वै ॥ 8 ॥
तव प्रसादाद्देवेश धर्मे तिष्ठन्ति जन्तवः ॥
तव प्रसादाद्देवेश सङ्करो नैव जायते ॥ 9 ॥
सतां सदा गतिर्देव त्वमेव परिकीर्तितः ॥
जगतोऽस्य जगन्नाथ मर्यादापरिपालकः ॥10 ॥
2.8.m:
Because people come into your presence / having placed both good deeds and evil deeds before them, therefore you are called Mṛtyu.
And because you make an end of all beings, / therefore you are called Antaka by all the gods, O you of great splendour.
You are celebrated as the first son of Vivasvat; / therefore you are named Vaivasvata among all the gods.
Indeed, you stand measuring the divisions of time beginning with kalās for all [beings]; / therefore the name Kāla is declared for you by those of true discernment.
When life and deed are exhausted, you seize a person by force; / therefore you are indeed called in the world the Stealer of All Life.
By your favour, O lord of the gods, creatures abide in dharma; / by your favour, O lord of the gods, confusion of classes does not arise.
You alone are celebrated, O god, as the constant refuge of the virtuous; / O lord of the world, protector of the bounds of this universe,

पाहि मां त्रिदशश्रेष्ठ दुःखितां शरणागताम् ॥
पितरौ च तथैवास्य राजपुत्रस्य दुःखितौ ॥ 11 ॥
यम उवाच ॥
स्तुतेन भक्त्या धर्मज्ञे मया तुष्टेन सत्यवान् ॥
तव भर्ता विमुक्तोऽयं लब्धकामा व्रजाबले ॥ 12 ॥
राज्यं कृत्वा त्वया सार्धं वत्सराशीतिपञ्चकम् ॥
नाकपृष्ठमथारुह्य त्रिदशैस्सह रंस्यते ॥ 13 ॥
स्तोत्रेणानेन धर्मज्ञे कल्यमुत्थाय यश्च माम् ॥
कीर्तयिष्यति तस्यापि दीर्घमायुर्भविष्यति ॥ 14 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥ एतावदुक्त्वा भगवान्यमस्तु विमुच्य तं राजसुतं महात्मा ॥
अदर्शनं तत्र जगाम राम कालेन सार्धं सह मृत्युना च॥15॥
2.8.m:
protect me, O best of the thirty gods, afflicted and seeking refuge, / and likewise the grieving parents of this prince.
Yama said: / Praised with devotion, O knower of dharma, and pleased by you, / this husband of yours, Satyavat, is released; go, O woman, having obtained your desires.
Having ruled the kingdom together with you for eighty-five years, / he shall ascend to the vault of heaven and delight with the thirty gods.
And whoever, rising at dawn, praises me with this hymn, / O knower of dharma, he too shall have a long life.
Puṣkara said: / Having spoken thus, the venerable, noble Yama, having released that prince, / vanished from sight there, O Rāma, together with Kāla and Mṛtyu.

पुष्कर उवाच ॥
गवां हि पालनं राज्ञा कर्तव्यं भृगुनन्दन ॥
गावः पवित्राः संगत्या गोषु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 1 ॥
