गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिश्च रोचनम् ॥
षडङ्गमेतन्माङ्गल्यं पवित्रं तु पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 6 ॥
2.9.m:
Their word never becomes false here in the worlds of moving and unmoving beings; / therefore, they must always be revered completely by those who desire all their wishes.
2.42 / Puṣkara said: / The protection of cows must indeed be performed by a king, O scion of Bhṛgu. / Cows are purifying by association; the worlds are established in cows.
Cows extend the sacrifice; cows are the mothers of the universe. / Their dung and urine are traditionally held to be the supreme destroyers of misfortune.
They should indeed be used with effort; Fortune is established there. / And one who knows should feel no aversion toward their dung and urine.
One should not emit spit or the like upon the urine and dung of cows. / The dust of cows is supremely holy, destroying misfortune and obstacles.
And scratching cows destroys all impurities. / And the water from their horns is equal to the water of the Jāhnavī.
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and yellow pigment: / this sixfold collection is auspicious, and each part is purifying on its own.

2.9.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam ..
pavitraṃ paramaṃ jñeyaṃ snāne pāne ca bhārgava .. 7 ..
rakṣoghnametanmāṅgalyaṃ kaliduḥkhapraṇāśanam ..
rocanā ca tathā dhanyā rakṣoragagadāpahā ..
yastu kalye samutthāya mukhamājye nirīkṣate ..
tasyālakṣmīḥ kṣayaṃ yāti vardhate na tu kilbiṣam .. 9 ..
gavāṃ grāsapradānena puṇyaṃ sumahadaśnute ..
yāvatyaḥ śaknuyādgāvaḥ sukhaṃ dhārayituṃ gṛhe .. 2.42.10 ..
dhārayettāvatīrnityaṃ kṣudhitāstu na dhārayet ..
duḥkhitā dhenavo yasya vasanti dvija mandire .. 11 ..
narakaṃ samavāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
dattvā paragave grāsaṃ puṇyaṃ sumahadaśnute .. 12 ..
śaiśiraṃ sakalaṃ kālaṃ grāsaṃ paragave tathā ..
dattvā svargamavāpnoti saṃvatsaraśatāni ṣaṭ .. 13 ..
2.9.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् ॥
पवित्रं परमं ज्ञेयं स्नाने पाने च भार्गव ॥ 7 ॥
रक्षोघ्नमेतन्माङ्गल्यं कलिदुःखप्रणाशनम् ॥
रोचना च तथा धन्या रक्षोरगगदापहा ॥
यस्तु कल्ये समुत्थाय मुखमाज्ये निरीक्षते ॥
तस्यालक्ष्मीः क्षयं याति वर्धते न तु किल्बिषम् ॥ 9 ॥
गवां ग्रासप्रदानेन पुण्यं सुमहदश्नुते ॥
यावत्यः शक्नुयाद्गावः सुखं धारयितुं गृहे ॥ 2.42.10 ॥
धारयेत्तावतीर्नित्यं क्षुधितास्तु न धारयेत् ॥
दुःखिता धेनवो यस्य वसन्ति द्विज मन्दिरे ॥ 11 ॥
नरकं समवाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
दत्त्वा परगवे ग्रासं पुण्यं सुमहदश्नुते ॥ 12 ॥
शैशिरं सकलं कालं ग्रासं परगवे तथा ॥
दत्त्वा स्वर्गमवाप्नोति संवत्सरशतानि षट् ॥ 13 ॥
2.9.m:
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, clarified butter, and kuśa water: / this should be known as supremely purifying for bathing and drinking, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
This is auspicious, slaying demons, and destroying the distress of Kali. / Yellow pigment is likewise blessed, warding off demons, serpents, and diseases. / Whoever rises at dawn and gazes at his face in clarified butter, / his misfortune perishes and his sin does not increase.
By giving a mouthful of food to cows, one attains very great religious merit. / As many cows as one is able to keep comfortably in one's home,
so many he should keep constantly; but he should not keep hungry ones. / In whose house, O twice-born, cows dwell in misery,
he goes to hell; there should be no doubt about this. / Having given a mouthful of food to another's cow, one attains very great merit.
Having given a mouthful of food to another's cow throughout the winter season, / one attains heaven for six hundred years.

2.9.s:
agrabhaktaṃ naro dattvā nityameva tathā gavām ..
māsaṣaṭkena labhate nākalokaṃ samāyutam .. 14 ..
sāyaṃ prātarmanuṣyāṇāmaśanaṃ devanirmitam ..
tatraivamaśanaṃ dattvā gavāṃ nityamatandritaḥ .. 15 ..
dvitīyaṃ yaḥ samaśnāti tena saṃvatsarānnaraḥ ..
gavāṃ lokamavāpnoti yāvanmanvantaraṃ dvija .. 16 ..
gavāṃ pracāre pānīyaṃ dattvā puruṣasattamaḥ ..
vāruṇaṃ lokamāsādya krīḍatyabdagaṇāyutam ..
parāṃ tṛptimavāpnoti yatrayatrābhijāyate .. 17 ..
gavāṃ pracārabhūmiṃ tu vāhayitvā halādinā ..
narakaṃ mahadāpnoti yāvadindrāścaturdaśa .. 16 ..
gavāṃ pānapravṛtānāṃ yastu vighnaṃ samācareta ..
brahmahatyā kṛtā tena ghorā bhavati bhārgava ..
siṃhavyāghrabhayatrastāṃ paṅkamagnāṃ jale gatām .. 19 ..
gāmuddhṛtya naraḥ svarge kalpabhogānupāśnute ..
gavāṃ yavasadānena rūpavānabhijāyate .. 2.42.20 ..
2.9.d:
अग्रभक्तं नरो दत्त्वा नित्यमेव तथा गवाम् ॥
मासषट्केन लभते नाकलोकं समायुतम् ॥ 14 ॥
सायं प्रातर्मनुष्याणामशनं देवनिर्मितम् ॥
तत्रैवमशनं दत्त्वा गवां नित्यमतन्द्रितः ॥ 15 ॥
द्वितीयं यः समश्नाति तेन संवत्सरान्नरः ॥
गवां लोकमवाप्नोति यावन्मन्वन्तरं द्विज ॥ 16 ॥
गवां प्रचारे पानीयं दत्त्वा पुरुषसत्तमः ॥
वारुणं लोकमासाद्य क्रीडत्यब्दगणायुतम् ॥
परां तृप्तिमवाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥ 17 ॥
गवां प्रचारभूमिं तु वाहयित्वा हलादिना ॥
नरकं महदाप्नोति यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्दश ॥ 16 ॥
गवां पानप्रवृतानां यस्तु विघ्नं समाचरेत ॥
ब्रह्महत्या कृता तेन घोरा भवति भार्गव ॥
सिंहव्याघ्रभयत्रस्तां पङ्कमग्नां जले गताम् ॥ 19 ॥
गामुद्धृत्य नरः स्वर्गे कल्पभोगानुपाश्नुते ॥
गवां यवसदानेन रूपवानभिजायते ॥ 2.42.20 ॥
2.9.m:
A man who gives the first portion of his food to cows every day / attains the realm of heaven for ten thousand years within six months.
The evening and morning meals of men were ordained by the gods. / Giving such food to cows constantly and untiringly,
the man who eats the second portion himself, after one year, / attains the world of cows for as long as a manvantara lasts, O twice-born.
The best of men, having provided drinking water in the pasture of cows, / reaches the world of Varuṇa and sports there for ten thousand years; / and he attains supreme satisfaction wherever he is born.
Having plowed the pasture land of cows with a plow or the like, / one falls into a terrible hell for as long as fourteen Indras rule.
Whoever causes an obstacle to cows engaged in drinking, / by him the dreadful murder of a brahmin has been committed, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / [A cow] terrified by fear of a lion or tiger, sunk in mud, or fallen into water,
rescuing [such] a cow, a man enjoys pleasures in heaven for an aeon. / By the gift of grass to cows, one is born handsome,

2.9.s:
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti lāvaṇyaṃ ca dvijottama ..
auṣadhaṃ ca tathā dattvā virogastvabhijāyate .. .. 21 ..
2.9.d:
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति लावण्यं च द्विजोत्तम ॥
औषधं च तथा दत्त्वा विरोगस्त्वभिजायते ॥ ॥ 21 ॥
2.9.m: attains great good fortune and charm, O best of the twice-born; / and having given medicine, one is born free from disease.

2.9.s:
auṣadhaṃ lavaṇaṃ toyamāhāraṃ ca prayacchataḥ ..
vipattau pātakaṃ nāsya bhavatyudbandhanādikama .. 22 ..
2.9.d:
औषधं लवणं तोयमाहारं च प्रयच्छतः ॥
विपत्तौ पातकं नास्य भवत्युद्बन्धनादिकम ॥ 22 ॥
2.9.m: For one who gives medicine, salt, water, and food [to a cow], / no sin accrues if misfortune, such as death by hanging or the like, should occur.

2.9.s:
vaktavyatā divāpāle rātrau svāmī na tadgṛhe ..
tatrāpi tanniyuktaśca kaścidanyo na cedbhavet .. 23 ..
2.9.d:
वक्तव्यता दिवापाले रात्रौ स्वामी न तद्गृहे ॥
तत्रापि तन्नियुक्तश्च कश्चिदन्यो न चेद्भवेत् ॥ 23 ॥
2.9.m: Blame falls upon the herdsman by day; at night the owner [is responsible] if it is not in his house, / provided that no other person appointed by him is present there.

2.9.s:
tāsāṃ cedaviruddhānāṃ carantīnāṃ mitho vane ..
yāmutpatya vṛko hanyānnapālastatra kilbiṣī .. 24 ..
2.9.d:
तासां चेदविरुद्धानां चरन्तीनां मिथो वने ॥
यामुत्पत्य वृको हन्यान्नपालस्तत्र किल्बिषी ॥ 24 ॥
2.9.m: If, while they are grazing peacefully together in the forest, / a wolf should leap up and kill one of them, the herdsman is not guilty of sin.

2.9.s:
saṃruddhāsu tathaivāsu vṛkaḥ pāle tvanāyati ..
yāmutpatya vṛko hanyātpāle tatkilbiṣaṃ bhaveta .. 25 ..
2.9.d:
संरुद्धासु तथैवासु वृकः पाले त्वनायति ॥
यामुत्पत्य वृको हन्यात्पाले तत्किल्बिषं भवेत ॥ 25 ॥
2.9.m: Likewise, when they are penned up, if a wolf [attacks] when the keeper does not come, / whichever [cow] a wolf attacks and kills, the guilt for that falls on the keeper.

2.9.s:
govadhena naro yāti narakānekaviṃśatim ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryaṃ tāsāṃ tu pālanam .. 26 ..
2.9.d:
गोवधेन नरो याति नरकानेकविंशतिम् ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कार्यं तासां तु पालनम् ॥ 26 ॥
2.9.m: By killing a cow, a man goes to twenty-one hells; / therefore, by all efforts, their protection must be performed.

2.9.s:
vikrayācca gavāṃ rāma na bhadraṃ pratipadyate ..
tāsāṃ ca kīrtanādeva naraḥ pāpādvimucyate .. 27 ..
2.9.d:
विक्रयाच्च गवां राम न भद्रं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
तासां च कीर्तनादेव नरः पापाद्विमुच्यते ॥ 27 ॥
2.9.m: And from the sale of cows, O Rāma, one does not attain good fortune; / but simply by glorifying them, a man is freed from sin.

2.9.s:
tāsāṃ saṃsparśanaṃ dhanyaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..
dānena ca tathā tāsāṃ kulānyapi samuddharet .. 28 ..
2.9.d:
तासां संस्पर्शनं धन्यं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥
दानेन च तथा तासां कुलान्यपि समुद्धरेत् ॥ 28 ॥
2.9.m: Touching them brings blessing and destroys all defilements; / and likewise through the gift of them, one may uplift even [entire] lineages.

2.9.s:
udakyā sūtiko doṣo naiva tatra gṛhe bhavet ..
bhūmidoṣāstathānye'pi yatraikā vasate tu gauḥ .. 29 ..
2.9.d:
उदक्या सूतिको दोषो नैव तत्र गृहे भवेत् ॥
भूमिदोषास्तथान्येऽपि यत्रैका वसते तु गौः ॥ 29 ॥
2.9.m: The fault of a menstruating woman or of a woman in childbed does not occur in that house, / nor other faults of the ground, wherever even a single cow resides.

2.9.s:
gavāṃ niśvāsavātena parā śāntirgṛhe bhaveta ..
nīrājanaṃ tatparamaṃ sarvasthāneṣu kīrtitam .. 2.42.30 ..
2.9.d:
गवां निश्वासवातेन परा शान्तिर्गृहे भवेत ॥
नीराजनं तत्परमं सर्वस्थानेषु कीर्तितम् ॥ 2.42.30 ॥
2.9.m: Through the wind of the breath of cows, supreme peace arises in the house; / that is proclaimed the highest lustration in all places.

2.9.s:
gavāṃ saṃsparśanādrāma kṣīyate kilbiṣaṃ nṛṇām ..
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam .. 31 ..
2.9.d:
गवां संस्पर्शनाद्राम क्षीयते किल्बिषं नृणाम् ॥
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् ॥ 31 ॥
2.9.m: From touching cows, O Rāma, the sin of men diminishes. / Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curds, ghee, water with kuśa grass,

2.9.s:
ekarātropavāsaṃ ca śvapākamapi śodhayet ..
pṛthaktvapratyayābhyastamatisantapanaṃ smṛtam .. 32 ..
2.9.d:
एकरात्रोपवासं च श्वपाकमपि शोधयेत् ॥
पृथक्त्वप्रत्ययाभ्यस्तमतिसन्तपनं स्मृतम् ॥ 32 ॥
2.9.m: and fasting for a single night will purify even an outcaste. / Practised with each substance separately, it is known as the atisantāpana [penance];

2.9.s:
sarvāśubhavimokṣāya purā caritamīśvareḥ ..
pratyekaṃ ca tryahābhyastaṃ cātisāṃtapanaṃ smṛtam .. 33 ..
2.9.d:
सर्वाशुभविमोक्षाय पुरा चरितमीश्वरेः ॥
प्रत्येकं च त्र्यहाभ्यस्तं चातिसांतपनं स्मृतम् ॥ 33 ॥
2.9.m: it was undertaken of old by the lords for liberation from all misfortune. / Practised with each [substance] for three days, it is traditionally known as the atisāntāpana,

2.9.s:
sarvakāmapradaṃ rāma sarvāśubhavināśanam ..
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ payasā divasānekaviṃśatim .. 34 ..
2.9.d:
सर्वकामप्रदं राम सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ॥
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं पयसा दिवसानेकविंशतिम् ॥ 34 ॥
2.9.m: which grants all desires, O Rāma, and destroys all misfortune. / The kṛcchrātikṛcchra [penance] is observed with milk for twenty-one days;

2.9.s:
nirmalāstena cīrṇena bhavanti puruṣottamāḥ ..
tryahamuṣṇaṃ pibenmūtraṃ tryahamuṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibet .. .. 35 ..
2.9.d:
निर्मलास्तेन चीर्णेन भवन्ति पुरुषोत्तमाः ॥
त्र्यहमुष्णं पिबेन्मूत्रं त्र्यहमुष्णं घृतं पिबेत् ॥ ॥ 35 ॥
2.9.m: having observed it, men become spotless and supreme among men. / For three days one should drink warm urine; for three days one should drink warm ghee;

2.9.s:
tryahamuṣṇaṃ payaḥ pītvā vāyubhakṣaḥ paraṃ tryaham ..
taptakṛcchramidaṃ proktaṃ sarvāśubhavināśanam .. 36 ..
2.9.d:
त्र्यहमुष्णं पयः पीत्वा वायुभक्षः परं त्र्यहम् ॥
तप्तकृच्छ्रमिदं प्रोक्तं सर्वाशुभविनाशनम् ॥ 36 ॥
2.9.m: having drunk warm milk for three days, one subsists on air for the next three days. / This is declared the taptakṛcchra, destroying all misfortune.

2.9.s:
śītakṛcchrastathaivaiṣa kramācchītaiḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
sarvāśubhavināśāya nirmito brahmaṇā svayam .. 37 ..
2.9.d:
शीतकृच्छ्रस्तथैवैष क्रमाच्छीतैः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
सर्वाशुभविनाशाय निर्मितो ब्रह्मणा स्वयम् ॥ 37 ॥
2.9.m: Likewise, this cold penance (śītakṛcchra) is proclaimed in the same order with cold [substances]; / it was instituted by Brahmā himself for the destruction of all misfortune.

2.9.s:
gomūtreṇa caretsnānaṃ vṛttiṃ kuryāttu gorasaiḥ ..
utthitāmutthitastiṣṭhedupaviṣṭāsu nā sthitaḥ .. 38 ..
2.9.d:
गोमूत्रेण चरेत्स्नानं वृत्तिं कुर्यात्तु गोरसैः ॥
उत्थितामुत्थितस्तिष्ठेदुपविष्टासु ना स्थितः ॥ 38 ॥
2.9.m: One should bathe with cow urine and make one's livelihood through the products of cows. / When [the cow] stands up, one should stand; when they are seated, a man should remain [seated].

2.9.s:
abhuktavatsu nāśnīyādapītāsu ca no pibet ..
trāṇaṃ tu rāmākṛtvaiva tathā deve pravarṣati .. 39 ..
2.9.d:
अभुक्तवत्सु नाश्नीयादपीतासु च नो पिबेत् ॥
त्राणं तु रामाकृत्वैव तथा देवे प्रवर्षति ॥ 39 ॥
2.9.m: While they have not eaten, one should not eat; while they have not drunk, one should not drink. / And without providing shelter for them, O Rāma, when the god [Indra] rains,

2.9.s:
trāṇaṃ naivātmanaḥ kāryaṃ bhayā rttāśca samuddharet ..
ātmānamapi santyajya govrataṃ tatprakīrtitam .. 2.42.40 ..
2.9.d:
त्राणं नैवात्मनः कार्यं भया र्त्ताश्च समुद्धरेत् ॥
आत्मानमपि सन्त्यज्य गोव्रतं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 2.42.40 ॥
2.9.m: one must not seek shelter for oneself, and one should rescue those afflicted by fear, / even giving up one's own life: that is declared the vow of cows (govrata).

2.9.s:
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ māsenaikena bhārgava ..
vratenānena cīrṇena golokaṃ puruṣo vrajet .. 41 ..
2.9.d:
सर्वपापप्रशमनं मासेनैकेन भार्गव ॥
व्रतेनानेन चीर्णेन गोलोकं पुरुषो व्रजेत् ॥ 41 ॥
2.9.m: In one month, O Bhārgava, it brings pacification of all sins; / by observing this vow, a man goes to the world of cows (Goloka),

2.9.s:
abhīṣṭamatha vā rāma yāvadindrāścaturdaśa ..
gavāṃ nirhāranirmuktānaśnanpratidinaṃ yavān .. 42 ..
2.9.d:
अभीष्टमथ वा राम यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्दश ॥
गवां निर्हारनिर्मुक्तानश्नन्प्रतिदिनं यवान् ॥ 42 ॥
2.9.m: or to whatever is desired, O Rāma, for as long as fourteen Indras [endure]. / Eating daily barley grains that have passed out in cow dung,

2.9.s:
māsena tadavāpnoti yatki ñcinmanasecchati ..
gomatīṃ ca tathā vidyāṃ sāyaṃ prātastathā japan .. 43 ..
2.9.d:
मासेन तदवाप्नोति यत्कि ञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति ॥
गोमतीं च तथा विद्यां सायं प्रातस्तथा जपन् ॥ 43 ॥
2.9.m: in a month he attains whatever he desires in his mind. / And likewise, reciting the Gomatī hymn morning and evening,

2.9.s:
golokamāpnoti naro nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
uparyupari sarveṣāṃ gavāṃ lokaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 44 ..
2.9.d:
गोलोकमाप्नोति नरो नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
उपर्युपरि सर्वेषां गवां लोकः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 44 ॥
2.9.m: a man attains the world of cows; no doubt should be entertained on this point. / Above all [other worlds], the world of cows is proclaimed,

2.9.s:
nivasanti sadā yatra gāvastvākāśagā divi ..
vimāneṣu vicitreṣu vṛteṣvapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ .. 45 ..
2.9.d:
निवसन्ति सदा यत्र गावस्त्वाकाशगा दिवि ॥
विमानेषु विचित्रेषु वृतेष्वप्सरसां गणैः ॥ 45 ॥
2.9.m: where cows, moving through the sky, dwell eternally in heaven, / on wonderful aerial chariots surrounded by celestial nymphs,

2.9.s:
kiṅkiṇī jālacitreṣu vīṇāmurajanādiṣu ..
sadā kāmajalā nadyaḥ kṣīrapāyasakardamāḥ .. 46 ..
2.9.d:
किङ्किणी जालचित्रेषु वीणामुरजनादिषु ॥
सदा कामजला नद्यः क्षीरपायसकर्दमाः ॥ 46 ॥
2.9.m: adorned with nets of small bells, resounding with lutes and drums, / [where there are] rivers whose water is always according to desire, having milk and rice-pudding for their mud,

2.9.s:
śītalāmalapānīyāḥ suvarṇasikatāstathā ..
puṣkariṇyaḥ śubhāstatra vaiḍūryakamalotpalāḥ .. 47 ..
2.9.d:
शीतलामलपानीयाः सुवर्णसिकतास्तथा ॥
पुष्करिण्यः शुभास्तत्र वैडूर्यकमलोत्पलाः ॥ 47 ॥
2.9.m: with cool, pure water and sands of gold; / auspicious lotus-ponds are there, with blue and white lotuses of lapis lazuli;

2.9.s:
mānasī ca tathā siddhiḥ tatra loke bhṛgūttama ..
tañca lokaṃ narā yānti gavāṃ bhaktyā na saṃśayaḥ .. 48 ..
2.9.d:
मानसी च तथा सिद्धिः तत्र लोके भृगूत्तम ॥
तञ्च लोकं नरा यान्ति गवां भक्त्या न संशयः ॥ 48 ॥
2.9.m: and mental perfection exists in that world, O foremost of the Bhṛgus. / And to that world men go through devotion to cows, without doubt.

2.9.s:
gomatīṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm ..
tāṃ tu me vadato vipra śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ .. 49 ..
2.9.d:
गोमतीं कीर्तयिष्यामि सर्वपापप्रणाशिनीम् ॥
तां तु मे वदतो विप्र शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः ॥ 49 ॥
2.9.m: I shall proclaim the Gomatī [vidyā], which destroys all sins; / listen with an attentive mind, O brahmin, as I speak it to you:

2.9.s:
gāvaḥ surabhayo nityaṃ gāvo guggu lugandhikāḥ...
gāvaḥ pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ svastyayanaṃ param .. 2.42.50 ..
2.9.d:
गावः सुरभयो नित्यं गावो गुग्गु लुगन्धिकाः॥।
गावः प्रतिष्ठा भूतानां गावः स्वस्त्ययनं परम् ॥ 2.42.50 ॥
2.9.m: 'Cows are fragrant always; cows smell of bdellium; / cows are the foundation of all creatures; cows are the supreme blessing;

2.9.s:
annameva paraṃ gāvo devānāṃ haviruttamam ..
pāvanaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ rakṣanti ca vahanti ca ..51..
2.9.d:
अन्नमेव परं गावो देवानां हविरुत्तमम् ॥
पावनं सर्वभूतानां रक्षन्ति च वहन्ति च ॥51॥
2.9.m: cows are the supreme food, the highest oblation of the gods; / they are the purifier of all beings; they protect and they carry;

2.9.s:
haviṣā mantrapūtena tarpayantyamarāndivi ..
ṛṣīṇāmagnihotreṣu gāvo home prayojitāḥ .. 52 ..
2.9.d:
हविषा मन्त्रपूतेन तर्पयन्त्यमरान्दिवि ॥
ऋषीणामग्निहोत्रेषु गावो होमे प्रयोजिताः ॥ 52 ॥
2.9.m: with oblation purified by mantras they satisfy the immortals in heaven; / in the agnihotras of the sages, cows are employed in the oblation;

2.9.s:
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ gāvaḥ śaraṇamuttamam ..
gāvaḥ pavitraṃ paramaṃ gāvo maṅgalamuttamam .. 53 ..
2.9.d:
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां गावः शरणमुत्तमम् ॥
गावः पवित्रं परमं गावो मङ्गलमुत्तमम् ॥ 53 ॥
2.9.m: of all beings indeed, cows are the supreme refuge; / cows are the highest purifier; cows are the supreme auspiciousness;

2.9.s:
gāvaḥ svargasya sopānaṃ gāvo dhanyāssanātanāḥ ..
oṃ namo gobhyaḥ śrīmatībhyaḥ saurabheyībhya eva ca .. 54 ..
2.9.d:
गावः स्वर्गस्य सोपानं गावो धन्यास्सनातनाः ॥
ओं नमो गोभ्यः श्रीमतीभ्यः सौरभेयीभ्य एव च ॥ 54 ॥
2.9.m: cows are the stairway to heaven; cows are blessed and eternal. / Oṃ, reverence to the cows, the radiant daughters of Surabhi;

2.9.s:
namo brahmasutābhyaśca pavitrābhyo namonamaḥ ..
brāhmaṇāścaiva gāvaśca kulamekaṃ dvidhā sthitam .. 55 ..
2.9.d:
नमो ब्रह्मसुताभ्यश्च पवित्राभ्यो नमोनमः ॥
ब्राह्मणाश्चैव गावश्च कुलमेकं द्विधा स्थितम् ॥ 55 ॥
2.9.m: and reverence to the daughters of Brahmā, to the pure ones, reverence, reverence! / Brahmins and cows are a single family, standing divided in two:

2.9.s:
ekatra mantrāstiṣṭhanti havirekatra tiṣṭhati ..
devabrāhmaṇagosādhusādhvībhiḥ sakalaṃ jagat .. 56 ..
2.9.d:
एकत्र मन्त्रास्तिष्ठन्ति हविरेकत्र तिष्ठति ॥
देवब्राह्मणगोसाधुसाध्वीभिः सकलं जगत् ॥ 56 ॥
2.9.m: in the one place reside the mantras; in the other place resides the oblation. / By the gods, brahmins, cows, holy men, and virtuous women, the entire world

2.9.s:
dhāryate vai sadā tasmātsarve pūjyatamā sadā ..
yatra tīrthe sadā gāvaḥ pibanti tṛṣi tā jalam ..
uttaranti pathā yena sthitā tatra sarasvatī ..57..
2.9.d:
धार्यते वै सदा तस्मात्सर्वे पूज्यतमा सदा ॥
यत्र तीर्थे सदा गावः पिबन्ति तृषि ता जलम् ॥
उत्तरन्ति पथा येन स्थिता तत्र सरस्वती ॥57॥
2.9.m: is indeed always sustained; therefore, all are always most worthy of worship. / At whatever sacred ford thirsty cows always drink water, / and along whichever path they cross over, there Sarasvatī is present.

2.9.s:
gavāṃ hi tīrthe vasatīha gaṅgā puṣṭistathā tadrajasi pravṛddhā ..
lakṣmīḥ karīṣe praṇatau ca dharmastāsāṃ praṇāmaṃ satataṃ ca kuryāt .. 58 .. ..
2.43
.. puṣkara uvāca .. ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi tava rāma cikitsitam ..
saṃkṣepeṇa gavāṃ puṇyaṃ sārabhūtaṃ śṛṇuṣva tat .. .. 1 ..
śṛṅgamūleṣu dhenūnāṃ tailaṃ dadyātsasaindhavam ..
śṛṅgīvīrabalāmāṃsīkalkasiddhaṃ samākṣikam .. 2 ..
simicūrṇayutaṃ deyamathavāpi tathā ghṛtam ..
karṇamūleṣu sarveṣu mañjiṣṭhāhiṅgusaindhavaiḥ .. 3 ..

mākṣikaṃ saindhavaṃ śaṃkhaṃ tagarīṃ pippalīṃ sihām .. 4 ..
ajākṣīreṇa saṃpeṣya gulikāṃ kārayedbhiṣak ..
etannetrāñjanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ghṛtamākṣikasaṃyutam .. 5 ..
bilvamūlamapāmārgaṃ dhātakīṃ ca sapāṭalām ..
kuṭajaṃ dantamūleṣu lepaṃ tacchūlanāśanam .. 6 ..
2.9.d:
गवां हि तीर्थे वसतीह गङ्गा पुष्टिस्तथा तद्रजसि प्रवृद्धा ॥
लक्ष्मीः करीषे प्रणतौ च धर्मस्तासां प्रणामं सततं च कुर्यात् ॥ 58 ॥ ॥
2.43
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि तव राम चिकित्सितम् ॥
संक्षेपेण गवां पुण्यं सारभूतं शृणुष्व तत् ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
शृङ्गमूलेषु धेनूनां तैलं दद्यात्ससैन्धवम् ॥
शृङ्गीवीरबलामांसीकल्कसिद्धं समाक्षिकम् ॥ 2 ॥
सिमिचूर्णयुतं देयमथवापि तथा घृतम् ॥
कर्णमूलेषु सर्वेषु मञ्जिष्ठाहिङ्गुसैन्धवैः ॥ 3 ॥
सिद्धं तैलं प्रदातव्यं गोरसो वाथवा पुनः ॥
माक्षिकं सैन्धवं शंखं तगरीं पिप्पलीं सिहाम् ॥ 4 ॥
अजाक्षीरेण संपेष्य गुलिकां कारयेद्भिषक् ॥
एतन्नेत्राञ्जनं श्रेष्ठं घृतमाक्षिकसंयुतम् ॥ 5 ॥
बिल्वमूलमपामार्गं धातकीं च सपाटलाम् ॥
कुटजं दन्तमूलेषु लेपं तच्छूलनाशनम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.9.m:
For Gaṅgā resides at the sacred water of cows, and nourishment grows in their dust; / Lakṣmī resides in their dung, and dharma in bowing to them; one should always bow down to them.'
Puṣkara said:
Hereafter I shall declare to you the treatment of cattle, O Rāma, / in brief, the meritorious essence; listen to that.
At the base of the horns of milch cows one should apply oil with rock salt, / prepared with a paste of śṛṅgī, vīrā, balā, and māṃsī, along with honey;
or likewise ghee mixed with powder of simi should be given. / At the base of all ears, [oil] prepared with Indian madder, asafoetida, and rock salt
should be applied, or alternatively cow's milk products. / Honey, rock salt, conch shell, tagarī, pippalī, and sihā,
having ground [these] with goat's milk, the physician should make a pill. / This is an excellent eye-salve when combined with ghee and honey.
Roots of bilva, apāmārga, dhātakī, along with pāṭalā, / and kuṭaja applied as an ointment to the roots of the teeth destroys toothache.

2.9.s:
dantaśūlaharairdravyairghṛtaṃ rāma vipācitam ..
mukharogaharaṃ jñeyaṃ jihvārogeṣu saindhavam .. 7 ..
śṛṅgaveraṃ haridre dve triphalāṃ ca galagrahe ..
śṛṅgaveraṃ haridre dve valkalaṃ kuṭajasya ca .. 8 ..
apāmārgaviḍaṃgāṃśca lavaṇena vimiśritam ..
auṣadhaṃ mukharogaghnaṃ jvaradāhavināśanam .. 9 ..

triphalāghṛtasamiśraṃ gavāṃ pānaṃ praśasyate .. 2.43.10 ..
śatapuṣpāyutaṃ pakvaṃ tailaṃ kuṭajacitrakaiḥ ..
gavāṃ rāma pradātavyaṃ sarvahṛdroganāśanam .. 11 ..

ānāhe ghṛtasaṃyuktāṃ dāpayetpadmacāriṇīm .. .. 12 ..

śṛṅgaveraṃ ca dārvīṃ ca kāse śvāse pradāpayet ..13..
dātavyā bhagnasandhāne priyaṅgurlavaṇānvitā .
vātarogeṣu sarveṣu śatapuṣpāvipācitam .. 14 ..
2.9.d:
दन्तशूलहरैर्द्रव्यैर्घृतं राम विपाचितम् ॥
मुखरोगहरं ज्ञेयं जिह्वारोगेषु सैन्धवम् ॥ 7 ॥
शृङ्गवेरं हरिद्रे द्वे त्रिफलां च गलग्रहे ॥
शृङ्गवेरं हरिद्रे द्वे वल्कलं कुटजस्य च ॥ 8 ॥
अपामार्गविडंगांश्च लवणेन विमिश्रितम् ॥
औषधं मुखरोगघ्नं ज्वरदाहविनाशनम् ॥ 9 ॥
हृच्छूले बस्तिशूले च वातरोगे क्षते तथा ॥
त्रिफलाघृतसमिश्रं गवां पानं प्रशस्यते ॥ 2.43.10 ॥
शतपुष्पायुतं पक्वं तैलं कुटजचित्रकैः ॥
गवां राम प्रदातव्यं सर्वहृद्रोगनाशनम् ॥ 11 ॥
अतीसारे हरिद्रे द्वे पाठां चैव प्रदापयेत् ॥
आनाहे घृतसंयुक्तां दापयेत्पद्मचारिणीम् ॥ ॥ 12 ॥
सर्वेषु कुष्ठरोगेषु तथा शाखागदेषु च ॥
शृङ्गवेरं च दार्वीं च कासे श्वासे प्रदापयेत् ॥13॥
दातव्या भग्नसन्धाने प्रियङ्गुर्लवणान्विता ।
वातरोगेषु सर्वेषु शतपुष्पाविपाचितम् ॥ 14 ॥
2.9.m:
Ghee cooked with substances that alleviate toothache, O Rāma, / is known to remove diseases of the mouth; rock salt [should be used] in diseases of the tongue.
Ginger, both kinds of turmeric, and triphalā [should be used] in throat obstruction; / ginger, both kinds of turmeric, and the bark of kuṭaja,
Apāmārga and viḍaṅga, combined with salt, / is a medicine that destroys oral diseases and removes fever and burning sensation.
In chest pain, bladder pain, diseases of wind, and likewise in wounds, / a draught of milk mixed with triphalā and ghee is praised for cattle.
Oil boiled with dill, kuṭaja, and citraka / should be given to cattle, O Rāma; it destroys all heart disease.
In diarrhoea, one should administer the two types of turmeric and pāṭhā; / in constipation, one should administer padmacāriṇī mixed with ghee.
In all skin diseases and likewise in ailments of the extremities, / and in cough and asthma, one should administer ginger and dārvī.
Priyaṅgu combined with salt should be given for setting fractures. / In all diseases of wind, [oil] boiled with dill—

gavāṃ tailaṃ pradātavyaṃ sarvavātagadāpaham ..
yūṣaṇaṃ madhusaṃmiśraṃ kapharogeṣu dāpayet .. 15 ..
pitta rogeṣu sarveṣu madhuyaṣṭivipācitam ..
gavyamājyaṃ pradātavyaṃ sarvapittagadāpaham .. 16 ..
śākhoṭakaramāpānaṃ raktapitte praśasyate ..
godhūmānāṃ ca cūrṇāni māṣāścaiva sasarṣapāḥ .. 17 ..
payasā ca samāloḍya gurumiśrāḥ pradāpayet ..
raktasrāveṣu kṛcchreṣu gavāmetatpraśasyate .. 18 ..
tilāmbhakaruhāṃścaiva haritālaṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā ..
bhagnakṣatānāṃ dhenūnāṃ lepane tatpraśasyate .. 19 ..
vatsānāṃ ca sarogāṇāṃ pāṭhāṃ takreṇa pāyayet ..
haridrāṃ kṣīrasaṃyuktāmathavā rogaśāntaye .. 2.43.20 ..
māṣāstilāḥ sagodhūmāḥ paśukṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ tathā ..
eṣāṃ piṇḍāḥ pradātavyā lavaṇena susam̐skṛtāḥ..

2.9.d:
गवां तैलं प्रदातव्यं सर्ववातगदापहम् ॥
यूषणं मधुसंमिश्रं कफरोगेषु दापयेत् ॥ 15 ॥
पित्त रोगेषु सर्वेषु मधुयष्टिविपाचितम् ॥
गव्यमाज्यं प्रदातव्यं सर्वपित्तगदापहम् ॥ 16 ॥
शाखोटकरमापानं रक्तपित्ते प्रशस्यते ॥
गोधूमानां च चूर्णानि माषाश्चैव ससर्षपाः ॥ 17 ॥
पयसा च समालोड्य गुरुमिश्राः प्रदापयेत् ॥
रक्तस्रावेषु कृच्छ्रेषु गवामेतत्प्रशस्यते ॥ 18 ॥
तिलाम्भकरुहांश्चैव हरितालं घृतं तथा ॥
भग्नक्षतानां धेनूनां लेपने तत्प्रशस्यते ॥ 19 ॥
वत्सानां च सरोगाणां पाठां तक्रेण पाययेत् ॥
हरिद्रां क्षीरसंयुक्तामथवा रोगशान्तये ॥ 2.43.20 ॥
माषास्तिलाः सगोधूमाः पशुक्षीरं घृतं तथा ॥
एषां पिण्डाः प्रदातव्या लवणेन सुसम्̐स्कृताः॥
पुष्टिप्रदा तु वत्सानां वृषभाणां बलप्रदा ॥ 21 ॥
2.9.m:
oil should be given to cattle; it removes all wind ailments. / In diseases of phlegm, one should give yūṣaṇa mixed with honey.
In all diseases of bile, clarified butter from cows boiled with liquorice / should be given; it removes all bile ailments.
A draught of śākhoṭaka is praised in internal hemorrhage. / Wheat flour, black gram, and mustard seeds—
stirred into milk and mixed with jaggery, should be administered; / this is praised for cattle in painful discharges of blood.
Sesame, lotus roots, yellow orpiment, and ghee: / that is praised for smearing on cows that are fractured or wounded.
One should make diseased calves drink pāṭhā with buttermilk, / or turmeric mixed with milk, for the alleviation of disease.
Black gram, sesame seeds with wheat, milk of animals, and ghee: / lumps of these, well-seasoned with salt, should be given; / they grant nourishment to calves and bestow strength upon bulls.

2.9.d:
देवदारुवचामांसीगुग्गुलुर्हिङ्गुसर्षपाः ॥
एष धूपः प्रदातव्यः किञ्चिद्घृतपरिप्लुतः ॥ 22 ॥
सर्वग्रह विनाशाय पलङ्कशयुतः शुभः ॥
घण्टा चापि गवां कार्या धूपेनानेन धूपिता ॥ 23 ॥
अश्वगन्धा तिलं चुक्रं वस्तियोगे प्रशस्यते ॥
अश्वगन्धायुतं तक्रं तिलान्वस्ति प्रशस्यते ॥
भवति क्षीरिणी तेन धेनुर्भृगुकुलोद्भव ॥ 24 ॥
पिण्याकमेव निर्दिष्टं गवां राम रसायनम् ॥
शीतोदपानमार्द्रञ्च यवसं च विवर्जयेत् ॥ 25 ॥
जरान्विता तथा स्थानं तच्च शीतं द्विजोत्तम ॥
धार्यं चैव गवां मध्ये मत्तोजः सर्वथा भवेत् ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
गवां वेश्मनि दीपास्तु दातव्या राम रात्रिकाः ॥ 27 ॥
गवां हि रोगोपशमाय शस्तं गतेऽर्धमासे लवणं सदैव ॥
आनाहशूलारुचिनाशनं तदजाविकस्यापि तथा प्रशस्तम् ॥28॥
2.9.m:
Devadāru, vacā, māṃsī, guggulu, asafoetida, and mustard seeds: / this incense should be offered, lightly sprinkled with ghee,
combined with palaṅkaśā, auspicious for the destruction of all harmful spirits. / A bell for cows should also be fumigated with this incense.
Aśvagandhā, sesame, and vinegar are praised in an enema mixture; / buttermilk combined with aśvagandhā and an enema of sesame are praised; / through that, O descendant of Bhṛgu's race, the cow becomes rich in milk.
Oil-cake alone is taught as a tonic for cattle, O Rāma; / one should avoid cold water for drinking and wet fodder.
[An animal] afflicted with old age and a cold shelter, O best of the twice-born, [should be avoided]; / and among cattle one should maintain vigour; they should always be vigorous.
Lamps should be kept at night in the dwelling of cattle, O Rāma.
Salt is indeed always beneficial for the alleviation of diseases in cattle when half a month has elapsed; / it destroys constipation, colic, and loss of appetite; it is likewise praised for goats and sheep.

2.44
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि शान्तिकर्म गवां तव ॥
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं तथा पुष्टिविवर्धनम् ॥ ' ॥
पञ्चमीषु च शुक्लासु श्रियः पूजा विधीयते ॥
गवां पुरीषे धर्मज्ञ धूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥ 2 ॥
वन्यैः सुकुसुमैर्भक्त्या ब्राह्मणानां च पूजनम् ॥
तत्रैवाहनि कर्तव्यं वासुदेवस्य पूजनम् ॥ 3 ॥
स हि सर्वगतो देवः क्षीरोदधिनिकेतनः ॥
त्रैलोक्याधारभूतानां विशेषेण तथा गवाम् ॥ 4 ॥
आश्वयुक्शुक्लपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्यां भृगूत्तम ॥
वृत्रान्तकस्य कर्तव्यस्तदा यागस्तु गोमता ॥ '5 ॥
गन्धधूपनमस्कारपुष्पदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥
इह प्रजायाः साम्राधः पृषदश्वा तथैव च ॥ 6 ॥
2.9.m:
Thus ends the forty-third chapter, entitled 'Treatment of Cattle', in the second book of the illustrious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the account given by Puṣkara to Rāma.
2.44
Puṣkara said:
After this I shall declare to you the rite of pacification for cattle, / regular, occasional, and for specific desires, and likewise increasing nourishment. / On the fifth lunar days of the bright fortnight, worship of Śrī is prescribed / upon the dung of cows, O knower of dharma, with abundance of incense, lamps, and food,
with wild, lovely flowers offered in devotion, and worship of brahmins; / on that very day the worship of Vāsudeva must be performed.
For he is the all-pervading god whose abode is the ocean of milk, / especially [the refuge] of cows, who are the support of the three worlds.
On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / a sacrifice to the slayer of Vṛtra should be performed by the owner of cattle, / with abundance of perfume, incense, obeisance, flowers, lamps, and food. / [With the mantras] 'iha prajāyāḥ', 'sāmrādhaḥ', and likewise 'pṛṣadaśvā',

2.9.d:
घृतप्रतीकश्च तथा रौद्रीभिश्च भृगूत्तम ॥
नित्याभिश्च तथा वह्निं घृतेन जुहुयाद्बुधः ॥ 7 ॥
अम्भस्थेति च मन्त्रेण लवणं चाभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
दध्ना संप्राशनं कार्यं दधिक्राव्णेत्यनन्तरम् ॥ 8 ॥
यजमानेन देया च धेनुः स्याच्छतधेनुना ॥
तदूनवित्तो दद्याच्च होत्रे शक्त्यैव दक्षिणाम्॥9॥
गावः स्वलंकृताः पश्चाद्गन्धमाल्यफलादिभिः ॥
स्वाशिता मुक्तवत्साश्च कुर्युर्वह्निं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥ 2.44.10 ॥
क्ष्वेडाकिलकिलाशब्दैः शङखवाद्यरवैस्तथा ॥
वृषाणां योजयेद्युद्धं गोपालानां तथैव च ॥ 11 ॥
द्वितीयेऽहनि धेनूनां वृषाणां सह वत्सकैः ॥
लवणं तत्प्रदातव्यं ब्राह्मणेनाभिमन्त्रितम॥12॥
भोजनं गोरसप्रायं ब्राह्मणांश्चात्र भोजयेत् ॥
स्वस्ति वाच्यं ततः पश्चाद्दत्तदायान्विसर्जयेत ॥ 1 3॥
2.9.m:
and with 'ghṛtapratīka', and with the Raudrī verses, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / and with the daily verses, the wise man should offer ghee into the fire.
And he should consecrate salt with the mantra 'ambhasthe'; / the eating [of salt] should then be done with curds, with the mantra 'dadhikrāvṇā'.
A cow should be given by the sacrificer who possesses a hundred cows; / one of lesser wealth should give a sacrificial fee to the hotṛ according to his capacity.
Afterwards, the cows, well-adorned with perfumes, garlands, fruits, and the like, / well-fed, and with calves released, should circumambulate the fire.
With shouts, joyous cries, and the sounds of conches and musical instruments, / he should arrange a contest of bulls and likewise of cowherds.
On the second day, that salt consecrated by a brahmin / should be given to the cows and bulls together with their calves.
And he should feed brahmins here with food consisting mostly of dairy products; / afterwards, benedictions should be pronounced, and having given their gifts, he should dismiss them.

2.9.d:
नित्यमेतत्तु वो दिष्टं शान्तिकर्म शुभं गवाम् ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि कर्म नैमित्तिकं तव ॥ 14 ॥
धेनूनां मारके प्राप्ते तथा रोगाऽद्युपद्रवे ॥
क्षीरक्षये तथान्यस्मिन्प्रकृतेस्तु विपर्यये ॥ 15 ॥
त्रिरात्रोपोषितो विद्वानेकरात्रोषितोऽथ वा ॥
गवां मध्ये शुभे देशे स्थण्डिलं परिकल्पयेत॥16॥
अष्टपत्रं लिखेत्पद्मं कर्णिकाकेसरान्वितम् ॥
पूजयेत्कर्णिकामध्ये वासुदेवं श्रिया सह ॥ 17 ॥
कृसरैः पूजन कार्यं देवतानां यथाक्रमम् ॥
यासां तासां प्रवक्ष्यामि तव नामानि भार्गव ॥ 18 ॥
सुभद्रां नाम दिग्धेनुं पूर्वभागे समर्चयेत् ॥
पूजनीयस्ततो ब्रह्मा सुरभिस्तदनन्तरम् ॥ ॥ 19 ॥
ततः सूर्यस्ततो धेनुर्बहुरूपा द्विजोत्तम ॥
ततस्तु पृथिवीं देवीं ततोऽनन्तं प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 2.44.20 ॥
2.9.m:
This regular, auspicious pacification rite for cattle has been shown to you; / after this I shall declare to you the occasional rite.
When a murrain among cows has arrived, or an affliction such as disease, / or a loss of milk, or in any other disruption of their natural state,
the learned man, having fasted for three nights or having fasted for one night, / should prepare an altar in an auspicious place amidst the cattle.
He should draw an eight-petalled lotus endowed with a pericarp and filaments; / in the middle of the pericarp he should worship Vāsudeva together with Śrī.
Worship of the deities should be performed in proper order with rice boiled with pulses; / I shall declare their names to you, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
One should worship the quarter-cow named Subhadrā in the eastern part; / then Brahmā is to be worshipped, and immediately after him Surabhi.
Then the Sun, then the cow Bahurūpā, O best of the twice-born; / then one should worship the goddess Earth, and then Ananta.

2.9.d:
ततश्च विश्वरूपाक्षं दिग्धेनुं तदनन्तरम् ॥
ततः सिद्धिं ततो ऋद्धिं ततः शान्तिं समर्चयेत् ॥ 21 ॥
रोहिणी नाम दिग्धेनुस्ततः पूज्या द्विजोत्तम ॥
ततश्चन्द्रमसं देवं महादेववृषं ततः ॥ 22 ॥
महादेवं ततो देवं पूजयेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥
इत्येता देवताः प्रोक्ताः कृसरे तव षोडश ॥ 23 ॥
पत्रेषु पूजनीयाश्च दिक्पालाश्च यथादिशम् ॥
गन्धमाल्यनमस्कारधूपदीपान्नसम्पदा ॥ 24 ॥
प्रत्येकां पूजयेद्राम देवतां प्रयतो द्विजः ॥
पूर्णकुम्भानि सर्वाणि प्रत्येकं विनिवेदयेत ॥ 25 ॥
भक्त्यास्थगितवक्त्राणि वर्धमानैस्सतण्डुलैः ॥
सहिरण्यैर्यथाशक्ति ततो होमं समारभेत् ॥ 26 ॥
वेदिं कृत्वा यथशास्त्रं समिध्य च हुताशनम् ॥
एकैकं दैवतं राम समुद्दिश्य यथाविधि ॥ 27 ॥
2.9.m:
And then Viśvarūpākṣa, immediately after him the quarter-cow; / then one should worship Siddhi, then Ṛddhi, then Śānti.
Then the quarter-cow named Rohiṇī is to be worshipped, O best of the twice-born; / then the god Moon, and then the bull of Mahādeva.
Then, immediately after that, one should worship the god Mahādeva. / Thus have these sixteen deities been declared to you upon the rice-and-sesame dish, [O Rāma].
And on leaves, the guardians of the directions should be worshipped in their respective directions, / with an abundance of perfumes, garlands, obeisances, incense, lamps, and food.
The twice-born, composed in mind, should worship each deity individually, O Rāma. / He should offer full water-jars to each one individually,
their openings devoutly covered with platters accompanied by rice-grains, / and accompanied by gold according to one's capacity; then he should begin the fire offering.
Having prepared the altar according to the scriptures and kindled the fire, / addressing each deity according to rule, O Rāma,

2.9.d:
चतुर्थ्यन्तेन धर्मज्ञ नाम्ना तु प्रणवादिना ॥
होमद्रव्यैस्तथैकैकं शतसंख्यं तु होमयेत् ॥ 28 ॥
समिधः क्षीरवृक्षस्य अक्षतानि तिलाम्̐स्तथा ॥
सिद्धार्थकान्यथाज्यं च प्रत्येकं जुहुयात्क्रमात् ॥ 29 ॥
ततो रक्षोहणैर्मन्त्रैर्जुहुयाद्गौरसर्षपान् ॥
ततः समापयेद्विद्वानग्निकर्म यथाविधि ॥ 2.44.30 ॥
सुवर्णं च तथा कांस्यं धेनुं वस्त्रयुगं तथा ॥
कर्तुर्देयमुपस्रष्टुर्वस्त्रयुग्मं गुरोस्तथा ॥ 31 ॥
भोजनं गोरसप्रायं ब्राह्मणांश्चात्र भोजयेत् ॥
स्वस्ति वाच्यं ततः पश्चाद्दत्तदाया द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 32 ॥
रक्षोहणैस्तथा मन्त्रैः कुर्युरभ्युक्षणं गवाम् ॥
गवां च पूजा कर्तव्या गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः ॥ 33 ॥
मोक्तव्याश्च तदा वत्सा यथाकामं द्विजोत्तम ॥

2.9.m:

Firewood of milky trees, unbroken grains, and sesame, / white mustard seeds, and then clarified butter, he should offer sequentially for each one.
Then he should offer white mustard seeds with the demon-destroying mantras; / then the wise man should conclude the fire ritual according to rule.
Gold, bronze, a cow, and a pair of garments / are to be given to the performer, and a pair of garments to the supervisor and the guru.
And here he should feed the brahmins with food rich in dairy products; / thereafter, having received their gifts, the foremost of the twice-born should be asked to pronounce a blessing.
Then with the demon-destroying mantras they should sprinkle the cows; / and worship of the cows should be performed with perfumes, garlands, and ointments.
And then the calves should be set free at will, O foremost of the twice-born. / This rite of pacification for cattle, for the pacification of all portents,

रोचनां च समंगां च क्षिपेत्कुम्भद्वये ततः ॥

खट्वांगेन तु दातव्यं तथा धूपं द्विजोत्तम ॥ 42 ॥
ततस्तु पूजा कर्तव्या देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥

Then worship should be performed of the disc-bearing God of gods; / then he should offer clarified butter preceded by the syllable Om to all

2.45 / Puṣkara said: / The victory of kings depends on horses, O delight of the Bhṛgus; / therefore, by every effort, the acquisition of horses [must be made].

2.9.d:
राज्ञा यत्नवता भाव्यं पालने च विशेषतः ॥
तावन्तस्तुरगा धार्या यावतां पोषणं सुखम् ॥ 2 ॥
कर्तुं शक्यं न धार्यास्ते दुःखिताः क्षुधितास्तथा ॥
दुःखितास्ते श्रियं लोके विनिघ्नन्ति जयं तथा ॥ 3 ॥
धारणीयाः सुविहिता विधिना यवसादिताः॥
विधृतास्ते तथा कुर्युर्लोकद्वयजयं तथा ॥4॥
मङ्गल्यास्ते पवित्रास्ते रजस्तेषां तथैव च ॥
कैवल्यस्यैव ते भक्ता देवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥5॥
अन्ति मध्ये तथा तेन नानुज्ञाता दिवौकसाम् ॥
ततोऽश्वमेधतुरगस्तस्यैवैकस्य हूयते ॥ 6 ॥
सर्वरत्नाधिको जातस्तुरगोऽमृतमन्थनात् ॥
उच्चैःश्रवास्तेन हयः सर्वरत्नोत्तमः स्मृतः ॥ 7 ॥
सपक्षा देववाह्यास्ते मनुष्याणामपक्षकाः ॥
पद्मना शालिहोत्रेण वाहनार्थं पुरा कृताः ॥ 8 ॥
नीराजयन्ति ते देशान्ह्रेषितैर्बलशालिनः ॥
गन्धर्वास्ते विनिर्दिष्टाः श्रियः पुत्रा जितश्रमाः ॥ 9 ॥
2.9.m:
A king must be diligent, especially in their protection. / Only so many horses should be kept as can be fed comfortably;
they must not be kept distressed and hungry; / distressed, they destroy fortune in the world, and likewise victory.
Properly maintained, nourished with grass and fodder according to rule, / maintained [thus], they bring victory in both worlds.
They are auspicious, they are pure, and so too is their dust; / they are devoted to the isolated, supreme god Parameṣṭhin alone.
Indeed, in the midst [of the gods] they were permitted by him alone among the gods; / therefore, the horse of the horse-sacrifice is offered to him alone.
Superior to all jewels, the horse was born from the churning for nectar; / hence the horse Uccaiḥśravas is considered the foremost of all jewels.
They were winged, the mounts of the gods; for men they became wingless, / created of old by Śālihotra, born from the lotus, for the purpose of riding.
Mighty, they consecrate the lands with their neighing; / they are declared to be Gandharvas, sons of Śrī, conquerors of fatigue.

2.9.m:
Horses are the principal limb of the army and its supreme splendor; / for traveling far and in battle, horses are the best of vehicles.
Mounted on a galloping horse, standing tall, wearing a crest of chowries, / the satisfaction that one feels, O Rāma, does not exist [even] in heaven.
By horses well equipped, mounted by armored men, / at their mere sight the hearts of the enemy army sink completely.
The sky whose column of dust raised by the hooves of horses imitates a parasol— / the entire earth adorned with mountains becomes subject to him in this world.
